A single low-credibility acquisition with a verifiable lawful purpose sits at a monitoring tier. A single high-credibility finding — lethal materiel obtained, a barrier deliberately overcome, or insider access acquired to a controlled environment — sits at an investigation tier. Convergence — materiel, access means, and technical capability assembling toward one coherent attack means — sits at an elevation tier and should be treated as active mobilization. Acquisition in a compressed timeframe, or capability converted from latent to operational, sits at a committed-actor tier and indicates the intervention window is closing. Because this tactic equips the threat, findings here warrant faster escalation than the earlier target-development tactics, and any finding correlating with surveillance, rehearsal, or staging behavior elsewhere warrants immediate response-protocol activation regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Multiple lower-tier findings correlating in time or toward one attack means compose to a higher aggregate tier than any one warrants alone; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered actions: the monitoring tier triggers logging and pattern-detection; the investigation tier triggers actor identification, a capability assessment, and a review of the subject's exposure; the elevation tier triggers a structured threat assessment, subject-protective measures, and law-enforcement liaison; the committed-actor tier triggers defensive-posture coordination and urgent law-enforcement engagement.

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises when the second person is more than a name — when the association is corroborated across modalities, persists over time, and is backed by recoverable artifacts (shared communications, joint research, transferred material) rather than a single observer's inference. Credibility falls when the reported connection is thin, when the associate's involvement admits an obvious social or professional explanation, and when that benign reading was never ruled out.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-modal corroboration — the same associate surfaces across multiple observation modes (communications, in-person meetings, financial or logistical traces) tied to the actor's grievance against the target within overlapping timeframes.
Temporal persistence — the association is observed developing across weeks-to-months, with the second voice recurring in the grievance narrative rather than appearing once.

Material evidence of the tie — recovered messages, shared documents, joint search history, or transferred target information that physically links the actor and the associate; does not depend on a witness's accurate recall.

First-hand witness fidelity — a named witness directly observed or was party to the recruitment or coordination; high-resolution reporting covering who was approached, what was asked, the pretext used, and the operational ask.
Behavioral specificity — the reported coordination names the associate's specific role (access, transport, capability, information) rather than a vague sense that the actor 'has someone helping'.

Source motivation aligned with accuracy — reporting comes from a trained professional or neutral party through a formal channel, not an informal tip from someone with a stake in the actor's relationships.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — single uncorroborated tip that the actor 'is talking to someone'; reporter cannot describe the associate or be re-contacted.
Content-specificity weakness — a new contact noted with no operational detail, fitting dozens of ordinary friendship, family, or work explanations.
Temporal-pattern weakness — a one-time observed meeting or message with no follow-through, cadence, or escalation.
Source-motivation misalignment — reporter has structural reason to read menace into the actor's associations (custody dispute, workplace rivalry, estranged family member).
Unrebutted mundane explanation — the association admits a plausible benign interpretation (shared hobby, coworker, relative) that investigation did not rule out.
Reconstructive memory — the connection is named only after an event, with details that may be retrofitted to a coordination narrative rather than observed contemporaneously.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when the actor demonstrates the operational skill to build and run a network — recruiting willing or unwitting participants, compartmenting who knows what, transferring attack-relevant material cleanly, and using cutouts that preserve deniability. Capability falls when recruitment attempts are clumsy or rebuffed, when the actor cannot conceal the coordination, and when the 'network' amounts to a single incidental contact with no operational function.
high_signal_anchors: Effective recruitment tradecraft — the actor successfully draws in accomplices, including unwitting ones enlisted under a pretext that conceals the operational purpose (help with a 'personal problem' that is really access).
Compartmentation and deniability — roles are distributed so participants hold only their piece; use of cutouts or handlers insulates the actor and preserves plausible deniability.

Clean information transfer — attack-relevant material (target details, schedule, environmental data, capability) moves to associates through channels chosen to resist discovery, not casual open messaging.
Multi-node coordination — logistics, timing, and tasking are synchronized across two or more participants across overlapping timeframes; not incidental co-presence.
Access to a witting co-ideologue base — the actor operates inside a forum, cell, or encrypted group that endorses targeted harm and can supply capability, reinforcement, or additional participants.
Operational security in coordination — the actor screens associates, controls what each knows, and manages the association to avoid drawing scrutiny to the target or the plan.
low_signal_anchors: Failed or rebuffed recruitment — the actor's approach was declined, reported, or recognized as inappropriate by the person solicited.
Conspicuous coordination — the actor discusses the grievance or plan openly with associates in the clear, with no concealment or compartmentation.
Pretext failure on approach — the person solicited immediately recognized the ask as unusual or alarming.
No operational function — the new associate has no discernible role in access, transport, capability, or information; the tie is purely social.
Single-node reach — no evidence of more than one contact, and no coordination artifact linking that contact to the operation.
Discipline failures — the actor exposes the plan, the target, or co-participants in ways that breach any operational cover a real network would maintain.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when the actor's coordination is oriented toward acting on the target — when a second voice enters the grievance narrative, when associates are enlisted specifically to extend access, capability, or reach against the named target, and especially when reconnaissance or capability acquisition is paired with the recruitment. Intent falls when the association is generic social or ideological affiliation with no operational ask, when a contact does not escalate, and when the connection has a verifiable non-hostile purpose.
high_signal_anchors: A second voice in the grievance narrative — another individual is drawn into and amplifies the actor's grievance against the target; the introduction of that voice is the first detectable operational shift.

Recruitment for operational advantage — the actor solicits family, coworkers, or social connections specifically for access, transportation, capability, or information about the target or target environment.

Transfer of attack-relevant material — the actor hands off target details, schedule, environmental data, or capability to an associate, indicating shared operational purpose rather than shared venting.
Coordination toward a target-directed act — logistics or tasking are organized around reaching the target, not around a lawful shared activity.

Recruitment paired with reconnaissance or acquisition — network-building is observed alongside casing of the target's environment or capability acquisition; the combination is intent-diagnostic in a way neither indicator is alone.
Compressed-window associate onboarding tied to the target — new associations with no social basis appear in a tightening timeframe and orbit the specific target rather than the actor's general life.
low_signal_anchors: Generic affiliation — the actor joins groups or befriends people around a shared ideology or interest with no operational ask attached to the target.
One-time contact without escalation — an association was observed but produced no coordination artifact, cadence, or target-directed tasking.
Verifiable legitimate basis — the associate is a genuine coworker, relative, or professional contact whose relationship checks out on inquiry.
No transfer or tasking — the actor talks to the associate but no target information, capability, or role assignment moves between them.
Target ambiguity — new associations exist but are not oriented toward the named target; the pattern fits the actor's social life rather than an operation.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the network materially extends the actor's reach to the target — when a recruited associate supplies access, insider position, transport, or presence the actor lacks alone, and when that participant is being actively used rather than merely known. Opportunity falls when solicited participants decline, when the associate's position is degraded or cleared, and when the network confers no reach the actor did not already have; when opportunity appears reduced, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: Recruited access being exploited — an associate is actively supplying access the actor lacks (after-hours entry, keys, insider position, credentials) toward reaching the target or target environment.

Distributed positional reach — participants are located or positioned to place the operation near the target during vulnerable windows the actor alone could not cover; the network closes a geographic or presence gap.

Insider participant in the target's orbit — a recruited co-worker, vendor, family member, or social connection sits inside the target's environment and is being leveraged for intelligence or access, not merely present.
Capability supplied by the network — an associate provides means, materials, or specialized capability the actor could not acquire alone, enlarging what the operation can do.
Transport or mobility enabled — a participant provides vehicles, routes, or logistics that give the actor reach to the target's location when the target is predictably present.
Functioning coordination cadence — a working meeting or communication rhythm exists that lets the network task, update, and act in concert against the target.
low_signal_anchors: Recruitment refused by a hardened contact — the person solicited declined, reported the approach, or is unwilling; the access sought was not obtained. Durable signal if the refusal is firm.

Institutional rule-out of the insider tie — access audits or formal process actively cleared the suspected participant's ability to provide reach, not merely failed to find it. High-confidence absence.
Structural degradation of the participant's access — the associate's access pathway ended (role terminated, relationship severed, relocation); the reach the network offered is durably gone.
Association without operational reach — the associate adds no access, capability, position, or transport beyond what the actor already had; the tie does not enlarge opportunity.

Coordination stalled after challenge — the network's activity halted after detection or a participant's withdrawal, with no adaptation or replacement. Transient: may flip back if the actor re-recruits.

Distance not closed by the network — even with associates, no participant is positioned near the target, and the collective reach still requires major travel not yet made. Transient: may close if the actor commits.

false_positive_context.criteria: Ordinary life is dense with associations that resemble network development on the surface — people share grievances, coordinate logistics, join affinity groups, and enlist family and coworkers for wholly benign reasons. What distinguishes a false-positive from a real concern is whether the association has a verifiable legitimate purpose, whether the connection carries any operational function directed at the target, and whether an obvious social or professional basis for the tie was checked rather than assumed hostile.
contexts: Ordinary social and family ties — friends, relatives, roommates, and coworkers with everyday reasons to communicate, coordinate schedules, or share transportation, unconnected to any target.

Legitimate shared advocacy — people organizing around a grievance through lawful channels (complaints, union activity, litigation, protest planning) with no operational orientation toward harming an individual.
Affinity and interest communities — hobbyist, gaming, faith, political, or fandom groups where strong shared identity and heated rhetoric are normal and not tied to a target-directed plan.

Professional and support relationships — attorneys, advocates, counselors, and colleagues legitimately given case or personal details; new coworkers, tenants, or teammates onboarding into someone's orbit.

Life-transition contact churn — a burst of new associations from a move, job change, breakup, or new venue that looks like compressed-window recruitment but reflects an ordinary change in circumstances.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Findings correlating with staging-class behaviors elsewhere — capability acquisition by the network, observed dry runs, or schedule alignment with an action window — warrant immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Escalation tier-determination for network-development findings depends on three factors: credibility of the association per the credibility criteria, breadth across modalities, and persistence over time. A single low-credibility association with an available social or professional explanation sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility association carrying an operational function against the target — a role in access, capability, transport, or information transfer — sits at the investigation tier. Cross-modal corroboration of coordinated activity, or a confirmed transfer of attack-relevant material to an associate, sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating the case as multi-node target development rather than a solo actor. A functioning network that persists despite implemented countermeasures, or recruitment paired with reconnaissance or capability acquisition, sits at the committed-actor tier and suggests movement toward mobilization. Multiple lower-priority indicators — a new unexplained associate, a shifted contact pattern, a shared grievance — may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding warrants in isolation, and correspondingly the confirmed ABSENCE of any associate involvement is itself diagnostic of a lone-operator case and should be recorded, not just left blank; consumer triage tooling should make both the composition rule and the diagnostic-absence signal explicit. Tier-triggered response actions: the monitoring tier triggers logging and pattern-detection across the actor's contacts; the investigation tier triggers associate-identification and role-assessment plus target-vulnerability review; the elevation tier triggers countermeasure activation and assessment of each participant's reach; the committed-actor tier triggers defensive-posture upgrade and scoping of the full network; any participant or the actor matching a known threat actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

tactics.name: Network Development
tactics.notes: Recruiting and organizing facilitators, access agents, cutouts, and handlers who will support the operation. Network development converts a solo actor into a multi-node threat with distributed capabilities and deniability. For lone actors, this tactic may be absent — its absence is itself an indicator of actor type.
tactics.cpn_notes: Encrypted messaging apps, dark web forums, and privacy-preserving communications platforms are the coordination infrastructure for modern operational networks. Recruitment can occur entirely online with no physical meeting before execution.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor introduces another individual to the grievance narrative through shared communications, joint research, or coordinated complaint

Threat actor begins coordinating logistics, schedules, or transportation with another individual whose role is functional rather than social — task division, lookout positioning, synchronized movement, or logistics the relationship itself does not explain
Threat actor communicates with peers, online associates, or co-ideologues in a forum or platform that openly endorses violence or targeted harm
Threat actor recruits or attempts to recruit family members, employees, or social connections to provide access, transportation, capability, or information about the target or target environment
Threat actor transfers targeting information — target details, schedule, environmental data, capability — to another individual via written or verbal communication
Threat actor's pattern of contact shifts to include new associates whose connection has no clear social or professional basis, particularly in a compressed time window

countermeasures.measure: Maintain insider-threat program coverage of association patterns including new co-worker affiliations, off-hours coordination, and out-of-band communication channels
countermeasures.limitations: Personal associations are protected information; programs must be scoped to job-relevant context. False-positive rate is high without behavioral baseline

countermeasures.measure: Deliver awareness briefings for associates of the targeted subject — coworkers, family members, friends — on common recruitment patterns including requests to provide access, transportation, or information that seems unrelated to legitimate need
countermeasures.limitations: Recruitment requests may be subtle or framed as personal favors. Effectiveness depends on the associate's ability to recognize the pattern in retrospect

countermeasures.measure: Conduct open-source and authorized closed-source intelligence collection on online forums and platforms known to host content that endorses violence or coordinates targeted harm against individuals, mapping participants to organizational interest where appropriate
countermeasures.limitations: Most participants in such forums are not operationally relevant; analyst time is the binding constraint. Privacy and platform-policy considerations require careful scoping

countermeasures.measure: Establish reporting expectations across the workforce for unusual coordination requests, recruitment overtures, or off-band communications that touch organizationally sensitive information
countermeasures.limitations: Reporting culture matures slowly; many concerning requests are dismissed as harmless when received

response_protocols.trigger: Single Network Development indicator reported (recruitment overture, unusual co-coordination, joint grievance escalation)
response_protocols.action: Document the indicator. Conduct a 5-business-day preliminary assessment that includes (a) corroboration of the observation, (b) baseline review of the threat actor's recent association patterns, (c) identification of the recruited individual or associate. Determine whether the association is operationally relevant or socially incidental.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Association determined operationally relevant OR concurrent indicators surface from another Phase 1 tactic.
response_protocols.legal_notes: Investigation of personal associations carries privacy implications; coordinate with legal before any inquiry beyond the immediate observation. Document factually. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

response_protocols.trigger: Multiple Network Development indicators co-observed for the same threat actor OR confirmed transfer of attack-relevant information OR confirmed recruitment of an associate to provide access or capability
response_protocols.action: Convene the threat management team. Conduct full risk assessment including the recruited associate's risk profile. Brief protective operations on the expanded threat surface (now multi-node). Coordinate with HR if an associate is an employee; coordinate with law enforcement if recruitment crosses into criminal conspiracy.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Multi-node coordination demonstrates means and proximity to targeted subject OR confirmed planning across the network.
response_protocols.legal_notes: Conspiracy thresholds and reporting obligations vary materially by jurisdiction. Document the indicator constellation that drove escalation including evidence of coordination beyond mere association. Preserve evidence. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

tactics.field_notes: By the time Network Development is observable, the threat actor has decided they need help — co-conspirators for execution, witting or unwitting accomplices for capability acquisition, or supporters for ideological reinforcement. The introduction of a second voice into the grievance narrative is the first detectable shift. Once that voice is present, an investigator can usually find concrete artifacts: shared communications, joint research, transferred information, and sometimes a meeting cadence that did not exist before. Network Development can be small (one accomplice for transportation) or large (a cell organized around a shared ideology). The work for the analyst is distinguishing connection that is operationally relevant from connection that is socially incidental. The absence of Network Development in a developing case is itself diagnostic — it signals the threat actor is preparing as a lone operator and the case will likely not produce coordination artifacts.
observed_contexts: workplace violence case where the threat actor recruited a coworker to provide after-hours building access in exchange for help with personal grievances unrelated to the attack

domestic case where the threat actor's pattern of contact shifted in the weeks before mobilization to include a new associate met online whose role in the attack was not understood until after-action review
extremist case where co-ideologue communications in an encrypted group preceded coordinated capability acquisition by months

Across casework, insider actors building target access often work through people already in their orbit — co-workers, family members, professional contacts drawn in to extend access without drawing scrutiny
lone-actor case where the absence of any associate involvement was itself diagnostic; the threat assessment team correctly anticipated a single-actor execution

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises when the cover-construction indicator is corroborated by a failed verification attempt, persists across multiple contacts, and is backed by recoverable artifacts or a first-hand challenger who probed the claimed role. Credibility falls when the account was never actually tested, the observation is a single fleeting impression, and a plausible benign reason for the identity mismatch was never ruled out.
high_signal_anchors: Verification-failure corroboration — the claimed employer, work order, appointment, or sponsoring contact was actually checked through a normal channel and could not be confirmed; the gap is documented, not merely suspected.
Temporal persistence — the same fabricated identity or pretext is observed across weeks-to-months or multiple approach attempts, not a one-time encounter.

Material evidence — recovered forged badge, fabricated business card, screenshotted shell profile, or reception log physically links the actor to the false identity; does not depend on accurate witness recall.
First-hand challenger fidelity — a named person who interrogated the claimed role reports the specific jargon miss, the missing artifact, and the procedural question the actor could not answer.
Second-order mismatch specificity — the report names the exact detail an actual role-holder would know that the actor got wrong, not a vague 'seemed off' impression.
Source motivation aligned with accuracy — trained gate, reception, or security staff reporting through a formal channel after a deliberate role challenge, not an informal after-the-fact hunch.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — single unverified impression that 'the uniform looked wrong'; the reporter cannot be re-contacted to detail what was actually checked.
Content-specificity weakness — a generic sense of not-belonging with no concrete role-knowledge gap, unverifiable identifier, or artifact named.
Temporal-pattern weakness — one fleeting sighting of an out-of-place identity with no challenge, no follow-through, and no re-appearance.
Source-motivation misalignment — reporter has structural reason to cast the person as an impostor (custody dispute, neighbor conflict, professional rivalry).
Unrebutted mundane explanation — the identity mismatch admits a benign reading (new hire, subcontractor, recently rebranded vendor) that verification never actually tested.
Reconstructive memory — the account of jargon errors or missing paperwork is reconstructed long after the encounter and may be retrofitted to a suspicion formed later.

capability.criteria: Capability rises with the depth and durability of the constructed identity — a legend that survives verification, employer-plausible artifacts, an online footprint that back-stops the persona, and role knowledge convincing enough to pass initial scrutiny. Capability falls when the cover is a thin behavioral pretext, the artifacts are absent or crude, the role knowledge collapses on the first real question, and the identity leaves no supporting trail.
high_signal_anchors: Durable legend construction — fabricated identity backed by verifiable history: registered business presence, aged online footprint, references or a phone number that answers in-character.

Employer-plausible artifacts — credentials, uniform, and vehicle marking are internally consistent and materially convincing (correct logo, badge format, plate-to-name coherence), not obviously homemade.
Role-knowledge fluency — actor uses correct trade jargon, knows routine procedures, and answers basic operational questions a real role-holder would field, holding cover through initial challenge.
Digital back-stopping — shell social-media profiles or business pages are populated over time to withstand a casual lookup, not empty accounts created days before the approach.
Coordinated validation — cover is reinforced by a second party (insider sponsor, cutout, staged scheduled delivery or accompanied walkthrough) that vouches for or pre-clears the identity.
Adaptive cover maintenance — actor sustains the pretext across repeated contacts and adjusts the story to fit new scrutiny without breaking character.
low_signal_anchors: Thin behavioral pretext only — jogger, dog-walker, rideshare passenger with no identity apparatus to test or defeat.
Missing or crude artifacts — no work order, no truck, no badge, or credentials that are visibly fabricated on first inspection.
Role-knowledge collapse — actor uses wrong jargon and cannot answer basic procedural questions the first time they are asked.
Empty digital footprint — persona has no supporting online presence, or accounts created immediately before the approach with no history.
No corroborating trail — name, employer, license plate, or business name returns nothing through normal verification, and nothing back-stops the claim.
No validation support — cover stands alone with no sponsor, cutout, or staged appointment; collapses the moment a single reference is checked.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when the constructed identity is purpose-built to place the actor near a named subject, is maintained specifically to enable repeated approach or access rather than one-time entry, and pairs with stated grievance or an operational objective. Intent falls when the identity mismatch is incidental, the encounter does not recur, and a verifiable legitimate purpose behind the persona surfaces.
high_signal_anchors: Cover purpose-built for the target — the pretext, uniform, or persona is specifically shaped to explain presence at the subject's residence, workplace, or regular venues.
Access-seeking construction — fabricated credentials are deployed to reach restricted environments the subject occupies, not merely to loiter in public space.
Sustained persona maintenance — actor invests in keeping the cover alive across weeks or months and multiple approaches, indicating planned repeated contact rather than a single pass.
Escalating use of the cover — the identity is reused to move from surveillance toward closer approach, appointment-setting, or direct interaction with the subject.
Retention and investment in the legend — registered business, aged shell profiles, or acquired artifacts kept ready for later use, suggesting operational commitment beyond curiosity.

Hostile attribution paired with cover-building — actor has expressed grievance, blame, or fixation toward the subject AND is observed constructing an identity to approach subject-associated locations. The combination is intent-diagnostic in a way no single indicator captures.
low_signal_anchors: Incidental identity mismatch — out-of-place appearance with no observable orientation toward any specific subject or protected environment.
One-time encounter without escalation — pretext used once with no return, no repeat approach, and no pattern.
Verifiable legitimate purpose — the seemingly-false role checks out on inquiry (genuine subcontractor, new employee, rebranded vendor, licensed professional).
No investment in durability — thin momentary pretext dropped immediately, with no artifacts, online back-stopping, or maintenance.
Target ambiguity — the constructed identity is not tied to any particular subject; presence fits a general location or opportunity rather than person-targeting.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the constructed identity actually works — it grants the actor unchallenged presence or access to the subject's environment, exploits weak verification practice, and is reinforced by an insider who validates it, especially when the subject is predictably present. Opportunity falls when verification friction defeats the cover, the access pathway is closed, or the subject's posture blocks the pretext; when opportunity appears reduced, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: Cover passed unchallenged — the false identity actually secured entry or presence; no one checked credentials, work order, or sponsoring contact.
Weak-verification exploitation — actor exploits an environment with no gate discipline, no work-order confirmation, or no visitor-validation practice against the subject's location.

Insider validation being exploited — an identified insider sponsor actively vouches for or pre-clears the cover (validates a forged badge, arranges an accompanied walkthrough). Dormant insider ties are potential; the exploitation pattern is what is high-signal.

Access-granting role coherence — the chosen cover (vendor, contractor, delivery, utility) maps to a role that legitimately reaches restricted, subject-occupied space and would not normally be questioned.
Timing alignment — the cover is deployed during windows when the subject is predictably present and the access it grants coincides with those windows.
Standing reusable access — the constructed identity yields recurring, unsupervised access (issued badge, recurring delivery slot) rather than a single successful entry.
low_signal_anchors: Cover defeated by verification — the challenge exposed the missing work order or nonexistent employer and the actor was denied. Durable signal: the pretext is burned at that site and will not reconstitute without a new legend.
Institutional rule-out of insider validation — access audits or formal process actively cleared any insider sponsor, not merely failed to find one. High-confidence absence.

Structural access degradation — the cover's access pathway is closed (credential flagged, vendor list corrected, role no longer admitted). Distinct from a single failed entry: a durable structural change.
Challenged without adaptation — actor left when questioned and did not return or re-tool the identity. Transient signal: may flip back if the actor builds a stronger legend.
Access requires presence not yet achieved — the cover exists but the actor has not closed distance to the subject's environment to deploy it. Transient: may close if the actor commits.

Subject's posture blocks the pretext — reception hardening, mandatory work-order confirmation, or staff trained to challenge roles neutralizes the actor's known cover. Transient unless the practice is sustained.

false_positive_context.criteria: Many legitimate people appear out-of-role, present unfamiliar credentials, or cannot be instantly verified — a new subcontractor without a badge yet, a rebranded vendor, a genuine tradesperson between systems. What distinguishes a false-positive from real cover construction is whether the identity resolves to a verifiable legitimate purpose, a transparent accountable person behind it, and role knowledge that holds up once actually checked rather than collapsing under scrutiny.
contexts: Legitimate but unverified-yet roles — new hires, day-labor or subcontractors not on the roster, vendors mid-rebrand, temp staff, or trades whose work order is real but not on hand at the moment of contact.

Genuine credential and access business — delivery drivers, utility and service technicians, inspectors, appraisers, and contractors with real appointments who legitimately reach restricted space and simply look unfamiliar.
Personal or community presence — neighbors, family, dating-app matches, or social connections orienting to a person or place without any deceptive intent.
Non-threatening online personas — pseudonymous hobby, privacy, or professional-separation accounts that look like shell profiles but back a benign purpose.
Authorized covert roles — licensed private investigators, journalists using neutral pretext, and authorized security or red-team assessors operating under lawful engagement with accountable identity.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Findings correlating with staging-class behaviors elsewhere — weapon acquisition, observed dry runs, schedule alignment with action windows — warrant immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Escalation tier-determination for cover-construction findings depends on three factors: credibility of the indicator per the credibility criteria, the depth and durability of the constructed identity, and persistence across contacts. A single thin, unverified identity mismatch with an available mundane explanation sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility indicator — a verification actually failed, a forged artifact recovered, or a role-knowledge collapse documented against a subject-relevant environment — sits at the investigation tier. Corroboration across modes — a fabricated credential plus a shell online persona plus an unconfirmable identifier converging on the same subject — sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating as deliberate cover-for-action target development. A cover that survives challenge, is reinforced by an insider validator, or is sustained and re-tooled despite being questioned sits at the committed-actor tier, suggesting potential entry into mobilization. Multiple lower-priority indicators correlating temporally or modally may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any individual finding warrants in isolation; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered response actions: the monitoring tier triggers logging and pattern-detection workflows; the investigation tier triggers actor-identification effort, artifact preservation, and second-order verification of the claimed role; the elevation tier triggers countermeasure activation appropriate to the subject's posture, including access-control tightening and insider-sponsor review; the committed-actor tier triggers defensive-posture upgrade; confirmed actor identity matching a known threat actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

tactics.name: Cover Construction
tactics.notes: Building a false identity or pretext that explains the actor's presence near the subject without raising suspicion. Cover construction ranges from a minimal behavioral pretext (posing as a jogger) to a full legend (fabricated identity with verifiable history).
tactics.cpn_notes: Synthetic social media presence, forged digital credentials, and fake email and phone infrastructure are standard components of modern cover identity construction. A digital footprint is now an expected component of a credible legend.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor adopts an identity, uniform, or vehicle marking inconsistent with their actual employment, education, or background
Threat actor presents fabricated credentials — employer ID, contractor badge, business cards, vendor identification — when seeking access to restricted environments
Threat actor establishes shell social media profiles, online personas, or business presence to support a cover identity used for approach or surveillance
Threat actor's stated reason for being at a location does not align with verifiable activity — no work order, no scheduled appointment, no destination, no sponsoring contact

Threat actor's verbal account of their role contains gaps inconsistent with someone actually in that role — wrong jargon, missing routine knowledge, cannot answer basic procedural questions someone working that job day-to-day would know
Threat actor's identifying details — name, employer, license plate, business name — cannot be corroborated through normal verification channels

countermeasures.measure: Enforce visitor verification protocols requiring confirmable work orders, scheduled appointments, or sponsoring contact before access to restricted environments
countermeasures.limitations: Verification fatigue erodes effectiveness during high-traffic periods; sophisticated threat actors pre-stage sponsoring contacts that withstand basic verification

countermeasures.measure: Train reception and security personnel on second-order identity verification — challenge questions about role-specific knowledge, procedural details, and routine artifacts the cover identity should possess
countermeasures.limitations: Personnel may default to politeness over challenge; effectiveness depends on culture that empowers reception staff to question

countermeasures.measure: Pre-coordinate supplier and vendor visits including verified contact lookup, expected arrival window, and named individuals authorized to attend
countermeasures.limitations: Pre-coordination overhead can slow legitimate operations; emergency or unscheduled visits create gaps in coverage

countermeasures.measure: Implement two-factor identity verification for sensitive area access — visual badge plus sponsoring-contact callback or biometric, with escort requirements for unverified visitors
countermeasures.limitations: Cost and friction grow with sensitivity tier; insider sponsors can defeat callback verification if not separately validated

response_protocols.trigger: Single Cover Construction indicator detected (unverifiable identity claim, fabricated credentials, role-knowledge incongruity reported by reception or peer)
response_protocols.action: Document the indicator. Detain politely if the individual is on-site; verify identity through sponsoring contact or external corroboration. Report to threat management team within the same business day. Preserve any physical artifacts (business cards, IDs, vehicle photos).
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Identity cannot be corroborated OR cover artifact connects to other concerning context (prior surveillance reports, prior access attempts).
response_protocols.legal_notes: Detention or extended challenge of an individual carries legal implications that vary by jurisdiction. Coordinate with legal before any action beyond polite verification. Document factually; do not characterize the individual's intent. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

response_protocols.trigger: Cover construction detected at access to a sensitive area OR concurrent with other Phase 1 indicators OR coupled with proximity to the targeted subject
response_protocols.action: Activate full incident response. Detain pending verification where lawful. Notify law enforcement; pretexting at protected sites may itself be unlawful. Implement enhanced posture for the targeted subject and the affected facility. Capture all physical and digital evidence of the cover construction.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Cover construction breaches a sensitive perimeter OR threat actor flees on challenge OR identity ties to prior threat case.
response_protocols.legal_notes: Pretexting and trespass laws vary; some jurisdictions criminalize cover construction at protected sites independently of intent. Preserve evidence carefully. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

tactics.field_notes: The thing about Cover Construction is that it doesn't usually fail at the cover — it fails at the second-order detail nobody scripted: the wrong jargon for the role, a missing employer-issued artifact, a procedure that does not match the claimed credential, or knowledge gaps an actual member of that role would not have. A threat actor with a 'utility worker' cover may have the uniform but no work order, no truck, and no answer for which substation they're servicing. An investigator catches Cover Construction by interrogating the second order: not 'is this person who they claim to be?' but 'do their answers, artifacts, and behavior match the role they claim?' The signal is small mismatches between the claimed identity and the operational details only someone actually working that role would know. Cover Construction can range from a minimal behavioral pretext (posing as a jogger or rideshare passenger) to a full legend (fabricated identity with verifiable employer history and online footprint), and the detection difficulty rises in proportion.
observed_contexts: executive protection case where a threat actor in a contractor uniform was challenged at reception; the work order did not exist and the truck in the parking lot belonged to a different vendor
stalking case where the threat actor maintained a fabricated dating-app persona for months to support repeated approach attempts on the targeted subject
insider-conspirator case where an external accomplice presented forged contractor credentials in coordination with an insider sponsor who validated the cover

Vendor or contractor identity is the dominant cover-for-action pattern across facility-targeted casework — fabricated business presence supported by visible artifacts (badge requests, scheduled deliveries, accompanied walkthroughs) that precede any kinetic action
domestic case where a low-tech behavioral cover (jogger, dog walker) sustained repeated environmental survey of the targeted subject's residence over several weeks

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises when a pathway signal is reported first-hand by someone with direct knowledge, is corroborated across independent reporters or record types, and persists or escalates over time rather than appearing as an isolated remark. Credibility falls when a single reporter relays a vague or second-hand concern, when the reported behavior admits an ordinary explanation that was never examined, and when the signal cannot be re-contacted or documented.
high_signal_anchors: First-hand reporter fidelity — a named associate, family member, or coworker who personally heard the ideation, saw the preparation, or witnessed the leakage, reporting specific words, objects, and timing rather than an impression.

Cross-reporter corroboration — the same grievance-to-action progression surfaces independently from more than one reporter or across peer report, writing, and record, converging on the same threat actor.
Documentary backing — the pathway signal is fixed in recoverable form: the actor's own writing, chat logs, browser history, purchase or procurement records, or media collected about prior attackers.

Temporal escalation across weeks-to-months — ideation, planning, and preparation signals appear in sequence over time, matching the literature's pathway progression rather than a single out-of-character moment.
Behavioral specificity — the reported signal names a specific method, a specific target or target environment, or a specific timing, not a generalized wish for harm.
Accuracy-aligned source — a mandated or professional reporter (clinician, threat-assessment team member, HR, school official) relaying through a formal channel with no stake in the outcome.
low_signal_anchors: Single vague concern — one reporter conveys unease about the actor 'seeming off' with no observable behavior attached.
Second-hand relay — the reporter heard about the ideation or preparation from someone else and cannot identify the original witness.
Unrebutted ordinary explanation — the behavior (a gun purchase, a trip, an angry post) has a routine explanation for this actor that the assessment never ruled out.
Reporter-motivation misalignment — the reporter is in active conflict with the actor (custody dispute, workplace grievance, breakup) and has reason to frame ordinary behavior as menacing.
Isolated out-of-baseline moment — a single dark statement or image with no antecedent grievance and no subsequent progression.
Reconstructive recall — the concern is raised long after the fact, with details that may be retrofitted to a threat narrative rather than observed at the time.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when the actor's preparation behaviors show that the means, access, and know-how to carry out the contemplated act are actually being assembled — weapons acquired, tradecraft studied, dry runs conducted, logistics arranged. Capability falls when the pathway remains confined to speech and fantasy, when preparation attempts stall or fail, and when the contemplated method exceeds what the actor can plausibly obtain or execute.
high_signal_anchors: Means acquisition underway — the actor is obtaining or has obtained the weapon, materials, or tools consistent with the stated or inferred method, evidenced in procurement, financial, or possession records.
Rehearsal and reconnaissance — documented dry runs, surveillance of a location, or timing observation that translate a plan into practiced execution.
Tradecraft study — the actor is studying prior attackers' methods, collecting how-to detail, or analyzing target-environment specifics with evident comprehension, not idle browsing.
Logistical assembly — travel, staging, disguise, or access arrangements are being put in place around the contemplated act.
Operational security in preparation — the actor conceals purchases, uses cover for reconnaissance, or compartments the plan from those who might report it, indicating disciplined capability-building.
Demonstrated proficiency with the method — prior training, occupational skill, or practiced familiarity that makes the contemplated method achievable rather than aspirational.
low_signal_anchors: Speech-only pathway — ideation and grievance are expressed but no acquisition, rehearsal, or logistics are observable.
Failed or abandoned acquisition — an attempt to obtain the means stalled, was denied, or was not pursued.
Method-capability mismatch — the contemplated act requires resources, access, or skill well beyond what the actor plausibly commands.
Fantasy without operational detail — violent imagery or admiration for attackers with no method, no target environment, and no preparatory step.
Conspicuous, undisciplined signaling — the actor broadcasts intent openly with no concealment, consistent with venting rather than a capability-building actor.
No progression from study to action — media about prior attacks is collected but never converted into any preparatory behavior.

intent.criteria: Intent rises as the actor's behavior moves along the pathway from grievance and ideation toward a specific, action-oriented commitment against a target, and especially when preparation, final-act signatures, or identification with prior attackers accompany a hardened grievance. Intent falls when expression stays at generalized grievance, when the actor articulates deterrents or alternatives to violence, and when apparent signals have a verifiable benign purpose.
high_signal_anchors: Ideation-to-action progression — an observable movement from generalized grievance through violent ideation to method selection, target evaluation, and preparation.
Framing violence as the only path — the actor casts harm to the target as justified, necessary, or the sole remaining option, closing off alternatives.

Final-act behavioral signature — distributing possessions, drafting a manifesto or legacy statement, recording a last message, or saying goodbye, indicating the actor believes the act is imminent and irreversible.
Identification with prior attackers — the actor models on, venerates, or seeks to emulate individuals who committed targeted violence, adopting them as a script for action.
Energy burst — a sudden visible surge in goal-directed research, communication, movement, or expenditure consistent with a decision to act rather than continued deliberation.

Hardened, personalized grievance paired with preparation — a fixed blame narrative aimed at a specific target or target category observed alongside any preparatory behavior; the pairing is intent-diagnostic in a way neither signal is alone.
low_signal_anchors: Generalized grievance only — anger or persecution themes with no target specificity and no action orientation.
Deterrence or ambivalence expressed — the actor voices consequences, future plans, help-seeking, or reasons not to act.
Verifiable benign purpose — a purchase, a search, or a trip that surfaces a legitimate explanation on inquiry (hunting season, occupation, hobby) that checks out.
Transient out-of-character moment that de-escalated — a dark statement followed by de-escalation, apology, or return to baseline with no further progression.
Fascination without personalization — interest in violence or prior attacks that is not attached to any specific target, environment, or grievance of the actor's own.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the actor's pathway is aimed at a target the actor can actually reach — combining knowledge of the target's routine and environment, positional access, and the absence of intervening barriers — and when preparation is timed to a window when the target is predictably reachable. Opportunity falls when the target is protected, distant, or unaware-but-hardened, when an intervention has interrupted the pathway, and when the durability of any reduction is uncertain.
high_signal_anchors: Pattern-of-life knowledge of the target — the actor reliably knows where and when the target is present through schedule, routes, or venue, giving the pathway an actionable window.
Positional access to the target environment — the actor lives, works, or is credentialed into the target's environment and is present during the target's vulnerable windows.
Preparation timed to an access window — reconnaissance, rehearsal, or logistics are aligned to a specific event, shift, or occasion when the target is predictably reachable.
Security-gap knowledge — the actor knows the target's protective weaknesses: patrol gaps, entry points, screening blind spots, or lapses in the target's own guardedness.
Exploited insider or proximate relationship — the actor is actively leveraging a relationship with, or role near, the target to gain intelligence or access, rather than holding a dormant connection.
No intervening barrier — no protective intervention, no-contact order, monitoring, or organizational response has yet interrupted the actor's approach to the target.
low_signal_anchors: Target hardened against the actor's methods — protective measures or a changed pattern-of-life have blocked the actor's known approach; durable while sustained.
Successful intervention on the pathway — a threat-assessment contact, arrest, hospitalization, or removal of means has interrupted progression; durability depends on whether the intervention holds.
Structural access loss — the actor's pathway to the target ended (role terminated, relationship severed, relocation, credentials revoked), a durable structural change.
Geographic distance not closed — the actor is far from the target and the contemplated act requires travel investment that has not been made; transient, may close if the actor commits.

Target unaware of no accessible routine — the actor lacks working knowledge of when or where the target is reachable, so preparation has no actionable window; transient if the actor develops that knowledge.
Deterred after a challenge — the actor withdrew after being confronted, reported, or detected and has not adapted; may flip back if the actor re-engages.

false_positive_context.criteria: Many of the behaviors that make up the pathway — buying a firearm, posting anger, researching a person, going quiet, giving things away — occur constantly for ordinary reasons, and a single one in isolation is a weak signal. What distinguishes a genuine pathway from a false positive is whether the behavior sits inside a progression tied to a grievance and a target, whether it has a verifiable legitimate purpose, and whether an ordinary life-context explains it more parsimoniously than a threat narrative.
contexts: Lawful and routine means-related activity — hunters, sport shooters, collectors, and occupational users acquiring or handling weapons for established, verifiable reasons unconnected to any grievance or target.

Ordinary grievance venting — angry speech, dark humor, or venting about a boss, ex, institution, or group that is emotionally intense but has no target specificity, no progression, and no preparation.

Life-transition behavior that mimics final-act signatures — giving away possessions, settling affairs, or withdrawing due to a move, illness, financial distress, or non-suicidal depression rather than an imminent act.

Non-violent fascination and media consumption — true-crime interest, journalistic or academic study of attackers, gaming, or edgy online subcultures without personalization to a target or any preparatory step.

Clinical crisis without a violence pathway — a mental-health emergency, suicidal ideation without targeted intent, or substance episode that presents as alarming change but is not directed toward harming a specific target.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Findings that align with staging-class behaviors — means acquisition matched to a method, observed dry runs or reconnaissance, an energy burst, or final-act signatures timed to an access window — warrant immediate activation of response and law-enforcement coordination regardless of this tactic's internal tier, because on the pathway these mark the narrowing gap between planning and attack. Absent that, tier-determination for pathway findings depends on three factors: the credibility of the reported signal per the credibility criteria, how far along the pathway the observable behaviors place the actor (ideation is earlier and lower than preparation and final-act behaviors), and persistence or escalation over time. A single low-credibility ideation report with an available ordinary explanation sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility signal with target specificity or a clear grievance-to-action progression sits at the investigation tier. Corroboration across reporters or record types converging on the same actor and target sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating the actor as being on an active pathway. Preparation, final-act, or energy-burst behaviors, or ideation persisting despite an attempted intervention, sit at the committed-actor tier and suggest entry into mobilization. Critically for this tactic, the recurring failure mode is fragmentation: several lower-priority signals scattered across different reporters and stages must be aggregated, because in composition they compose to a far higher aggregate tier than any single finding warrants in isolation — consumer triage tooling should make this aggregation rule explicit and default to it. Tier-triggered actions: the monitoring tier triggers logging and cross-reporter pattern-detection; the investigation tier triggers actor identification, grievance and target mapping, and a means-access check; the elevation tier triggers protective intervention appropriate to the target and coordination with a threat-management team; the committed-actor tier triggers defensive-posture upgrade and preparation to disrupt; and an actor whose identity or progression matches a known threat actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

tactics.name: Pathway Indicators
tactics.notes: Observable pre-attack behavioral signals — grievance escalation, ideation, leakage, and preparation behaviors — that indicate an actor is moving toward violence. For fixated individuals and insider threats, pathway indicators are often the only pre-attack detection window. These are not tactics the actor chooses to execute; they are behavioral byproducts of the threat development process detectable by protective intelligence practitioners.
tactics.cpn_notes: Online leakage via social media posts, forum activity, messaging apps, and blog content is now the most detectable pre-attack indicator channel. Digital leakage often occurs before physical preparation begins and may continue throughout the threat development cycle.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor exhibits ideation behavior — referencing violent solutions to grievance, romanticizing prior attackers, or framing harm to the target — a person, group, or population — as the only viable path forward
Threat actor moves from generalized statements of harm to specific planning behavior — selecting a method, identifying timing, evaluating opportunities for access to the target or target environment
Threat actor engages in preparation behavior — acquiring weapons, conducting dry runs, surveilling locations, or making logistical arrangements that converge on a specific time, place, or person
Threat actor exhibits a final-act behavioral signature — distributing personal possessions, writing a manifesto, recording a final statement, or saying goodbye to a confidant

Threat actor exhibits identification with prior attackers — collecting media coverage of past incidents, studying tradecraft details, or expressing admiration for individuals who have committed targeted violence
Threat actor exhibits a discrete escalation in the kind or intensity of violent imagery, statement, or low-level act distinct from the threat actor's prior behavioral baseline
Threat actor exhibits a sudden visible increase in goal-directed activity such as research, communication, movement, or expenditure consistent with imminent action

countermeasures.measure: Train the threat management team and security peer reporters on the eight pathway warning signs (per Meloy TRAP-18 / Calhoun-Weston pathway model) so concerning behaviors are recognized at the pattern level rather than as isolated events
countermeasures.limitations: Pathway literacy fades without periodic refresh; novel aggression and energy burst signals are particularly difficult to distinguish from baseline at low frequency

countermeasures.measure: Establish a structured behavioral assessment workflow that maps observed indicators to pathway stages (ideation, planning, preparation, breach, attack), with explicit escalation gates at each stage
countermeasures.limitations: Stage assignment requires trained judgment; pathway progression is not strictly linear and can compress under pressure or skip stages entirely in some case typologies

countermeasures.measure: Implement organizational reporting culture that captures pre-attack signals at low thresholds, including peer reports of concerning statements, fixation behaviors, and behavioral baseline shifts, without retaliation against reporters
countermeasures.limitations: Effectiveness depends on organizational trust and reporting maturity; many pre-attack signals are dismissed by associates as 'just talk' until corroborated by other indicators

countermeasures.measure: Conduct retrospective pathway analysis on prior threat assessment cases (closed and active) to validate that the framework distinguishes pathway progression from baseline behavior in the operational environment
countermeasures.limitations: Retrospective analysis is subject to hindsight bias; pathway-stage determinations made after a known outcome may not generalize cleanly to live cases

response_protocols.trigger: One or more pathway indicators detected at ideation or research stage for an identified threat actor, alone or in combination with other Phase 1 tactic indicators
response_protocols.action: Document each indicator against the pathway model. Conduct behavioral baseline review for the threat actor. Determine pathway stage (ideation / planning / preparation / breach / attack). Open or update the case file. Brief the threat management team within 5 business days. Establish a monitoring cadence appropriate to the assigned pathway stage.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Pathway progresses from ideation to planning OR concurrent indicators surface from another Phase 1 tactic for the same threat actor.
response_protocols.legal_notes: Pathway-stage determinations are protective intelligence assessments, not clinical or psychiatric findings — document them as observable behavior patterns, not mental health characterizations. If the threat actor is an employee, coordinate with HR before any direct engagement. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

response_protocols.trigger: Pathway indicators reach preparation stage (means acquisition, dry runs, logistical staging) OR a final-act behavioral signature is observed OR an energy burst is detected concurrent with prior pathway indicators
response_protocols.action: Convene the threat management team within 24 hours. Conduct formal threat assessment using structured professional judgment. Implement protective measures for the targeted subject including awareness brief, posture increase, and route variation. Initiate enhanced monitoring of the threat actor across available data sources. Coordinate with law enforcement; consider interdiction options if jurisdiction permits.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Threat actor demonstrates means and proximity to the targeted subject OR direct or indirect threat communicated OR breach attempt observed.
response_protocols.legal_notes: At preparation stage and beyond, parallel notifications to legal and (when applicable) law enforcement become standard. Document the indicator constellation that drove escalation — particularly the pathway-stage rationale — and preserve evidence of the original observations. Consult counsel on jurisdiction-specific reporting obligations and on privileged-communication scope for the threat management team. This guidance does not constitute legal advice.

tactics.field_notes: Pathway Indicators are the observable behaviors that mark a threat actor's progression toward an attack — grievance escalation, ideation, leakage, planning, preparation, and the final-act behaviors that often appear in the days or hours before mobilization. The pathway is described in the literature as a sequence of stages (Calhoun-Weston: ideation → research → planning → preparation → breach → attack; Meloy's TRAP-18 codifies the proximal warning signs). In casework, an analyst rarely observes every stage in order — what surfaces is a few signals from different stages, and the work is mapping those signals against the pathway model to locate the threat actor at a specific stage with a specific time horizon. The most catchable signals tend to be ideation (in writing or peer-reported speech), preparation (means acquisition shows up in financial or procurement records), and the energy burst right before action. The recurring detection failure is not absence of signal — it is failure to aggregate scattered signals across reporters and recognize them as pathway.
observed_contexts: [literature: MELOY-TRAP18-2016 / FEIN-VOSSEKUIL-1999 — consensus pattern of ideation-to-action progression preceding targeted attacks by weeks to months]
[literature: NTAC-MASS-2021 — pre-attack warning behaviors documented in the majority of mass attacks against public spaces]
[literature: FBI-PREATTACK-2018 — concerning behaviors observed by associates and family members during the months preceding active shooter attacks]
workplace violence case with documented progression from generalized grievance to specific planning to means acquisition over a six-month window
domestic terrorism investigation where peer-reported ideation and online identification with prior attackers preceded weapons acquisition by months

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises when the observed counter-surveillance behavior shows the over-engineered variance that separates a threat actor from a careful private citizen — the same behavior varied repeatedly in ways that solve for a specific surveillance-detection problem — and when that pattern is corroborated across observations and persists over time. Credibility falls when a single instance of route or persona variation is read as counter-surveillance without ruling out ordinary privacy-consciousness, convenience, or coincidence.
high_signal_anchors: Over-engineered variance — the actor changes vehicle, route, or arrival time more often, and across shorter distances, than any legitimate purpose requires; the variation itself is the tell, not the movement.

Repetition of the same varied behavior — the actor solves the same surveillance-detection problem the same way across multiple approaches to the same subject-associated location, indicating a deliberate method rather than random inconsistency.

Cross-family corroboration — behavior obfuscation (varied routes, dismount-and-walk) observed alongside persona obfuscation (cutouts, thin cover) or technical obfuscation (VPN/Tor/burner) against the same subject within overlapping timeframes.

Recoverable evidence of method — recovered burner devices, Tor/VPN artifacts, staged cover-story materials, or third-party call records that physically document the counter-surveillance tradecraft; does not depend on accurate witness recall.

First-hand witness fidelity — protective-detail member or trained observer directly logged the dismount-and-walk or vehicle-rotation sequence with timing, locations, and description, reporting through a formal channel.
Temporal persistence — counter-surveillance behavior observed across weeks-to-months of approaches, not a single anomalous trip that admits a mundane explanation.
low_signal_anchors: Single-instance variation — one changed route or one walk-then-drive transition with no repetition and no method visible behind it.
Source-quality weakness — uncorroborated tip that someone 'seemed to be avoiding cameras' with no operational detail and no re-contactable reporter.
Unrebutted mundane explanation — the varied approach admits ordinary causes (traffic, parking, errands, ride-share economics) that investigation did not rule out.
Ambient privacy-consciousness — the actor uses a VPN or declines to give a name in contexts where privacy-conscious citizens routinely do the same, with nothing tying it to the subject.
Source-motivation misalignment — reporter has structural motivation to frame benign caution as sinister tradecraft (active custody dispute, professional rivalry, ongoing litigation).
Reconstructive memory — reporting delay long enough that ordinary movements may be retrofitted into a counter-surveillance narrative rather than observed as one.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when the actor's counter-surveillance tradecraft is competent enough to actually defeat detection — clean vehicle and route switching, cutouts that insulate the actor from attribution, and technical anonymization that holds up under scrutiny — and when it spans multiple obfuscation families in a coordinated way. Capability falls when the tradecraft is clumsy, incomplete, or self-defeating: obvious maneuvers, cutouts that trace straight back, or anonymization tools misconfigured or abandoned.
high_signal_anchors: Clean behavior obfuscation — vehicle rotations, dismount-and-walk transitions, and timing changes executed smoothly enough to break a following surveillance, with no wasted or self-exposing movement.

Functional cutout tradecraft — third parties and intermediaries are used for calls, visits, and questions in a way that genuinely insulates the actor; the cutout does not obviously trace back to the actor on first inquiry.

Durable technical anonymization — VPN, Tor, burner devices, and pseudonymous accounts are configured and compartmented well enough to keep reconnaissance off the clear net until late in the planning cycle.
Multi-family coordination — behavior, persona, and technical obfuscation are combined deliberately against the same subject rather than a single ad-hoc trick.

Substitution discipline — the actor reliably reaches for technical surrogates (satellite imagery, Street View, live cameras, drone) precisely when physical presence would generate a detection signal, showing awareness of when to go dark.

Compartmented cover stories — a thin cover for proximity is held in reserve and activated only when challenged, kept distinct from the routine cover used for active access attempts, indicating rehearsed persona management.
low_signal_anchors: Conspicuous maneuvering — vehicle changes and doubling-back so overt that a lay observer notices, defeating the purpose of the counter-surveillance.
Cutout that collapses on contact — the intermediary immediately names or points back to the actor; later denial of the contact is easily disproven.
Misconfigured or abandoned anonymization — VPN leaks, logins from attributable accounts, burner used alongside the actor's real device, or clear-net slips that expose the reconnaissance.
Single-family attempt — only route variation, or only a VPN, with no coordination across obfuscation families.
Cover story that fails on challenge — the reserve pretext is implausible or inconsistent and does not survive a single question.
Self-exposing substitution — the actor turns to technical surrogates but still generates an attributable signal (personal account querying the address, drone flown from an identifiable position).

intent.criteria: Intent rises when the counter-surveillance behavior is organized around a specific named subject and reflects an assumption that a protective program is watching — the actor is not merely private, they are defeating surveillance they expect to exist around this subject — and especially when the behavior is paired with stated grievance or with retained reconnaissance product. Intent falls when the caution is generalized, incidental, or explained by a verifiable benign purpose.
high_signal_anchors: Subject-anchored counter-surveillance — the evasive routing, cutouts, or anonymized reconnaissance concentrate specifically on the named subject and subject-associated locations, not on the actor's life generally.

Assumption-of-coverage tell — the sophistication and targeting of the behavior imply the actor believes a protective or law-enforcement program is active around the subject, which is itself intent-diagnostic at the Target Development phase.
Escalating obfuscation over approaches — the actor's counter-surveillance tightens across successive approaches to the subject, adapting to what they think the protective posture can see.

Retention of reconnaissance product — imagery, notes, or schedule information gathered under cover of the counter-surveillance is archived and organized, suggesting later operational use rather than passing curiosity.

Hostile attribution paired with SD-CM behavior — the actor has expressed grievance, blame, or hostile attribution toward the subject AND is observed running counter-surveillance against subject-associated locations. The combination is intent-diagnostic in a way no single indicator captures.

Cover activated only near the subject — the reserve pretext for proximity is deployed specifically in the subject's environment when challenged, showing the concealment is purpose-built for this target.
low_signal_anchors: Generalized privacy behavior — the actor uses anonymity tools and varies routines across their whole life, not pinned to the subject.
Incidental variation without escalation — a single evasive-looking approach that never repeats or tightens.
Verifiable legitimate purpose — a lawful reason for the discretion (process server, licensed investigator, journalist protecting sourcing, protective professional) surfaces on inquiry and checks out.
No retention behavior — whatever was gathered under cover is not saved, organized, or acted on.
Target ambiguity — the evasive pattern spans several locations or subjects and fits geographic or lifestyle habit rather than person-targeting.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the actor's counter-surveillance actually works — they can conduct reconnaissance and approach the subject's environment while a protective program is present without being detected or interdicted — combining successful evasion, knowledge of the protective posture's blind spots, and the positional ability to be near the subject during vulnerable windows. Opportunity falls when the protective program detects, disrupts, or out-adapts the counter-surveillance; when opportunity appears reduced, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: Counter-surveillance succeeding undetected — the actor's evasive approaches continue to reach subject-associated locations without being interdicted, indicating the protective posture is not catching them.

Knowledge of protective-posture blind spots — the actor times approaches and routes to the gaps in the protective detail's coverage, patrol rotations, or camera fields, showing working awareness of how the surveillance around the subject operates.
Pattern-of-life mastery under cover — despite the obfuscation, the actor reliably locates the subject across schedule, routes, and venues; the informational dimension of opportunity is intact.

Geographic-temporal proximity — the actor lives or works near the subject's environment AND is available during the subject's vulnerable windows. Complementary to pattern-of-life mastery: schedule intelligence gathered from across the country still requires travel investment to act on.

Effective cutout access — an intermediary or insider the actor is actively leveraging extends the actor's reach into the subject's environment while keeping the actor himself off the protective program's radar.

Technical substitution preserving reach — satellite, Street View, live-camera, or drone surrogates let the actor keep building environmental knowledge without ever presenting a physical signal the protective program could act on.
low_signal_anchors: Counter-surveillance detected and attributed — the protective program identified the evasive pattern and tied it to the actor; the SD-CM effort failed against a hardened, alert posture. Durable signal: sticky unless the actor substantially re-tools.
Interdiction on approach — the actor was challenged, followed, or stopped during an evasive approach and did not return or adapt. Transient signal: may flip back if the actor adapts.

Cutout or anonymization rolled up — the intermediary was identified, or the technical anonymization was pierced (device seized, account attributed), collapsing the reach it provided. Durable where the pathway is structurally closed.

Structural access degradation — the actor's proximity or insider pathway terminated (relocation, relationship severed, role ended), so even successful evasion no longer reaches the subject. Durable structural change.

Geographic distance not closed — the actor conducts anonymized reconnaissance from across the country or region; acting on it still requires major travel investment not yet made. Transient: may close if the actor commits.

Subject's posture out-adapting the tradecraft — the protective program changed pattern-of-life, added active surveillance detection, or altered coverage so the actor's known counter-surveillance methods no longer work. Transient unless the change is sustained.

false_positive_context.criteria: Many legitimate activities produce behavior that looks like counter-surveillance tradecraft on the surface — a privacy-conscious citizen varies routines, a gig driver dismounts and walks, a journalist uses anonymity tools and cutouts to protect sourcing. What distinguishes a false-positive from a real concern is whether the varied or concealed behavior has a verifiable legitimate purpose, a transparent identity behind it, or ordinary lifestyle and convenience explanations — and, critically, whether it lacks the subject-anchored over-engineered variance that marks deliberate surveillance detection.
contexts: Ordinary privacy-consciousness — citizens who habitually use VPNs, decline to give names, vary routines, or avoid cameras out of general privacy preference, security-industry habit, or domestic-abuse-survivor caution unrelated to any target.
Convenience-driven movement — ride-share and delivery patterns, parking-then-walking, and route changes driven by traffic, cost, or errands that mimic dismount-and-walk or vehicle-rotation behavior.

Verified professional purpose with lawful discretion — journalists and investigators protecting sources, process servers, licensed private investigators, and repossession agents who legitimately use cutouts, cover, and low-profile approaches.

Legal authority — authorized law-enforcement, intelligence, or protective surveillance and licensed security professionals conducting authorized assessments who employ counter-surveillance tradecraft for lawful reasons.

Personal or social explanation — someone avoiding an ex, a creditor, or an awkward encounter, or using an intermediary for ordinary social reasons, producing evasive-looking behavior with no targeting intent.
