assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Detection of genuine surveillance-detection countermeasures is itself a high-confidence indicator — it implies the actor has reached operational sophistication and assumes a protective program is active around the subject — so findings here weight upward relative to their raw severity band. Findings correlating with staging-class behaviors elsewhere — weapon acquisition, observed dry runs, schedule alignment with action windows — warrant immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Escalation tier-determination for this tactic's findings depends on three factors: credibility of the indicator per the credibility criteria (above all, whether the over-engineered, subject-anchored variance that separates a threat actor from a careful citizen is actually present), breadth across obfuscation families, and persistence over time. A single low-credibility instance of route or persona variation with an available mundane explanation sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility, subject-anchored counter-surveillance behavior with clear method sits at the investigation tier. Corroboration across obfuscation families — behavior, persona, or technical obfuscation combining against the same subject — sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating as deliberate, sophisticated target-development. Counter-surveillance that persists and tightens despite implemented protective measures sits at the committed-actor tier, suggesting potential entry into mobilization. Multiple lower-priority indicators correlating temporally or across families may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any individual finding warrants in isolation; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered response actions: the monitoring tier triggers logging and pattern-detection workflows tuned for repetition of the same varied behavior; the investigation tier triggers actor-identification effort and assessment of what the actor's counter-surveillance implies about their knowledge of the protective posture; the elevation tier triggers counter-surveillance-detection tightening and protective-posture review appropriate to the subject; the committed-actor tier triggers defensive-posture upgrade and consideration that the actor may be preparing to act under cover of their tradecraft; confirmed actor identity matching a known threat actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

tactics.name: Surveillance Detection Countermeasures
tactics.notes: Actor takes deliberate actions to detect whether they are under protective intelligence or law enforcement surveillance. The presence of this behavior signals operational sophistication and awareness of protective programs. Detection of counter-surveillance attempts is itself a high-confidence indicator of a developing threat.
tactics.cpn_notes: Digital counter-surveillance includes checking devices for surveillance software, monitoring social media for mentions of their name or image, and using RF detection apps to identify surveillance equipment. Sophisticated actors may monitor protective intelligence social media accounts for indicators of active investigation.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor varies vehicle, route, or arrival time across repeated visits to a targeted-subject-associated location in a pattern consistent with deliberate surveillance detection
Threat actor performs vehicle dismounts and walking transitions at non-destination points (parking-lot-to-walking pattern, ride-share-then-walk) before arriving at the actual location of interest
Threat actor uses cutouts, intermediaries, or third parties for tasks that would normally be performed directly — calling, visiting, or asking questions about the targeted subject's environment
Threat actor substitutes physical reconnaissance with technical surrogates — satellite imagery, Street View, public live cameras, drone overflight — to avoid being physically observed at the location
Threat actor uses VPN, Tor, burner devices, anonymous accounts, or pseudonymous social media to mask digital reconnaissance activity directed at the targeted subject or environment
Threat actor maintains a thin cover story for proximity to the target environment that they activate only when challenged or observed, distinct from the routine cover used for active access attempts

countermeasures.measure: Train surveillance detection sweeps to recognize over-engineered variance — repeated minor changes to a recurring observation pattern that exceed organic schedule diversity
countermeasures.limitations: Distinguishing over-engineered variance from organic schedule diversity is judgment-intensive; false positive rate is high without trained operators

countermeasures.measure: Implement multi-camera correlation across non-adjacent observation points — matching faces, vehicles, or behavioral signatures across approach routes to detect cutout patterns and walking transitions
countermeasures.limitations: Cross-camera correlation requires coverage density and either operator time or analytics support; privacy considerations apply outside controlled environments

countermeasures.measure: Maintain network-level monitoring for access from anonymized IP ranges, Tor exit nodes, or pseudonymous services to high-value internal resources associated with the targeted subject
countermeasures.limitations: Anonymizing services have legitimate uses; alerting must be tuned to context to avoid noise. Sophisticated threat actors will rotate anonymizing infrastructure

countermeasures.measure: Conduct random-interval rotations of surveillance detection observation positions, vehicles, and personnel to defeat threat-actor pattern modeling of the protective surveillance team itself
countermeasures.limitations: Rotations create coverage gaps if not coordinated; sophisticated threat actors may infer the rotation schedule itself given enough observations

response_protocols.trigger: Single Surveillance Detection Countermeasure indicator detected (over-engineered variance, walking transition, cutout pattern, technical-surrogate reconnaissance)
response_protocols.action: Document the indicator. Conduct a 5-business-day preliminary assessment that includes (a) corroboration through additional observation, (b) cross-camera or multi-source correlation where available, (c) baseline review of any threat actor candidate. SD-CM behavior is itself a high-confidence signal of operational sophistication; treat the detection threshold accordingly.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: SD-CM activity confirmed across multiple observation points OR concurrent with other Phase 1 indicators.
response_protocols.legal_notes: Detection of SD-CM behavior raises the inferred sophistication of the threat actor and may justify enhanced monitoring within legal scope. Document the basis for any escalation. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

response_protocols.trigger: Multiple SD-CM indicators co-observed for the same threat actor OR SD-CM behavior coupled with confirmed environmental survey or capability acquisition
response_protocols.action: Convene the threat management team. Treat SD-CM presence as evidence of operational sophistication. Implement enhanced protective posture including SD team rotation and coverage tightening. Coordinate with law enforcement to share the SD-CM signature; an externally-coordinated threat actor may be in scope of broader investigation.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Threat actor demonstrates sophistication consistent with prior coordinated cases OR signature ties to a known threat actor or affiliated network.
response_protocols.legal_notes: Sharing surveillance signatures with law enforcement may carry information-sharing obligations or restrictions depending on jurisdiction and case context. Document the indicator constellation and observation conditions. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

tactics.field_notes: Surveillance Detection Countermeasures sort into three families: behavior obfuscation (varied routes, varied times, vehicle rotation, walk-then-drive transitions), persona obfuscation (cover stories, third-party proxies, fabricated employer affiliations to explain proximity to the target environment), and technical obfuscation (VPNs, Tor, burner phones, satellite or Street View imagery substituted for physical visits). The behavioral tell that separates a threat actor running SD-CMs from a careful private citizen is consistency — the threat actor varies the SAME behavior repeatedly in ways a private citizen would not, because the threat actor is solving for a specific surveillance-detection problem they expect the protected environment to have. An investigator catches SD-CM behavior by looking for over-engineered variance: too many vehicle changes for a single visit, too many short-distance walks before reaching the actual destination, too many cover stories that do not need to be cover stories. Detection of SD-CM behavior is itself a high-confidence indicator that the threat actor has reached operational sophistication and assumes a protective program is active around the targeted subject.
observed_contexts: executive protection case where the threat actor performed three vehicle changes within a four-mile corridor en route to repeated drive-bys of the targeted subject's residence
domestic case where the threat actor used a relative as a cutout to call the targeted subject's workplace and ask schedule-related questions, then later denied any such call had been made
insider-supported case where the threat actor relied entirely on satellite imagery and Street View for environmental survey to avoid generating any physical-observation signal
[literature: NTAC-MASS-2021 — pre-attack pattern of varied approaches and counter-surveillance behaviors observed in higher-sophistication mass attack cases]
extremist case where the threat actor used Tor and pseudonymous social media for all targeted-subject reconnaissance, with no clear-net signal until very late in the planning cycle

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises when repeated presence or dry-run behavior is corroborated across multiple observation points, persists as a temporal pattern that no legitimate routine explains, and is backed by recoverable evidence tying the actor to the target's environment. Credibility falls when the report rests on a single sighting, when the actor's presence admits an unexamined routine explanation, and when the rehearsal reading was reconstructed after an event rather than observed as an anomaly at the time.
high_signal_anchors: Multi-point corroboration — the same actor logged at the target site, along the approach route, and at an adjacent standoff position (parking lot, coffee shop, transit stop) within overlapping windows.
Temporal-pattern fidelity — repeated presence at consistent times across weeks that maps to a specific operational window rather than a work, commute, or errand schedule.

Material evidence of practice — range-ammunition or rental-vehicle receipts, dashcam or transit-card records, GPS or map data showing repeated route traversal, or dry-run notes recovered from the actor.

First-hand anomaly reporting — a named witness (cashier, doorman, neighbor) who noticed the actor's presence was purposeless — ordered and left without finishing, sat facing the entrance, never engaged normally.
Segment-specific timing behavior — the actor is observed clocking a discrete high-uncertainty step (shift change, lockup, arrival) repeatedly rather than loitering generally.
Reporting through a trained channel — protective detail, security officer, or law-enforcement observation with contemporaneous documentation, not an informal after-the-fact recollection.
low_signal_anchors: Single-sighting weakness — one observation of presence with no recurrence and no route or timing correlation.
Routine-explanation gap — actor's repeated presence coincides with a plausible commute, workplace, residence, or standing appointment that was never checked.
Vague-anomaly reporting — witness felt something was 'off' but cannot describe timing, positioning, or repetition with any specificity.
Reporter-motivation misalignment — the person flagging the pattern has a structural agenda (custody dispute, business rivalry, active litigation with the actor).
Reconstructive recall — the rehearsal interpretation only surfaced after an incident, with details likely retrofitted to the threat narrative.
Ambient-activity overlap — the site sits in a high-traffic area where repeated presence by many people is normal and the actor is not distinguishable from baseline foot traffic.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when the rehearsal reflects operational discipline — practicing discrete segments without revealing the whole, using stand-ins or remote sites to avoid detection signal, and running variants that show planning maturity. Capability falls when the practice is conspicuous, when the actor exposes operational artifacts unnecessarily, and when the behavior shows no ability to test the plan against realistic conditions.
high_signal_anchors: Compartmented rehearsal — actor practices a single segment (breach, timing, approach) in isolation, deliberately not walking the full operation where it would draw notice.
Stand-in tradecraft — use of a comparable building, vehicle, or role-player to rehearse execution without exposing the real target or premature intent.
Remote capability testing — weapon function checks, vehicle-handling runs, or breach-tool practice conducted at isolated locations that generate no target-adjacent signal.
Variant testing — actor runs the approach route or timing under alternate conditions (different time, direction, stand-in vehicle) to validate the plan against contingencies.
Detection-aware positioning — actor rehearses from standoff, varies observation posts, and avoids lingering past what each timing measurement requires.
Productive assumption-testing — actor measures a high-uncertainty operational segment and demonstrably adjusts the plan based on the result, not merely repeats the observation.
low_signal_anchors: Conspicuous practice — actor walks the full approach openly, lingers at the entrance, or handles operational artifacts (weapon, uniform) in view.
No-compartmentation repetition — repeated identical visits with no attempt at concealment, cover story, or standoff.
Premature exposure — rehearsal at the live target site in a way that would alert the subject or detail, revealing intent before capability is set.
Single-segment fixation without progression — actor observes the same step over and over with no evidence of variant testing or plan adjustment.
No realistic conditions — practice occurs only in settings that don't resemble the operational environment, offering no validation value.
Artifact-driven detection — actor's rehearsal is only known because operational artifacts (range purchases, rental records) surfaced, indicating weak operational security.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when the actor's behavior shifts from observing the target to practicing action against it — testing entry, timing execution windows, walking egress — and especially when rehearsal is paired with a fixed operational window or expressed grievance toward the target. Intent falls when presence has a verifiable benign purpose, when no action-rehearsal element is present, and when the pattern fits general interest rather than execution preparation.
high_signal_anchors: Observation-to-action shift — the actor's behavior at the target environment moves from watching to rehearsing: testing entry timing, probing response gaps, walking the egress route.
Execution-window alignment — repeated presence concentrates on the specific times a planned attack would occur (shift-change gap, lockup, predictable arrival), not on general coverage.
Egress rehearsal — the actor practices the exit, not just the approach; rehearsing escape signals commitment to acting rather than to observing.
Stand-in execution — rehearsing the act itself against a prop, comparable site, or role-player, which has no explanation other than preparing to perform it.
Retention of rehearsal work — timing notes, route maps, annotated schedules, or practice logs maintained for operational use.

Hostile attribution paired with rehearsal — the actor has expressed grievance, blame, or fixation toward the target AND is observed dry-running the approach. The combination is intent-diagnostic in a way no single indicator captures.
low_signal_anchors: Verifiable benign purpose — actor's repeated presence resolves to a job, residence, appointment, or relationship at or near the site that checks out.
Observation without action-rehearsal — actor watches but shows no entry-testing, timing-to-window, or egress-walking behavior.
Timing not tied to a window — presence is frequent but scattered across hours with no concentration on an operationally meaningful moment.
No retention — no notes, maps, or logs; presence is not organized toward a plan.
General-interest pattern — behavior fits curiosity about a location or event rather than preparation to act against a specific target.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when rehearsal confirms the actor can execute — validated timing against the target's predictable windows, tested access with no friction encountered, and positional ability to reach the target when it is present. Opportunity falls when the dry run meets defensive friction the actor does not adapt to, when access is tested and fails, or when distance from the target is not closed; when opportunity appears reduced, whether that reduction is durable matters.
high_signal_anchors: Validated execution window — rehearsal has confirmed a repeatable moment (shift-change gap, lockup, arrival) when the target is reachable and defenses are thin.
Access tested without friction — the actor's rehearsed approach or entry encountered no challenge, detection, or countermeasure and proceeded unimpeded.
Pattern-of-life confirmation through rehearsal — repeated visits have verified the target's schedule and predictable presence, converting assumption into working knowledge.

Geographic-temporal proximity — the actor lives or works close enough to run repeated rehearsals AND is available during the target's vulnerable windows. Complementary to pattern-of-life confirmation, not redundant: schedule knowledge without proximity still requires travel investment, and proximity without a validated window lacks an actionable moment.
Response-gap identification — rehearsal has located a specific defensive weakness (patrol rotation, camera blind spot, unlocked egress) the actor can exploit on execution.

Rehearsed exploited access — the actor has practiced using a legitimate role, insider connection, or credential to reach the target environment, and is actively leveraging it rather than holding it dormant.
low_signal_anchors: Rehearsal defeated by hardened posture — the dry run met active countermeasures that blocked the approach. Durable signal: the low-opportunity reading is sticky and won't reconstitute without major actor adaptation or a posture change.
Access test failed — the actor's rehearsed entry was challenged, detected, or physically blocked, and no successful variant was found.
Structural access loss — the role, credential, or relationship the rehearsal relied on has since ended. Distinct from temporary friction: a durable structural change.
Friction encountered without adaptation — actor abandoned the rehearsal after being challenged or noticed and did not return or adjust. Transient: may flip back if the actor adapts.
Distance not closed — actor rehearsed remotely or from a distance but has not staged the travel or presence needed to act. Transient: may close if the actor commits.

Window not validated — repeated presence never resolved into a reliable moment of target vulnerability; the target's pattern remained too variable to exploit. Transient unless the variability is sustained.

false_positive_context.criteria: Repeated presence and route or timing behavior look, on the surface, exactly like ordinary life — a regular at a coffee shop, a commuter who drives the same street, a hobbyist who function-checks a firearm at a range. What separates a false positive from operational rehearsal is whether the repeated presence has a verifiable legitimate purpose, whether the actor's identity and routine are transparent and check out, and whether the timing tracks a mundane schedule rather than an operational window.
contexts: Ordinary routine and residence — commuters on a fixed route, regulars at a venue near the site, neighbors and residents whose repeated presence maps to home, work, or a standing appointment.
Verified professional purpose — delivery drivers, transit and rideshare operators, contractors, surveyors, and service providers whose recurring site presence is business-driven and documented.

Legitimate skills practice — licensed shooters function-checking or practicing at ranges, driving enthusiasts on track or handling runs, hobbyists with a documented recreational basis for the activity.
Legal authority — authorized law-enforcement or protective surveillance, licensed investigators on lawful matters, and security professionals conducting sanctioned route or access assessments.
Event and community activity — attendees, vendors, or volunteers repeatedly present for a scheduled event; fans or admirers engaged in invasive but non-threatening repeat presence.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Because Operational Rehearsal is a Mobilization-phase tactic, its findings carry an inherently compressed timeline: rehearsal implies the plan already exists and is being validated against reality, so tier logic here biases toward action. Findings correlating with other staging-class behaviors — weapon acquisition, final-act preparation, communicated intent, or schedule alignment with a specific attack window — warrant immediate activation of response and law-enforcement coordination regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Tier-determination otherwise rests on three factors: credibility of the rehearsal indicator per the credibility criteria, breadth across observation points and modes, and persistence of the pattern over time. A single low-credibility sighting with an available routine explanation sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility rehearsal indicator with an action-rehearsal element (entry-testing, egress-walking, window-aligned timing) sits at the investigation tier and, given the phase, should be worked with urgency. Multi-point corroboration — repeated presence confirmed across the site, route, and standoff positions against the same target — sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating as active pre-attack preparation. Rehearsal persisting despite implemented countermeasures, or a confirmed observation-to-action shift, sits at the committed-actor tier and indicates the actor is at or past the go/no-go decision point. Multiple lower-priority indicators correlating temporally or across observation points may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding warrants in isolation; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered response actions: the monitoring tier triggers logging and pattern-detection across site, route, and standoff observation points; the investigation tier triggers actor identification and immediate target-vulnerability assessment; the elevation tier triggers countermeasure activation, protective-detail notification, and window-hardening; the committed-actor tier triggers defensive-posture upgrade and law-enforcement engagement. Confirmed actor identity matching a known threat actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

tactics.name: Operational Rehearsal
tactics.notes: Controlled dry run of the planned approach — timing assessments, route confirmation, access testing, go/no-go decision point validation. Operational rehearsal is a controlled exercise, not the live approach. Distinct from Partial Approach Rehearsal (TM0209), which uses the live target site with abort triggers.
tactics.cpn_notes: GPS and mapping apps, real-time traffic data, and satellite imagery are standard rehearsal planning tools. Digital simulation of timing and routing can substitute for physical rehearsal in some scenarios.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor performs repeated visits to the target site at consistent times concentrated on one recurring window rather than varied across the day, without legitimate purpose
Threat actor drives or walks the same route to or past the target on multiple occasions, sometimes with stand-in vehicles or alternative timing to test variants
Threat actor times specific high-uncertainty operational segments — security shift change, building lockup, route arrival — repeatedly to validate planning assumptions

Threat actor conducts partial rehearsal of equipment or capability — weapon function checks at remote locations, vehicle handling tests, breach-tool practice — outside any legitimate context (organized sport, licensed range use, professional training)
Threat actor uses stand-in targets — a comparable building or vehicle, a sim prop, or a role-player mimicking the individual — to rehearse execution without prematurely revealing intent
Threat actor's behavior at the target environment shifts from observation to action-rehearsal — testing entry timing, identifying response gaps, walking the egress route

countermeasures.measure: Maintain behavioral-baseline awareness across the targeted subject's environment — coffee shops, parking facilities, perimeter — with reception and staff trained to flag repeat visitors who do not fit a recognizable pattern
countermeasures.limitations: Baseline awareness depends on stable staffing; high-turnover environments lose continuity. False positives are common where the protected environment overlaps with a high-foot-traffic neighborhood

countermeasures.measure: Implement multi-camera correlation across approach routes and adjacent locations to identify repeat presence consistent with rehearsal — same face, same vehicle, same behavioral pattern observed across non-adjacent points
countermeasures.limitations: Cross-camera correlation requires coverage density and analyst time or analytics support. Sophisticated threat actors rotate vehicles and clothing to defeat correlation

countermeasures.measure: Apply random-interval variation to security patterns — shift change times, lockup procedures, patrol routes — to defeat rehearsal-based timing capture
countermeasures.limitations: Operational predictability has legitimate value (staff coordination, contractor scheduling); over-randomization erodes effectiveness. Sophisticated threat actors infer the randomization schedule given enough observations

countermeasures.measure: Conduct after-action review of any unusual-behavior reports against the timeline of any subsequent attempted attack to identify retrospective rehearsal signals and refine baseline awareness training
countermeasures.limitations: Hindsight bias inflates the apparent clarity of pre-incident signals; retrospective patterns must be validated against negative cases to remain useful

response_protocols.trigger: Single Operational Rehearsal indicator detected (repeat presence at unusual times, route walk-through, equipment function check at the protected environment)
response_protocols.action: Document the indicator. Conduct a 5-business-day preliminary assessment that includes (a) corroboration through adjacent observations or camera review, (b) identification of any threat actor candidate, (c) cross-reference against open threat assessment cases. Determine whether the observed pattern is consistent with rehearsal or with legitimate routine.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Rehearsal pattern confirmed across multiple observations OR concurrent indicators surface from another Phase 1 or Phase 2 tactic.
response_protocols.legal_notes: Observation of an unidentified individual in public space generally requires no legal pre-clearance. Investigative escalation (identification, surveillance) carries jurisdiction-specific privacy implications. Document factually. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

response_protocols.trigger: Multiple Operational Rehearsal indicators co-observed for the same threat actor OR rehearsal coupled with confirmed capability acquisition, cover construction, or pathway indicators
response_protocols.action: Convene the threat management team within 24 hours. Conduct formal threat assessment. Implement enhanced protective posture for the targeted subject including route variation and surveillance detection. Coordinate with law enforcement; rehearsal-stage detection provides the strongest pre-incident interruption window. Initiate enhanced monitoring of the threat actor.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Rehearsal completion observed OR transition behavior toward execution stage.
response_protocols.legal_notes: Pre-incident interruption at rehearsal stage carries the highest preventive leverage; document the indicator constellation thoroughly to support any law enforcement engagement. Preserve evidence. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

tactics.field_notes: Operational Rehearsal is the threat actor's dress rehearsal — a partial or full walkthrough of the planned attack to test the plan against reality. It is often only recognizable in retrospect: the person sitting in the coffee shop across from the target's office didn't draw attention at the time; only after the attack does the cashier remember the man who came in three Tuesdays in a row, ordered the same drink, sat by the window, and left without finishing it. Most rehearsals are partial — the threat actor practices the breach but not the egress, or times the security shift but not the actual approach. Full rehearsals are rarer because they require operational artifacts (uniforms, weapons, vehicles) that themselves create detection signal. What an analyst is looking for is repeated presence at consistent times that no normal activity explains.
observed_contexts: executive protection case where the threat actor was identified after the attack as having visited the targeted subject's office building and adjacent coffee shop on multiple consecutive Tuesdays

workplace violence case where the threat actor performed weapon function checks at a remote rural site weeks before the attack, identified retrospectively through purchase records of range-style ammunition the threat actor had no documented sporting use for
domestic case where repeated drive-bys of the targeted subject's residence, varying time and direction across visits, were recognized as rehearsal only after the attack
[literature: NTAC-MASS-2021 — pre-attack rehearsal patterns documented in mass attacks against public spaces, including timing studies of security shift changes]
facility attack case where the threat actor performed partial rehearsal at a similar building (same architecture, same retail tenant) before targeting the actual location

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises when the same concealment signature is corroborated across independent observers, persists as a pattern rather than a single anomaly, and is backed by recoverable evidence of a deliberate cover — a slip, an artifact, or a contradiction that outlasts the actor's account. Credibility falls when the report is a single uncorroborated impression, when the 'gap' or evasiveness admits an ordinary life explanation that was never ruled out, and when the observation surfaces so late that the concealment narrative may be retrofitted rather than observed.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-observer corroboration — the same unaccounted-for time, guardedness, or story inconsistency is independently reported by family, peers, and a system anomaly (IT, financial, location data) against the same actor within overlapping timeframes.
Temporal persistence — the concealment pattern (recurring absences, sustained compartmentalization) holds across weeks to months, not a single unexplained evening.

Recoverable anti-forensic evidence — deleted grievance posts recovered from cache or archive, a separate device or encrypted account surfaced, cash-withdrawal records with no documented purpose; physical proof of a cover rather than an impression of one.

First-hand witness fidelity — a named peer or family member directly observed the evasiveness and can report specifics: what was asked, the irritable or deflecting response, when sharing stopped, what routine changed.

Contradiction specificity — the inconsistency is concrete and checkable: a claimed location that cell-tower data contradicts, a claimed meeting with no corresponding record, a receipt gap tied to a specific window.
Source motivation aligned with accuracy — the concern is raised through a formal or protective channel (workplace, IT security, a worried family member) rather than an informal tip with an agenda.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — single anonymous or second-hand report of someone being 'secretive lately,' with no corroborating modality and no re-contactable reporter.
Content-specificity weakness — vague sense of withdrawal or privacy with no concrete gap, contradiction, or artifact behind it.
Temporal-pattern weakness — one unexplained absence or one deleted post with no follow-through, escalation, or repetition.
Source-motivation misalignment — the reporter has structural reason to read secrecy as sinister (custody dispute, breakup, workplace rivalry, ongoing litigation).

Unrebutted ordinary explanation — the concealment-looking behavior fits a mundane private matter (new relationship, health issue, second job, financial embarrassment) that investigation did not rule out.
Reconstructive memory — the evasiveness is 'recognized' only after an unrelated alarm, so the timeline and details may be fitted to the threat narrative rather than observed at the time.

capability.criteria: Capability rises with operational discipline that sustains a cover — compartmentalization that separates the operation from normal life, anti-forensic hygiene that removes evidence, cash-based and anonymized handling that defeats financial tracing, and cover stories durable enough that observers do not initially recognize the concealment. Capability falls when the concealment is sloppy — conspicuous secrecy, contradictions that surface immediately, single-mode hiding, or slips the actor does not notice or correct.
high_signal_anchors: Communications compartmentalization — a dedicated device, encrypted application, or anonymous account reserved for operationally relevant contacts and kept fully separate from normal-life comms.
Anti-forensic discipline — deliberate, staged removal of grievance posts and identifiable statements of intent, metadata scrubbing, or account curation that anticipates later scrutiny.
Financial tradecraft — shift to cash or anonymized-payment channels for operational expenses, structured to leave no documented purpose and evade routine transaction review.
Cover-story durability — inconsistencies do not surface under casual questioning; family and peers accept the account and only later recognize it did not fit.

Multi-modal concealment coordination — physical (unaccounted time), digital (compartmentalized comms, scrubbed presence), and financial concealment maintained together rather than a single lapse-prone channel.
Self-correcting operational security — the actor tightens discipline as execution nears, repairs slips, and adjusts the cover when questioned rather than abandoning it.
low_signal_anchors: Conspicuous secrecy — the concealment itself draws attention: overt evasiveness, dramatic irritability at routine questions, secrecy so abrupt it invites the scrutiny it was meant to avoid.
Immediate contradiction — the story falls apart on first check; claimed locations and records diverge on casual comparison.
Single-mode concealment — hides one channel (deletes posts) while leaving the operation visible in others (open device, traceable spending).
Uncorrected slips — the actor leaves artifacts where they should not be and does not notice or repair the exposure.
No compartmentalization — operationally relevant contacts and planning run through the same accounts and devices used in normal life.
Traceable financial handling — operational expenses run through ordinary documented accounts with no attempt at cash or anonymization.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when the concealment is not general privacy but is specifically shaped to protect operationally relevant activity against a named target — scrubbing statements of intent, compartmentalizing contacts tied to the operation, and hiding time or money that maps to preparation. Intent falls when the secrecy is generic, has a verifiable benign purpose, or reflects an ordinary life change unconnected to any target.
high_signal_anchors: Anti-forensic removal of intent evidence — selective deletion of prior grievance posts and identifiable statements of intent toward the subject, timed to the pre-execution window; hiding the mindset, not just the activity.

Concealment mapped to preparation — the unaccounted-for time, cash withdrawals, or compartmentalized comms align with other observed preparatory behavior against the target rather than standing alone.
Target-linked compartmentalization — the separate device or anonymous account is used for contacts, research, or planning tied to the named subject or the operation.

Grievance-plus-concealment pairing — the actor has expressed hostility or blame toward the subject AND is now suppressing that expression while going dark; the shift from open grievance to disciplined silence is intent-diagnostic in a way neither behavior is alone.
Discipline tightening toward a window — concealment intensifies and slips get repaired as a specific date, event, or opportunity approaches, indicating protection of an imminent plan.
Guardedness scoped to plans — the withdrawal and irritability concentrate specifically on questions about whereabouts, schedule, or intentions, not on general personal topics.
low_signal_anchors: Generic privacy change — increased secrecy with no linkage to a target, grievance, or preparatory activity; consistent with a purely personal matter.
Verifiable benign purpose — the gap, absence, or spending resolves to a legitimate cause (affair, second job, medical treatment, financial trouble) that checks out.
One-off deletion or absence — a single scrubbed post or missing evening with no pattern, no target linkage, and no follow-through.
Ordinary life-stage withdrawal — reduced sharing and irritability that track a known stressor (grief, job loss, relationship change) rather than an operation.
Target ambiguity — the concealment protects something unspecified; no named subject, grievance, or preparatory activity is attached to it.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the actor can sustain the concealment unchallenged — observers who could notice the gaps are absent, unaware, or not aggregating what they see; monitoring systems are not correlating the anomalies; and the actor's environment affords the private time and unmonitored channels the operation needs. Opportunity falls when attentive observers, aggregation of peer and family reports, or anomaly-detection systems are actively closing the space the concealment depends on; when opportunity appears reduced, whether the observation apparatus is durable or transient matters.
high_signal_anchors: No aggregation of scattered signals — family, peers, and system anomalies each hold a fragment of the concealment but nothing routes them to a single assessment point; the gaps stay invisible in aggregate.
Low-observation environment — the actor lives, works, or operates with enough autonomy that unaccounted-for time and private channels attract no scrutiny.
Unmonitored operational channels — the compartmentalized device, encrypted app, or cash flow sits outside any review that would surface it.
Compliant or unaware inner circle — family and peers accept the cover, do not question the guardedness, or normalize the withdrawal, giving the concealment room to hold.
Absence of anomaly correlation — no IT, financial, or physical-security process is cross-referencing the inconsistencies against each other or against a baseline.
Autonomy over pattern-of-life — the actor controls their own schedule and accounting enough to manufacture gaps and cover them without needing to explain.
low_signal_anchors: Reports being aggregated to assessment — peer and family concerns are already reaching a threat-assessment or security function that can correlate them. Durable signal: once aggregation exists it tends to persist and keeps closing the space.

Active anomaly detection — IT-security or financial monitoring is surfacing and correlating the compartmentalized device, scrubbing, or unexplained spending. Durable while the controls remain in place.
Attentive, questioning inner circle — family or peers press on the inconsistencies and escalate rather than accept the cover; the concealment is failing at the human layer.

Structural loss of private space — the actor's autonomy has narrowed (supervision, cohabitation change, monitored device or account) so gaps can no longer be manufactured unobserved. Durable structural change.
Concealment already breaking down — slips and contradictions are surfacing faster than the actor repairs them and are being noticed. Transient: may reconstitute if scrutiny lapses.
Temporary heightened scrutiny — a specific incident or question has raised attention for now, but no standing process sustains it. Transient: opportunity may reopen once attention fades.

false_positive_context.criteria: Secrecy, withdrawal, deleted posts, cash spending, and unexplained absences are ordinary features of private life long before they are ever concealment of an operation. What separates a false positive from a real concern is whether the hidden activity has a verifiable benign purpose, whether the secrecy is scoped to a target or grievance rather than to a personal matter, and whether the pattern is corroborated across modalities or is a single ambiguous impression. Most people going 'dark' are managing something private, not concealing preparation.
contexts: Ordinary private matters — an affair or new relationship, a medical or mental-health issue, financial embarrassment or debt, a second job or side venture; each produces gaps, guardedness, and undocumented spending with no target linkage.

Legitimate privacy and digital hygiene — routine social-media cleanup, use of encrypted apps and separate work devices for lawful reasons, deleting old posts out of general reputation management rather than anti-forensic intent.
Normal life-stage stress and withdrawal — grief, burnout, job loss, relationship breakdown, or adolescence producing reduced sharing, irritability at questions, and changed routines.
Legitimate cash and travel behavior — cash-preferring individuals, cultural or generational financial habits, undocumented trips for family or personal reasons that leave the same 'gap' signature.

Contextual over-reading by a motivated observer — a suspicious partner, rival, or estranged relative interpreting ordinary secrecy as sinister, especially amid custody disputes, breakups, or workplace conflict.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Because concealment's only direct signal is when it fails, any single slip should be read against the whole picture rather than dismissed as isolated; and concealment findings that correlate with staging-class behaviors elsewhere — weapon acquisition, dry runs, schedule alignment with an action window — warrant immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Tier determination for concealment findings depends on three factors: the credibility of the indicator per the credibility criteria, breadth across modalities (physical gaps, digital compartmentalization/scrubbing, financial anonymization, interpersonal guardedness), and persistence over time. A single low-credibility indicator with an available ordinary explanation sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility indicator — a recovered scrubbed statement of intent, a surfaced compartmentalized device, a checkable contradiction tied to a target — sits at the investigation tier. Cross-modal corroboration, two or more concealment indicators correlating against the same actor across different modes, sits at the elevation tier and should be treated as active mobilization concealment rather than ordinary privacy. Concealment that intensifies and self-corrects as a specific window approaches, or that persists despite questioning, sits at the committed-actor tier. Critically, concealment fragments distribute across observers who each see only a piece — peer, family, IT, finance; multiple lower-priority indicators correlating temporally or modally routinely compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single fragment warrants, and consumer triage tooling must make this aggregation rule explicit because the individual reports will each look benign. Tier-triggered actions: the monitoring tier triggers logging and cross-source aggregation workflows so scattered fragments can be correlated; the investigation tier triggers actor-identification, resolution of the contradiction, and a subject-vulnerability check; the elevation tier triggers protective coordination and interview/collection planning appropriate to an actor believed to be actively mobilizing under cover; the committed-actor tier triggers defensive-posture upgrade and consideration of intervention before the operation completes. Confirmed actor identity matching a known threat actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

tactics.name: Concealment
tactics.notes: Managing physical appearance and behavior to avoid detection under human observation. Actor blends into the environment appropriate to the location and context — adjusting dress, behavior, pace, and attention pattern to match expected profiles. Concealment is an ongoing behavioral discipline throughout the Approach phase, not a single action.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor's stated activity pattern develops gaps inconsistent with normal life — unaccounted-for time, unexplained absences, missing receipts or location data
Threat actor maintains compartmentalized communications — separate device, encrypted application, anonymous account — for a compartmented set of contacts kept separate from normal life
Threat actor's online presence becomes selectively curated — deletion of grievance posts, suppression of identifiable statements of intent, removal of evidence from social media
Threat actor's financial pattern shows withdrawals or transfers consistent with cash or anonymized-payment operational expenses, with no corresponding documented purpose
Threat actor introduces inconsistencies between stated activities and physical or digital evidence — claimed locations not matching cell-tower data, claimed meetings with no corresponding records

Threat actor's behavior toward family members or peers becomes guarded — withdrawal from normal sharing, requests for privacy that exceed ordinary, irritability at routine questions about plans or whereabouts

countermeasures.measure: Maintain peer and family awareness of behavioral-change indicators — uncharacteristic withdrawal, evasiveness about plans, unexplained gaps in routine — with low-threshold reporting paths to security or threat assessment teams
countermeasures.limitations: Behavioral changes have many benign explanations (personal stress, depression, life events); reporting culture must encourage flagging without requiring certainty

countermeasures.measure: For organizationally-employed individuals already in the threat assessment caseload, monitor work-account patterns for compartmentalization signals — separate browser sessions, encrypted-tunnel activity, unusual access patterns
countermeasures.limitations: Encrypted tunnels and personal-device usage can defeat work-account monitoring. Privacy and labor-relations considerations require careful scoping

countermeasures.measure: Establish low-threshold reporting paths for associates who notice incongruity between another person's account of activities and observable evidence
countermeasures.limitations: Many incongruities have benign explanations and are not reported because the associate can't articulate why something feels off

countermeasures.measure: Conduct periodic financial-pattern analysis (where authorized) for individuals already in the active threat assessment caseload, focused on cash withdrawals, anonymized payments, and procurement consistent with operational expense profiles
countermeasures.limitations: Financial monitoring of identified individuals carries jurisdiction-specific legal constraints; cash transactions have many lawful uses

response_protocols.trigger: Single Concealment indicator reported (peer-report of behavioral change, financial pattern shift, online curation activity)
response_protocols.action: Document the indicator. Conduct a 5-business-day preliminary assessment that includes (a) corroboration through additional reports or data sources, (b) baseline review of the threat actor's prior behavioral pattern, (c) cross-reference against any active threat assessment case. Determine whether observed change rises to operational concern.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Concealment pattern coupled with concurrent indicators from another Phase 1 or Phase 2 tactic.
response_protocols.legal_notes: Behavioral observations of associates and family members are protected information; consult legal before any inquiry beyond the immediate report. Document factually. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

response_protocols.trigger: Multiple Concealment indicators co-observed for the same threat actor OR concealment activity coupled with capability acquisition, cover construction, or pathway-stage progression
response_protocols.action: Convene the threat management team within 24 hours. Conduct formal threat assessment. Concealment combined with other Phase 1/2 indicators is a high-confidence signal of operational sophistication and pending action. Implement enhanced protective posture. Coordinate with law enforcement.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Concealment pattern persists or intensifies OR pathway indicators progress through preparation stage.
response_protocols.legal_notes: Concealment is rarely unlawful in itself; the response posture is preventive intelligence, not criminal investigation, until concrete operational indicators surface. Document the indicator constellation thoroughly. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

tactics.field_notes: The signature of Concealment is what a security professional doesn't see — the meeting with no record, the trip with no documented purpose, the equipment that doesn't show up in any inventory. Concealment is constant through mobilization, and its only direct signal is when it fails. The threat actor reveals the operation through a slip, a contradiction, an artifact left where it shouldn't be — and that slip is often the only pre-execution signal a threat assessment team gets. The detection vector is the details that don't add up — a story that doesn't quite fit, a routine that doesn't quite match the cover, an absence where presence is expected. Concealment intensifies as the operation approaches execution; the threat actor is increasingly aware that any leak compromises the plan, and the discipline tightens accordingly.
observed_contexts: workplace violence case where the threat actor's documented routine showed a 90-minute weekly gap with no claimed activity, recognized as concealment only after the attack identified an unaccounted-for rehearsal site
domestic case where peer reports of evasiveness and unexplained nighttime absences preceded the attack by weeks, but were not aggregated to the threat assessment level until after the incident

extremist case where the threat actor curated their social media presence in the months before the attack — deleting older grievance posts and suppressing identifiable statements of intent — recognized as anti-forensic concealment in retrospect
[literature: FBI-PREATTACK-2018 — pre-attack pattern of financial withdrawals consistent with cash-based operational expense in active shooter cases]

insider threat case where compartmentalized communications via a separate device were detected through corroborating peer report and IT-anomaly observation, leading to interruption before mobilization completed

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises when a breach or breach attempt is corroborated by more than one control surface — an alert officer's account backed by access-log anomalies, camera correlation, or credential-system telemetry — and when recoverable evidence physically ties the actor to the entry event. Credibility falls when the report rests on a single unverified observation, when the entry admits a routine access explanation that was never checked, and when the timing or identity details cannot be reconstructed from any independent record.
high_signal_anchors: Multi-surface corroboration — a witness account of the breach attempt aligns with independent records such as badge-reader logs, camera correlation, or a sponsoring-contact validation failure, against the same entry event.

Credential-system telemetry — access-control logs show a badge presented at the perimeter with no corresponding swipe at expected interior checkpoints, or a credential used outside its registered holder's normal pattern.

Recovered material evidence — fabricated work-order documentation, a forged or stolen credential, or defeated-lock forensics physically link the actor to the entry point; does not depend on accurate witness recall.

First-hand officer fidelity — a named security officer directly challenged or observed the actor and reports the pretext used, the entry point, the timing relative to shift change, and a description of the actor and any documents presented.

Behavioral specificity — the actor presented a specific claimed appointment, named a specific sponsoring contact, or used a service-side access point in a way that maps to a known operational plan rather than casual wrong-door error.
Reporting through accountable channel — the account originates from a trained access-control professional filing through a formal incident channel, not an informal after-the-fact rumor.
low_signal_anchors: Single-surface weakness — one officer's uncorroborated impression of a suspicious entrant with no supporting log, camera, or credential record.
Routine-access explanation unrebutted — the entry fits an ordinary contractor, delivery, or visitor pattern that investigation did not actually rule out.
Timing-detail loss — the entry event cannot be pinned to a specific window and no record independently fixes when it occurred.
Identity ambiguity — description of the entrant is too generic to distinguish the actor from routine service traffic through the same access point.
Reporting delay — the breach is reconstructed long after the fact, so entry-point details may be retrofitted to a threat narrative rather than observed at the time.

Source-motivation misalignment — the report originates with a party who has a structural motive to characterize an ordinary entry as a breach (staffing dispute, vendor conflict, blame-shifting after a loss).

capability.criteria: Capability rises when the breach method shows preparation matched to the target's protective posture — durable cover, working credentials, timing tuned to defender rhythms, and technical means to defeat the specific control in play. Capability falls when the attempt is improvised, the cover collapses under the first challenge, the credential fails validation, or the actor has no means to defeat the control beyond hoping it is unattended.
high_signal_anchors: Posture-matched method — social-engineering approach for a low-profile access point versus technical defeat for a hardened one; the actor selected the method that fits this perimeter rather than a generic try.
Durable cover construction — fabricated contractor uniform, prepared work-order paperwork, or a claimed appointment that holds up at reception and is not immediately recognized as false.
Working credential tradecraft — a fabricated or stolen badge good enough to pass initial presentation, or knowledge of which credential type the perimeter reader will accept.
Defender-rhythm timing — the attempt is staged at shift change, off-hours, or a coverage seam, indicating the actor learned the schedule of the people and cameras guarding the perimeter.
Physical-defeat competence — demonstrated means to climb, force, or bypass the specific control (electronic lock, fence line, secured door) at a point chosen to be out of active observation.
Insider-supported validation — an insider sponsor is positioned to vouch for the cover or open a service-side path, giving the breach a validation layer a lone outsider could not manufacture.
low_signal_anchors: Improvised attempt — actor tries a door or gate opportunistically with no cover, credential, or prepared story.
Cover collapse on first challenge — reception or an officer immediately recognizes the pretext or paperwork as false.
Credential rejection — the presented badge fails the reader or the holder plainly does not match the credential's registered owner on the first check.
No defeat means for the control in play — actor faces a hardened perimeter with only a hope that it is unattended; no tool, technique, or access to bypass it.
Front-of-house-only approach — actor attempts the most observed, most staffed entry with no awareness of the friendlier service-side surface.
Timing blind to defender rhythm — attempt made during peak staffing and full camera coverage, showing no reconnaissance of when the perimeter is weak.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when the actor's presence at the perimeter is purposeful and target-directed rather than incidental — deliberate defeat or deception of an access control, concentration on a non-standard entry chosen to avoid detection, and behavior consistent with reaching a specific protected subject. Intent falls when the entry has a verifiable legitimate purpose, when the actor withdraws on challenge without persistence, and when nothing ties the attempt to a particular target.
high_signal_anchors: Deliberate control defeat or deception — tailgating an authorized person, presenting a fabricated or stolen credential, or forcing a control, as opposed to an honest mistaken-door entry.

Non-standard entry selection — actor concentrates on a loading dock, service entrance, or camera gap specifically because it is less observed, indicating a choice to avoid detection rather than convenience.
Timing chosen against verification — presenting off-hours or when the sponsoring contact cannot be reached, so the cover cannot be checked in real time.

Target-directed movement after entry — once past the perimeter, the actor's path orients toward the protected subject's location rather than wandering or conducting business consistent with the claimed purpose.
Persistence across control failure — after one entry point challenges or rejects the actor, the actor attempts a different point or a different method rather than abandoning the objective.

Hostile attribution paired with the breach — the actor has expressed grievance, blame, or threat toward the protected subject AND is now attempting to defeat the perimeter around that subject. The combination is intent-diagnostic in a way no single indicator captures.
low_signal_anchors: Verifiable legitimate purpose — the entrant is a real contractor, vendor, delivery, or visitor whose business and sponsor check out on inquiry.
Withdrawal on challenge — actor leaves immediately when questioned and makes no second attempt at any point.
No target linkage — the entry cannot be tied to any specific subject; behavior fits general trespass, theft, or shelter-seeking rather than person-targeting.
Wrong-door ambiguity — entry at a non-standard point is consistent with genuine confusion about the correct access route and self-corrects.
Single incidental encounter — one anomalous presentation with no persistence, no target-directed movement, and no supporting indicator.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the actor can convert a breach into reach of the protected subject — an unobserved or uncovered entry point, defender-schedule knowledge, an exploited insider path, and the positional ability to be at the perimeter when the subject is predictably inside. Opportunity falls when the perimeter is actively defended and adapted to, when access pathways are structurally closed, and when the subject's protective posture blocks the actor's known method; when opportunity appears reduced, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: Uncovered entry point — a side gate, service door, or perimeter gap with no camera coverage or active observation, letting the actor reach the protected space before any detection signal is generated.
Defender-schedule knowledge — actor knows shift-change windows, patrol rotations, or reception staffing gaps and stages the breach into them. The informational dimension of opportunity.

Positional presence in the subject's window — actor can physically be at the perimeter during the hours the protected subject is predictably present. The positional-and-availability dimension; complementary to schedule knowledge, not redundant — knowing the seam without being able to be there, or being there without knowing the seam, each falls short of a converted opportunity.

Exploited insider path — an insider sponsor is actively validating cover, opening a service entrance, or timing a coordinated entry for the actor. The EXPLOITATION pattern, not a dormant connection, is what is high-signal.
Interior reach past the perimeter — the breached point leads, without further hardened controls, into the space where the subject actually is, so the perimeter is the last real barrier.
Legitimate-role access — actor holds a role (vendor, contractor, staff) that grants unsupervised passage through the perimeter, making the breach a use of granted access rather than a defeat of it.
low_signal_anchors: Breach defeated by active defense — an alert officer caught the tailgate or challenged the credential and interrupted the actor before the subject was reached. Durable when the posture that caught it is sustained.
Structural access closure — the actor's pathway is gone (role terminated, insider sponsor removed, service-entrance procedure changed); a durable structural change, not a temporary gap.
Institutional rule-out of insider support — access audit or formal process actively cleared the possibility of an insider path rather than merely failing to find one. High-confidence absence.
Layered interior controls behind the perimeter — even a successful perimeter breach lands the actor in a controlled space still separated from the subject by further hardened barriers.
Withdrawal without adaptation — actor left after being challenged and did not return or try another point. Transient: may flip back if the actor adapts the method.

Subject posture blocks the method — the protected subject changed movement patterns, relocated, or hardened the venue so the actor's known breach method no longer reaches them. Transient unless the barrier is sustained.

false_positive_context.criteria: Perimeter access points see constant legitimate traffic that can surface-mimic a breach — a contractor at the wrong gate looks like an actor probing entry, a new employee tailgating out of habit looks like a defeat of access control, a delivery driver off-schedule looks like off-hours infiltration. What distinguishes a false positive from a real concern is whether the entrant has a verifiable legitimate purpose, a transparent and checkable identity, and institutional accountability that survives a challenge — not merely whether the entry looked unusual.
contexts: Verified service and business access — contractors, vendors, delivery drivers, maintenance, and inspectors with legitimate site-visit business, including off-hours and service-side entries their work genuinely requires.

Habitual or orientation error — new employees and visitors tailgating, using a wrong or non-standard entrance, or misjudging timing out of unfamiliarity rather than intent, self-correcting on direction.

Authorized security and legal activity — licensed security professionals conducting sanctioned physical penetration tests or access audits; law-enforcement or investigators operating with lawful authority at the perimeter.
Credential and system faults — genuine badge malfunctions, un-swiped interior readers, expired-but-valid credentials, or biometric mismatches caused by equipment error rather than impersonation.

Community and personal connection — current and former staff, family, or associates with a real reason to be at the perimeter (retirement visit, personal pickup, escorting) whose presence is accountable on inquiry.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: A perimeter breach or credible breach attempt is late-stage by definition — every earlier tactic that could have interrupted the actor has already failed, and the breach point sits inside the Mobilization phase — so tier logic here is compressed toward action. Escalation tier-determination depends on three factors: credibility of the breach indicator per the credibility criteria, the degree of deliberate control defeat or deception versus routine-access ambiguity, and whether the actor has interior reach toward the protected subject. A single low-credibility anomaly with an unrebutted routine-access explanation — an off-schedule entrant, an un-swiped reader — sits at the monitoring tier pending verification. A single high-credibility deliberate defeat or deception (confirmed tailgate, fabricated or stolen credential, forced non-standard entry) sits at the investigation tier and warrants immediate actor-identification effort and a check on the protected subject's current location and posture. Corroboration across control surfaces — a challenge account plus credential-system telemetry or camera correlation against the same entry event — sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating the breach as an in-progress approach on the subject, activating interception and protective response. A breach that continues or recurs despite an initial challenge, or that is validated by an exploited insider path, sits at the committed-actor tier and warrants an immediate defensive-posture upgrade and law-enforcement coordination. Multiple lower-confidence indicators correlating temporally or across access points may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding warrants in isolation; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Because this tactic places a hostile actor at or inside the last barrier around a person, any high-credibility finding here — and especially an actor identity matching a known threat actor profile — warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination and real-time protection of the subject regardless of internal tier.

tactics.name: Perimeter Breach
tactics.notes: Defeating the outermost security layer protecting access to the target — building perimeters, residential security, vehicle protection details, or controlled access zones. The method varies by target protective posture: social engineering for low-profile targets, technical defeat for hardened environments.
tactics.cpn_notes: Credential cloning, RFID/NFC skimming, and electronic lock exploit tools are cyber-enabled defeat methods that bypass physical barriers without direct force. Access control systems that are digitally exploitable change the threat calculus for protected subjects in secured environments.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor presents at a perimeter access point at off-hours or with timing inconsistent with verified visitor schedules, claimed appointments, or sponsoring contact
Threat actor attempts to bypass perimeter controls by tailgating an authorized individual through a secured access point
Threat actor uses a fabricated or stolen credential to attempt authorized passage through a perimeter access point
Threat actor defeats a physical perimeter control — climbing a fence, forcing a door, defeating an electronic lock — at a location not under active observation
Threat actor breaches the perimeter at a non-standard entry point — loading dock, service entrance, perimeter gap not under camera coverage
Threat actor's badge or credential is presented at the perimeter but the holder's biometric, photo, or behavioral profile does not match the credential's registered owner

countermeasures.measure: Maintain layered perimeter design with multiple sequential access controls so that a single-point breach does not yield interior access — outer fence, controlled entry, interior badge zones, sensitive-area additional barriers
countermeasures.limitations: Layered controls add cost and friction to legitimate operations. Insider sponsors with multi-tier access can defeat layering

countermeasures.measure: Conduct random-interval physical checks of non-primary perimeter access points — loading dock, service entrance, perimeter gaps — to validate posture and detect attempted breaches at unmanned locations
countermeasures.limitations: Random-interval checks have coverage gaps; sophisticated threat actors may infer the inspection cadence given enough observations

countermeasures.measure: Implement two-factor identity verification at perimeter access points — credential plus visual or biometric confirmation — for sensitivity-tiered locations
countermeasures.limitations: Two-factor friction can erode legitimate operations during high-traffic periods; biometric capture has privacy and regulatory implications

countermeasures.measure: Establish anti-tailgating training and physical controls — mantrap vestibule, single-occupant entry, badge re-validation — at high-sensitivity perimeter access points
countermeasures.limitations: Mantrap vestibules slow legitimate operations and may be bypassed via emergency exits or coordinated insider tailgating

response_protocols.trigger: Single Perimeter Breach indicator detected (off-hours unverified presence, tailgating attempt, fabricated credential at access point)
response_protocols.action: Detain the individual politely if lawful; verify identity through sponsoring contact or external corroboration. Notify the threat assessment team within the same business hour. Preserve any physical artifacts and access-attempt logs. Activate enhanced perimeter monitoring at adjacent access points.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Identity cannot be corroborated OR breach attempt connects to other concerning context (prior surveillance, prior cover construction).
response_protocols.legal_notes: Detention or extended challenge of an individual carries legal implications that vary by jurisdiction; coordinate with legal before any action beyond polite verification. Trespass and pretexting laws vary materially. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

response_protocols.trigger: Confirmed perimeter breach OR breach attempt coupled with capability acquisition or cover construction OR threat actor flees on challenge
response_protocols.action: Activate emergency response. Initiate facility lockdown per protocol. Notify law enforcement immediately. Implement enhanced protective posture for the targeted subject. Capture and preserve all physical and digital evidence of the breach attempt. Brief executive leadership.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Breach reaches sensitive interior area OR threat actor demonstrates means and proximity to the targeted subject.
response_protocols.legal_notes: Lockdown and emergency response are protective actions that do not require law enforcement authorization. Document the basis for initiating emergency protocols. Pretexting at protected sites and trespass into restricted areas may carry independent criminal liability; preserve evidence carefully. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

tactics.field_notes: Perimeter Breach almost never starts at the perimeter — by the time the threat actor reaches the breach point, the work was done in capability acquisition, cover construction, and rehearsal. The breach itself is often the easiest part of the operation because every choice that made it possible has already been made. Detection at the breach point is late detection by definition: every other tactic has failed to interrupt the threat actor. What surfaces in retrospect is usually the breach attempt that didn't quite fit — the contractor at the wrong gate, the badge that hadn't been swiped at expected interior checkpoints, the visitor whose sponsoring contact couldn't be reached. The most successful breaches in observed cases are the ones that didn't generate a detection signal until the threat actor was already inside the protected space.
observed_contexts: facility attack where the threat actor used a fabricated contractor uniform and prepared work-order documentation to pass perimeter reception, with the breach recognized only after cross-camera correlation in after-action review

executive protection case where a tailgating attempt at a parking-garage badge gate was caught by an alert security officer, leading to identification of the threat actor and interruption before reaching the targeted subject
insider-conspirator case where an external accomplice presented stolen credentials at a service entrance during a coordinated shift change, supported by an insider sponsor who validated the cover

Casework pattern: service-side access points — loading docks, vendor entrances, freight elevators — present a friendlier social-engineering surface than the front of house, and breach attempts during mobilization concentrate there

domestic attack at a protected residence where the threat actor breached the perimeter at a side gate with no camera coverage, with detection occurring only when the threat actor was already inside the property

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises when tier-transit anomalies are corroborated across independent access-control and observation systems, persist as a coherent path rather than a single flagged swipe, and are backed by recoverable evidence — badge logs, cross-camera correlation, door-controller telemetry — that survives without depending on accurate witness recall. Credibility falls when a single anomalous read is the only signal, when the transit admits an ordinary explanation nobody ruled out, and when the report comes late enough that the path is reconstructed rather than observed.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-system corroboration — the same subject's zone transit is independently visible in badge-reader logs, interior CCTV, and door-controller telemetry across overlapping timeframes, not a lone reader event.
Coherent multi-tier path — anomalous access reconstructs into a continuous route through successive tiers (lobby to controlled to restricted), not an isolated out-of-zone swipe.

Material access evidence — badge-swipe records above the holder's authorization, elevator-control logs, or bump-key audio-sensor traces that physically place the actor at each tier without relying on witness memory.

First-hand transition-witness fidelity — a named staff member who was tailgated, escorted, or socially engineered at a specific tier reports the pretext used, the actor's description, the transition point, and the timing with high resolution.
Path specificity — the reported movement names specific tiers, specific access points, and a specific end zone tied to the protected individual, not vague 'seen where they shouldn't be.'
Source motivation aligned with accuracy — security or access-control staff reporting a validated log anomaly through formal channel, not an informal 'that person looked off' tip.
low_signal_anchors: Single-read weakness — one out-of-zone badge event with no supporting camera or controller data and no path context around it.
Content-specificity weakness — 'someone was on a floor they didn't belong on' with no tier, timing, or access-method detail that could distinguish transit from a wrong turn.
Temporal-pattern weakness — a one-time tier anomaly with no continuation to the next tier and no repeat, consistent with an escort lapse rather than penetration.
Source-motivation misalignment — reporter has structural reason to flag the person (interpersonal dispute, turf friction over access authority) independent of the transit itself.
Unrebutted mundane explanation — the out-of-zone appearance fits an authorized-but-unlogged escort, a propped door, or a legitimate cross-department errand that investigation never checked.
Reconstructive memory — transit reported so long after the fact that the 'rehearsed path' impression may be retrofitted onto ordinary building movement.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when the actor defeats each successive access layer through a distinct, deliberate method — credential cloning, elevator or lock-control manipulation, durable pretexts that convert staff at tier edges — and demonstrates working knowledge of the tier topology rather than improvising. Capability falls when transit relies on a single lucky lapse, when pretexts collapse on first contact, when only one tier was ever crossed, and when out-of-zone presence shows confusion rather than method.
high_signal_anchors: Layer-specific method diversity — the actor uses a different, appropriate technique at each tier (tailgate one, social-engineer the next, bypass a lock at a third), indicating deliberate defeat of a layered design rather than one repeated trick.
Technical access tradecraft — credential cloning, elevator-system manipulation, electronic-lock or door-control bypass, or bump-key sequencing executed cleanly and without force.

Pretext durability across transitions — cover stories and escort-manipulation lines hold up with staff at successive tiers; personnel did not recognize they were being converted into an access vector.
Tier-topology fluency — movement shows the actor knows badge-zone boundaries, which tiers gate which, and where the seams between public-facing and restricted zones sit.
Infrastructure-defeat capability — actor reaches and manipulates interior security infrastructure (camera systems, alarm panels, door controllers) to smooth onward transit.
