Insider-sponsored bypass — actor is escorted through multiple zones by an insider with no zone-by-zone verification, converting a sponsor relationship into layered access beyond either party's authorization.
low_signal_anchors: Single-method repetition — actor only tailgates and stalls at the first tier that actually checks credentials.
Pretext failure at the edge — staff at a transition immediately recognized the escort or access request as irregular and stopped it.
Conspicuous transit posture — actor wanders, backtracks, or lingers at tier boundaries in a way that reads as lost rather than routed.
No infrastructure reach — actor cannot influence any door, elevator, or camera system; movement depends entirely on human lapses.
One-tier reach — only the outermost controlled layer was crossed; no evidence of a method for the next tier.
Force-dependent entry — actor resorted to forcing a door or barrier, signaling absence of the covert access capability this tactic rewards.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when transit is directional — each defeated tier moves the actor closer to the protected individual's location rather than dispersing through the building — and especially when the path matches a pre-determined route inconsistent with any claimed destination, or pairs zone penetration with expressed grievance toward the subject. Intent falls when out-of-zone movement is exploratory or errand-shaped, when a transition happened once without follow-on, and when a verifiable legitimate purpose for reaching the zone surfaces.
high_signal_anchors: Directional convergence — successive tier defeats trend toward the subject's known location or immediate environment, not lateral wandering.
Route-destination mismatch — the actor's interior path matches a pre-planned course inconsistent with the destination declared at the perimeter or in the visitor log.
Operational selectivity in transit — actor bypasses reception and escort touchpoints specifically, chooses tiers that gate access to the subject, and avoids tiers irrelevant to reaching them.
Sustained tier-by-tier adaptation — actor adjusts method as each layer presents different controls, tracking the defensive design across the transit rather than one-and-done.

Pre-planning artifacts — demonstrated foreknowledge of tier topology, badge-zone boundaries, or supervisory shift changes inconsistent with a first-time visitor, implying the path was studied for later use.

Hostile attribution paired with penetration — actor has expressed grievance, blame, or hostile attribution toward the protected individual AND is observed defeating interior layers toward that individual's zone. The combination is intent-diagnostic in a way no single indicator captures.
low_signal_anchors: Exploratory movement — out-of-zone appearance that meanders without converging on any protected location, consistent with curiosity or disorientation.
One transition without follow-on — a single tier was crossed but the actor did not press toward the next or return.
Verifiable legitimate purpose — contractor, vendor, auditor, or escorted-guest status surfaces on inquiry and accounts for the zone reached.
No route pre-determination — path reads as improvised and reactive to signage, not matched to a studied course toward the subject.
Destination ambiguity — actor's transit could terminate at many zones; no concentration on the one associated with the protected individual.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the layered design offers the actor a workable path to the subject's zone at a time the subject is predictably present — weak tier verification, insider sponsorship being exploited, knowledge of shift changes and badge-zone seams, and positional presence inside the outer layers when the subject is there. Opportunity falls when a tier actively defeats the transit, when insider pathways are institutionally closed rather than merely unused, and when the subject's presence or the zone's hardening removes the actionable window; when opportunity looks reduced, whether the reduction is durable matters.
high_signal_anchors: Unverified tier transitions — successive layers admit the actor without zone-by-zone validation; escort or badge checks are absent or unenforced at the seams.

Subject-presence timing — actor's transit is scheduled to reach the subject's zone during a window when the subject is predictably present. The informational dimension of opportunity: knowing when the target is at the end of the path.

Interior positional footing — actor already holds legitimate access to an outer tier (lobby, maintenance, vendor zone) and only needs to defeat the inner layers, closing most of the distance to the subject's environment. The positional dimension, complementary to presence timing: standing inside tier two with no idea when the subject is in tier five has footing without a window; knowing the schedule from outside the building has a window without footing.
Tier-seam and rotation knowledge — actor knows supervisory shift changes, badge-zone boundaries, and which transitions go unwatched, exposing exploitable gaps in the layered design.

Insider sponsor being exploited — an identified insider is actively escorting or credentialing the actor through zones beyond authorization; the active exploitation, not a dormant contact, is what's high-signal.
Direct inner-zone access — actor holds an unsupervised legitimate role that already places them at or adjacent to the subject's tier.
low_signal_anchors: Transit defeated at a hardened tier — a layer with enforced zone-by-zone verification actively stopped the actor's advance. Durable signal: sticky unless the actor acquires a new method or the tier's enforcement lapses.
Institutional rule-out of insider sponsorship — access audits or formal process actively cleared the escort/credential pathway, not merely failed to find one. High-confidence absence.

Structural access degradation — the actor's outer-tier foothold was terminated (badge revoked, vendor contract ended, sponsor relationship severed). Distinct from a temporary lapse: a durable structural change.
Challenged-and-withdrew — actor was stopped or questioned at a transition and left without adapting or re-attempting. Transient: may flip back if the actor returns with a new pretext.

Subject not present in the target zone — the end of the path is empty during the window the actor can reach it; physical convergence has not been timed to presence. Transient: may close if schedules align.

Zone hardening blocks known methods — new zone-by-zone verification, re-badging, or active supervision at seams neutralizes the actor's demonstrated techniques. Transient unless the hardening is sustained.

false_positive_context.criteria: Legitimate building operations routinely produce out-of-zone movement that resembles Zone Penetration on the surface — a contractor genuinely working an upper floor, a new employee taking a wrong turn, an escorted guest whose escort stepped away. What distinguishes a false positive from a real concern is whether the transit has a verifiable legitimate purpose, a transparent and validated identity behind the credential, and institutional accountability — a work order, an authorized escort, an access grant on record — that can be checked against the path.
contexts: Authorized work and service access — contractors, maintenance, IT, and vendors with valid work orders that legitimately require multi-tier movement; facilities staff performing rounds across zones.
Legitimate escorted access — guests, interviewees, or auditors moving through zones under an authorized escort where the escort momentarily lapsed or went unlogged, not an escort being manipulated.
Orientation and onboarding — new employees, transfers, or temporary staff who cross a tier boundary by mistake while learning the building's layout and badge zones.
Sanctioned security testing — authorized red-team or physical-penetration assessments and licensed security consultants deliberately probing tier controls under an approved scope.
Emergency and event exceptions — drills, evacuations, medical response, or sanctioned events during which normal zone verification is intentionally relaxed and cross-tier movement is expected.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Findings correlating with staging-class behaviors elsewhere — weapon acquisition, an observed dry run of the interior route, or transit timed to a confirmed action window against the subject — warrant immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier, because Zone Penetration sits in Mobilization and each defeated layer shortens the distance to the protected individual in real time. Escalation tier-determination for this tactic's findings depends on three factors: credibility of the transit indicator per the credibility criteria, breadth across access-control and observation systems, and persistence as a coherent multi-tier path. A single low-credibility out-of-zone read with an available mundane explanation sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility tier defeat with directional specificity toward the subject sits at the investigation tier. Cross-system corroboration — badge, camera, and controller telemetry reconstructing the same subject's continuous path across two or more tiers — sits at the elevation tier and should be treated as an in-progress approach, not retrospective anomaly review. A path that continues to advance despite a tier being hardened against it sits at the committed-actor tier and indicates an actor already inside the layered design and adapting. Multiple lower-priority transit anomalies correlating temporally or across systems may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single read warrants in isolation; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit, since the detection difficulty of this tactic rises with each inner tier and the upstream layers have already failed by the time the actor nears the subject. Tier-triggered response actions: the monitoring tier triggers access-log correlation and pattern-detection workflows; the investigation tier triggers actor-identification and immediate verification of the subject's location and presence; the elevation tier triggers real-time interdiction of the transit and lockdown of inner-tier access appropriate to the subject's posture; the committed-actor tier triggers protective movement of the subject and defensive-posture upgrade across the remaining layers; confirmed actor identity matching a known threat actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

tactics.name: Zone Penetration
tactics.notes: Moving through successive security layers after initial perimeter breach — from public space to controlled access, from controlled access to restricted zones, from restricted zones to the target's location. Each layer requires a distinct access method; failure at any layer aborts the approach.
tactics.cpn_notes: Electronic lock bypass and elevator system manipulation extend the actor's reach through security-tiered environments. Physical security systems with digital control planes are vulnerable to zone penetration via cyber methods without physical force.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor's badge is swiped at an access point above the tier authorized for the credential holder, with the holder either physically present or credentials cloned
Threat actor moves through interior security tiers via tailgating, escort manipulation, or social engineering of personnel staffing each tier
Threat actor uses elevator system manipulation, electronic lock bypass, or door-control system manipulation to defeat tier-internal access controls without force
Threat actor's path through the protected environment matches a pre-determined route inconsistent with the destination claimed at perimeter or in visitor logs
Threat actor accesses interior security infrastructure (camera systems, alarm panels, communication systems) at any point during transit through tiered zones
Threat actor's interior access pattern shows pre-planning artifacts — knowledge of tier topology, badge zone boundaries, supervisory shift changes — inconsistent with a first-time visitor

countermeasures.measure: Implement zone-by-zone access logging with anomaly alerting for badge use at unfamiliar tiers, off-hours interior access, and access patterns inconsistent with the holder's job function
countermeasures.limitations: Anomaly tuning requires baseline behavioral data per credential holder; high-turnover environments produce excess false positives

countermeasures.measure: Maintain interior CCTV coverage at zone transitions with cross-camera correlation supporting retrospective path reconstruction across the entire protected environment
countermeasures.limitations: Coverage gaps and non-coverage zones (restrooms, executive offices) cannot be addressed by CCTV alone; cross-camera correlation requires either operator time or analytics support

countermeasures.measure: Deploy two-factor zone authentication at sensitive-tier transitions — badge plus visual identification, or badge plus biometric — with logging of authentication failures
countermeasures.limitations: Two-factor friction can erode legitimate operations during high-traffic periods; biometric capture has privacy and regulatory implications

countermeasures.measure: Establish escort accountability protocols requiring sponsoring contact identification, visit purpose validation, and continuous-presence requirements within sensitive tiers
countermeasures.limitations: Escort discipline degrades during sustained operations and across shift changes; staff with established relationships may relax verification under social pressure

response_protocols.trigger: Single Zone Penetration indicator detected (badge anomaly, cross-camera inconsistency, route mismatch with stated destination)
response_protocols.action: Document the indicator. Conduct same-business-day verification of the credential holder, the visit purpose, and the sponsoring contact. Pull cross-camera footage to reconstruct the threat actor's path. Notify the threat assessment team. Activate enhanced posture at adjacent sensitive tiers.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Verification fails OR path reconstruction reveals additional unauthorized tier access OR threat actor identity ties to prior threat case.
response_protocols.legal_notes: Interior CCTV footage and access logs are generally accessible under normal security policy; coordinate with legal before retention or sharing beyond standard policy. Document factually. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

response_protocols.trigger: Confirmed unauthorized zone penetration OR penetration coupled with capability acquisition, cover construction, or pathway-stage progression
response_protocols.action: Activate emergency response. Initiate facility lockdown or containment as appropriate to the tier breached. Notify law enforcement immediately. Implement enhanced protective posture for the targeted subject. Capture and preserve all physical and digital evidence including credentials, vehicles, and devices in the threat actor's possession.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Penetration reaches the targeted subject's immediate environment OR threat actor demonstrates means and proximity.
response_protocols.legal_notes: Trespass into restricted areas may carry independent criminal liability; preserve evidence carefully. Use of force by security personnel is governed by jurisdiction-specific authority. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

tactics.field_notes: The signature of Zone Penetration is movement through a building that doesn't match the threat actor's stated reason for being there — a contractor on an executive floor, a vendor in a restricted communications room, a visitor escorted past the meeting room and never seen exiting. Each tier of a layered security design exists because the previous tier admitted someone whose access at the next tier wasn't validated. What an investigator looks for is the badge swipe at a tier above the holder's authorization, the appearance in CCTV at a location the threat actor has no apparent business being, and the timing pattern that suggests the path was rehearsed. Zone Penetration tactics range from low-tech (tailgating one tier, then social-engineering the next) to high-tech (cloning credentials at one tier and using elevator-system manipulation to reach another). The detection difficulty rises with each tier: by the time the threat actor reaches the target's immediate environment, the upstream tiers have already failed.
observed_contexts: executive protection case where a contractor with valid lobby-tier access tailgated through three interior tiers via successive social engineering of staff at each transition, identified retrospectively through cross-camera correlation
facility attack where the threat actor cloned a maintenance-tier badge and used elevator-system manipulation to reach an executive floor without ever interacting with reception or escort staff

insider-conspirator case where an external accomplice was escorted by an insider sponsor through multiple zones with no zone-by-zone verification, allowing access to a sensitive area outside the sponsor's authorization

Across casework, tailgating and escort manipulation are the standard methods for moving across interior access tiers — attaching to legitimate movement rather than presenting credentials, especially at the edges between public-facing and restricted zones

domestic attack at a protected residence where the threat actor entered via the perimeter then defeated three interior locks in sequence using bump-key tools, recognized through audio sensor logs in retrospect

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises when the elevation shows up in the audit trail as a concrete anomaly that persists under verification — a badge swipe at the wrong tier, a visitor with no sponsoring record, a work order with no match — and when independent records corroborate that the access exceeded what the holder's actual status authorized. Credibility falls when the only evidence is a subjective impression of an out-of-place person, when the anomaly resolves to a clerical error, or when a plausible administrative explanation was never checked against the authorization system of record.
high_signal_anchors: Audit-trail corroboration — the elevation is recorded as a concrete access-control anomaly (badge swipe at a tier inconsistent with role, visitor log entry with no sponsoring record, contractor with no matching work order) rather than a witness impression.
Sponsor verification failure — the claimed sponsoring contact does not exist, is uncontactable, or affirmatively denies the engagement when a callback is attempted.
Cross-record inconsistency — the actor's presented role, the access granted, and the authorization system of record disagree with each other in a way no single benign filing explains.
First-hand grantor fidelity — the guard, receptionist, or escort who granted access is named and reports the specific pretext used, the credential presented, the tier requested, and the timing.
Temporal persistence — the same actor or credential produces elevation anomalies across multiple visits, not a single one-off log entry that could be a scan glitch.
Recovered material link — doorbell or lobby camera, a photographed badge, or a fabricated work-order artifact physically ties the actor to the elevation event independent of grantor recall.
low_signal_anchors: Impression-only report — 'someone who looked out of place on the executive floor' with no corresponding access-control record or verifiable identity.
Single unresolved log entry — one tier-mismatched swipe that has an available clerical explanation (temporary badge re-provisioning, known access-system lag) not yet ruled out.
Grantor cannot be re-contacted — the person who granted access is unidentified or unavailable, so the pretext and credential cannot be reconstructed.
Benign administrative pattern unrebutted — the anomaly fits routine facility churn (new hire, vendor onboarding, badge reissue) that investigation did not check against the authorization record.
Reporter motivation misalignment — the account comes from someone with structural reason to embellish (interpersonal dispute, staffing grievance) and no independent record backs it.
Reconstructive recall — the elevation is reported so long after the fact that the pretext details may be retrofitted to a threat narrative rather than observed at the time.

capability.criteria: Capability rises with the operational craft required to defeat trust rather than barriers — durable pretexts, credible fabricated or cloned credentials, coordination with an insider, and the situational read to select the moment and the person most likely to grant access without challenge. Capability falls with clumsy pretexts that draw immediate suspicion, credentials that fail on first inspection, and elevation attempts that depend on luck rather than any repeatable method the actor can execute again.
high_signal_anchors: Durable pretext craft — the social-engineering framing (urgent need, name-dropped senior, plausible vendor role) holds up under grantor scrutiny; the grantor did not recognize they were being manipulated.

Credential fabrication or cloning capability — the actor produces a badge, work order, or appointment confirmation convincing enough to pass automated or human verification, implying access to cloning tools, template knowledge, or insider-supplied specifics.
Insider coordination — the elevation is sponsored or enabled by a current or former insider who supplies badges, cover roles, or the timing to bypass credential challenges.

Grantor-selection judgment — the actor targets the receptionist, temporary guard, or escort most susceptible to pressure or least equipped to verify, showing a working model of the facility's human weak points.
Cover-for-action durability — the actor sustains an assumed role (contractor, IT support, visiting executive) across the access window rather than a single bluff, and can re-justify returning.

Verification-bypass technique — demonstrated method for defeating the specific control in play (tailgating an authorized escort, spoofing a callback, timing entry to shift change) rather than a one-off improvisation.
low_signal_anchors: Clumsy pretext — the story draws immediate suspicion; the grantor recognized the request as unusual on first contact.
Credential fails inspection — the presented badge or work order is visibly off and does not survive routine verification.
No fallback when challenged — a single callback or ID request collapses the attempt and the actor has no adapted second approach.
Opportunistic tailgating only — the actor slips in behind others with no assumed role or pretext to justify presence once inside.
No insider or material support — reach depends entirely on the actor's own bluff with no fabricated artifact, cloned credential, or insider assist.
Single-point improvisation — the elevation worked once by luck (an unattended door, a distracted guard) with no repeatable method the actor controls.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when the elevation is purposeful reach toward a specific target rather than generic entry — access is sought to a tier, floor, or residence associated with a named individual, is timed to when that individual is present, and pairs with prior grievance or fixation toward them. Intent falls when the access has a verifiable legitimate purpose, when it is undirected wandering with no target concentration, or when it does not recur once the actor is inside.
high_signal_anchors: Target-tier concentration — the elevation is aimed specifically at the tier, floor, suite, or residence associated with the named target rather than general facility access.
Presence-timed entry — the access attempt aligns with windows when the target is predictably present (schedule, event, known routine), indicating the access is a means of reaching the person.

Grievance paired with elevation — the actor has expressed blame, threat, or fixation toward the target AND is observed deceptively acquiring access to the target's environment. The combination is intent-diagnostic in a way neither indicator is alone.
Persistence past the first grant — the actor re-establishes cover to return, maintaining the elevation rather than a single opportunistic entry, suggesting sustained operational purpose.
Selective interest inside — once elevated, the actor moves toward the target's specific space or information rather than behaving consistently with the assumed role.

Escalating access ambition — successive attempts reach for progressively higher or more target-proximate tiers, showing the actor is closing distance to the individual, not satisfied with generic entry.
low_signal_anchors: Verifiable legitimate purpose — a real vendor, contractor, or visitor relationship surfaces on inquiry and the elevation reconciles to authorized business.
Undirected access — the actor entered an elevated tier but showed no concentration on the target's space, associates, or presence windows.
One-time entry without return — access occurred once with no attempt to re-establish cover or come back.
Convenience, not targeting — the elevation reaches an area that is simply easier to enter, not one associated with the named individual.
No grievance or fixation context — the actor has no known hostile attribution toward the target and the access fits ordinary facility traffic.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when deception reliably converts into standing access the actor can act on — weak or unmanned verification, an exploitable insider who sponsors elevation, cover that survives repeated use, and positional reach to the target's tier during windows when the target is present. Opportunity falls when verification actively defeats the pretext, when the sponsoring path is closed or institutionally cleared, or when the target's tier is hardened against the actor's known method; when opportunity appears reduced, whether the reduction is durable or transient matters.
high_signal_anchors: Verification gap exploited — credential challenges, callbacks, or work-order matching are absent, unmanned, or routinely skipped, so the pretext meets no friction.
Standing cover access — the actor holds a role (contractor, vendor, IT support) that grants recurring elevated access without re-challenge; the elevation renews rather than expiring each visit.

Insider connection being exploited — a current or former insider is actively sponsoring the elevation (badges, escorting, cover roles). A dormant connection is potential; the active exploitation is high-signal.
Access-control blind-spot knowledge — the actor knows which entrance, shift, guard, or reception desk performs the least verification and routes elevation through it.

Positional-and-timing reach — the actor's elevated access lands at the target's tier during windows when the target is predictably present, converting access into an actionable opportunity against the person.
Escort exploitation available — an authorized escort relationship the actor can leverage to enter tiers they cannot reach independently remains open and unmonitored.
low_signal_anchors: Verification actively defeated the pretext — callback, ID check, or work-order match caught the elevation at the access point. Durable if the control is standing and enforced; the low-opportunity reading holds unless the actor finds a new method.
Sponsoring path institutionally cleared — an access audit or formal process affirmatively closed the insider or work-order route, not merely failed to find one. High-confidence absence.

Cover structurally terminated — the actor's role, badge, or relationship that enabled elevation has ended (contract closed, insider removed, credential revoked). Durable structural change, not temporary distance.
Challenged and did not adapt — the actor left after a single credential challenge and has not returned with a revised pretext. Transient: may flip back if the actor re-approaches with a new method.

Target tier hardened after detection — the specific floor, suite, or residence tightened verification following the incident; the actor's known method is blocked. Transient unless the hardening is sustained.
Elevation reached a non-target area — the access the actor can obtain does not position them near the target during presence windows; opportunity exists administratively but not against the person.

false_positive_context.criteria: Most access elevations are legitimate — facilities routinely escort vendors to restricted areas, issue temporary badges, and grant urgent-need access on good faith. What separates a benign elevation from a real concern is whether the access reconciles to a verifiable sponsor and work order, whether the identity behind it is transparent and accountable, and whether the tier granted matches an authorized business purpose rather than the actor's convenience.
contexts: Legitimate vendor and contractor access — service providers, IT support, deliveries, and maintenance escorted or badged into restricted tiers under a real, matchable work order or sponsoring contact.
Authorized visitors and guests — clients, interviewees, auditors, and executives from other sites granted elevated access through a valid host who confirms the engagement on callback.
Legitimate urgent-need grants — real emergencies, forgotten-badge employees, and time-pressured deliveries where staff extend access in good faith and the person's identity and purpose check out.

Administrative and provisioning artifacts — temporary badges, re-issued credentials, access-system lag, or role changes that produce tier-mismatch log entries with a routine HR or facilities explanation.

Authorized security testing — sanctioned red-team, physical penetration test, or tailgating awareness exercise conducted under a documented rules-of-engagement with facility leadership's prior knowledge.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Findings correlating with staging-class behaviors elsewhere — the elevated actor observed rehearsing routes to the target, weapon or restricted-item indicators, or timing aligned to the target's presence — warrant immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier, because access elevation is a Mobilization behavior and successful elevation places the actor inside the target's environment. Escalation tier-determination for this tactic's findings depends on three factors: credibility of the elevation per the credibility criteria, breadth across access points or modalities, and persistence over time. A single low-credibility indicator with an available administrative explanation sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility elevation anomaly — a verified sponsor denial, a cloned-credential hit, an unmatched work order at a target-associated tier — sits at the investigation tier. Corroboration across records or access points — two or more elevation anomalies tied to the same actor or credential, or an anomaly paired with prior grievance toward the target — sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating as active mobilization against the individual. Elevations that recur despite implemented verification countermeasures sit at the committed-actor tier and indicate an actor adapting to defeat controls. Multiple lower-priority indicators correlating temporally or across access points may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding warrants in isolation; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered response actions: the monitoring tier triggers audit-trail logging and access-pattern review; the investigation tier triggers actor-identification effort, sponsor and work-order validation, and a protective assessment of the target's exposure at the elevated tier; the elevation tier triggers immediate access revocation, verification hardening at the exploited point, and protective-detail notification; the committed-actor tier triggers a facility-wide credential and escort posture upgrade; confirmed actor identity matching a known threat actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination and immediate protective measures for the target.

tactics.name: Access Elevation
tactics.notes: Gaining higher-tier physical access through deception, social engineering, or credential abuse rather than force. Actor obtains access rights or physical proximity that their actual status does not authorize — vendor badge, escort manipulation, insider assistance. Distinct from Barrier Defeat (TM0302), which uses force.
tactics.cpn_notes: Cloned access credentials, spoofed caller ID, and fabricated digital authorization documents enable access elevation without physical contact. Attackers may use digitally-generated fake work orders or appointment confirmations to pass social engineering checkpoints.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor presents a fabricated or borrowed credential to a guard, receptionist, or escort to gain access above the tier their actual status authorizes

Threat actor exploits an authorized escort relationship to access a tier the threat actor cannot enter independently — vendor escorted into an executive area, contractor accompanied to a restricted server room
Threat actor uses social engineering — pretexted phone calls, urgent-need framing, name-dropping a senior — to convince personnel to grant access not normally extended
Threat actor's claimed sponsoring contact does not exist, is uncontactable, or denies the engagement when verified
Threat actor uses a cloned access credential, fabricated work order, or spoofed appointment confirmation to pass automated or human verification at an access point
Threat actor's access elevation creates an audit anomaly — a badge holder appearing at a tier inconsistent with role, a visitor with no sponsoring record, a contractor with no work-order match

countermeasures.measure: Require sponsoring-contact callback verification for all visitor access at sensitive tiers, with no admission until the sponsoring contact independently confirms the engagement
countermeasures.limitations: Callback verification slows legitimate operations and is often relaxed by reception staff under pressure to admit waiting visitors

countermeasures.measure: Implement work-order matching protocols requiring vendor and contractor visits to align with a pre-recorded order in the maintenance system before access is granted
countermeasures.limitations: Requires disciplined work-order entry that contractors may bypass for emergency calls; maintenance system integration adds operational overhead

countermeasures.measure: Train reception, escort personnel, and sensitive-tier custodians on common social-engineering pretexts including urgent-need framing, senior-name-dropping, and credential-loss claims
countermeasures.limitations: Training fades; staff turnover requires constant refresh. Effectiveness depends on a culture that empowers personnel to challenge senior-appearing requests

countermeasures.measure: Deploy biometric or multi-factor verification at sensitive-tier access points to defeat cloned or borrowed credentials
countermeasures.limitations: Biometric capture has privacy and regulatory implications; cost and friction may be unjustified for lower-sensitivity tiers

response_protocols.trigger: Single Access Elevation indicator detected (sponsoring contact unverifiable, badge tier mismatch, suspected social-engineering attempt)
response_protocols.action: Detain the individual politely if on-site; verify identity through independent channels including direct contact with the named sponsoring person. Notify the threat assessment team within the same business hour. Preserve any physical artifacts including credentials, work orders, and business cards. Pull access logs for review.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Identity cannot be verified OR access elevation connects to other concerning context (prior surveillance, prior cover construction, prior attempted approach).
response_protocols.legal_notes: Detention or extended challenge of an individual carries legal implications; coordinate with legal before any action beyond polite verification. Pretexting at protected sites may itself be unlawful in some jurisdictions. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

response_protocols.trigger: Confirmed access elevation past sensitive-tier controls OR access elevation coupled with capability acquisition or rehearsal indicators
response_protocols.action: Activate emergency response. Initiate sensitive-tier lockdown. Notify law enforcement. Implement enhanced protective posture for the targeted subject. Capture all physical and digital evidence including the threat actor's credentials and the audit trail of the elevation pathway. Brief executive leadership.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Threat actor reaches the targeted subject's tier OR demonstrates means and proximity.
response_protocols.legal_notes: Pretexting and unauthorized access at protected sites may carry independent criminal liability; preserve evidence under chain-of-custody discipline. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

tactics.field_notes: Access Elevation is the threat actor's exploitation of trust — gaining higher-tier physical access through deception, social engineering, or credential abuse rather than force. There's no physical signal in Access Elevation: no broken lock, no climbed fence, no tackled guard. The detection signal is the audit trail: the badge swipe at the wrong tier, the visitor log with a name nobody can verify, the contractor with no matching work order. Access Elevation is constant work for the threat actor because every successful elevation expires when the access window closes; the threat actor is not just gaining access once but maintaining the cover that justifies returning. An investigator catches Access Elevation by treating the audit trail as the primary evidence and validating each elevation against the holder's actual authorization.
observed_contexts: executive protection case where a threat actor presented a stolen contractor badge at reception, was escorted to a senior executive's floor, and was identified only when the escort attempted callback verification post-meeting

domestic protection case where a threat actor used a pretexted urgent-need claim — claiming to be a family member's friend with a delivery — to gain residence access, identified retrospectively through doorbell camera recovery
insider-conspirator case where the threat actor's elevation was sponsored by an insider, with the audit trail showing a series of badge swipes at tiers inconsistent with the contractor role on file

Casework pattern: access elevation through cover-for-action — the threat actor presents in a role that grants higher access than their actual status authorizes — vendor, contractor, visiting executive, IT support, or a social-engineering call to reception that produces a temporary badge — and operates from inside that elevated tier without the friction of credential challenges
facility attack case where the threat actor used a cloned employee badge to bypass automated verification, with the elevation recognized only after post-incident audit-trail analysis

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises when the reported position is corroborated across observation modes, when the static presence persists or recurs rather than being a single fleeting sighting, and when recoverable evidence — CCTV, cross-camera correlation, a trained witness's first-hand account — physically ties a specific actor to a specific vantage point over a specific span. Credibility falls when the sighting is thin, unrepeated, or reported so long after the fact that the duration and the line-of-sight claim cannot be reconstructed, and when the actor's stationary presence was never checked against a mundane reason to be there.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-modal corroboration — the same actor's static presence at a line-of-sight position is captured independently (CCTV plus witness, or physical plus vehicle-plate record) against the same targeted subject within overlapping windows.
Temporal recurrence — the actor holds or returns to the same vantage point across multiple days or nights, not a one-time stop, establishing a pattern rather than a coincidence.

Recoverable positional evidence — timestamped camera footage, cross-camera correlation, or logged vehicle presence that fixes the actor at the vantage point for a measurable duration; does not depend on accurate witness recall.

First-hand trained-witness fidelity — a baseline-aware observer (cashier, doorman, EP detail) directly noticed the actor, and reports position, duration, sightline, and behavior with operational specificity.
Positional specificity — the report names the exact seat, spot, or angle and its line-of-sight to the subject's route, residence, vehicle, or appointment, not a vague 'someone hanging around.'
Source motivation aligned with accuracy — the report comes through a formal protective or security channel from an observer with no stake in the outcome, not an informal tip carrying an agenda.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — single anonymous report of a 'suspicious person sitting there' with no corroboration and no way to re-contact the observer.
Content-specificity weakness — a stationary-presence claim with no stated sightline, duration, or angle that could fit any patron, waiting rider, or resting passerby.
Temporal-pattern weakness — one-time observation of someone stopped at a spot, with no recurrence, no sustained hold, and no follow-through.

Source-motivation misalignment — the reporter has structural reason to cast a stationary person as a threat (custody dispute, neighbor conflict, litigation) and the vantage-point framing may be motivated.
Unrebutted mundane explanation — the position admits a plausible benign reading (a bus stop, a smoke break, a work vehicle) that investigation never ruled out.
Reconstructive memory — the sighting is reported so late that 'he was watching the door' may be retrofitted from knowing an incident occurred, not from what was observed at the time.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when the actor selects and holds a position with tradecraft — a vantage point that pairs sightline with concealment, staging that supports sustained occupation, a pretext or cover that survives scrutiny, and operational alertness that reads as trained watching rather than idle waiting. Capability falls with a conspicuous, exposed, or repeatedly obvious posture, staging inadequate to hold the position, a cover story that collapses on first contact, and behavior that betrays presence rather than masking it.
high_signal_anchors: Concealed-sightline selection — the position is chosen so it simultaneously offers line-of-sight to the subject's route or venue and gives the actor visual cover, reflecting deliberate vantage-point craft.
Sustained-occupation staging — a vehicle, equipment, or supplies positioned to support holding the spot for hours or across nights, indicating the actor planned to remain rather than pass through.

Durable cover for presence — the actor's reason for being stationary (patron, worker, waiting rider) holds up under a witness's or challenger's scrutiny; the presence did not immediately read as anomalous.

Operational alertness under discipline — horizon scanning, watch-checking, or device-monitoring tied to the subject's expected arrival window, executed without drawing attention, consistent with a trained lookout rather than a distracted bystander.

Counter-detection positioning — the actor picks a spot outside camera coverage, varies which vantage point is used across days, or reads defender patrol timing to hold the position when observation is thinnest.

Positional endurance — the actor tolerates a prolonged, uncomfortable static hold (a stairwell, a parked vehicle with no occupant movement, a window seat for hours), demonstrating the committed patience the position demands.
low_signal_anchors: Conspicuous posture — the actor loiters in the open at an obvious sightline, is plainly watching the entrance, and lingers well past any routine reason to be there.
No-concealment repetition — repeated occupation of the same exposed spot with no cover, pretext, or attempt to blend into the location's normal use.
Cover failure on contact — the first time anyone speaks to the actor, the reason for being stationary falls apart or provokes obvious evasion.
Inadequate staging — the actor arrives with nothing to support a sustained hold and has to abandon the position quickly, showing no capacity to maintain it.
Fixed-vantage rigidity — the actor uses one obvious spot with no adaptation, easily patterned and easily displaced by routine activity.
Presence-betraying behavior — fidgeting, pacing, or drawing attention that surfaces the actor to staff or passersby, breaching the concealment a held position requires.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when the stationary presence is unmistakably oriented to the targeted subject — the sightline tracks the subject's route or appointment, the hold coincides with when the subject is expected, and the alertness behavior is timed to the subject's movement rather than ambient. Intent falls when the presence has a verifiable benign purpose, when the position does not actually command the subject's environment, and when the stop is isolated with no orientation to any specific person or window.
high_signal_anchors: Sightline oriented to the subject — the vantage point is specifically angled to the subject's known route, residence, vehicle, or appointment, not a generic view of a public area.
Window alignment — the actor holds the position during the subject's anticipated arrival or departure and disengages when the subject's window passes, coupling presence to the subject's schedule.
Target-timed alertness — scanning, watch-checking, and device-monitoring intensify as the subject's expected appearance approaches, showing the watching is about this subject.
Position-precedes-approach behavior — the actor is seen shifting from the held vantage toward the subject's path or point of arrival, indicating the position is a launch point, not an endpoint.

Recurrence against the same subject — the actor re-establishes the same or a rotated vantage point over successive days against the same subject, signaling operational commitment rather than momentary interest.

Hostile attribution paired with positioning — the actor has expressed grievance, blame, or hostile attribution toward the subject AND is observed holding a concealed line-of-sight position over the subject's environment. The combination is intent-diagnostic in a way neither indicator is alone.
low_signal_anchors: Generic stationary presence — a person stopped at a public spot with no observable orientation to any specific individual, route, or window.
One-time stop without escalation — the actor held a position once, did not return, and no approach or pattern followed.
Verifiable legitimate purpose — a work assignment, appointment, or transit wait surfaces on inquiry and accounts for the stationary presence and its location.
Sightline mismatch — the position's actual view does not command the subject's route or venue; the concern rested on assumed rather than real line-of-sight.
Ambient rather than subject-timed behavior — scanning or waiting continues regardless of whether the subject is present or expected, fitting general people-watching rather than target watching.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the held position actually places the actor within reach of the subject at a moment the subject is predictably present — a commanding sightline or proximity, occupation timed to the subject's window, and an environment offering no friction to the actor remaining. Opportunity falls when defensive posture displaces or blocks the position, when the vantage point does not close the gap to the subject in space or time, and when the subject's own pattern denies the actor an actionable window; where opportunity appears reduced, whether the reduction will hold matters.
high_signal_anchors: Uninterrupted hold — the actor occupies the vantage point without being challenged, moved, or observed by any countermeasure, and the presence continues unimpeded.

Commanding position achieved — the vantage point genuinely delivers the line-of-sight, approach angle, or proximity to the subject that the planned action would require; the position is operationally sufficient, not merely nearby.
Window coincidence — the actor is in position precisely during the subject's predictable arrival, departure, or routine presence, converting the held vantage into an actionable window.
Environmental gap knowledge — the actor holds the position at a time or spot that exploits known patrol gaps, camera blind spots, or thin-coverage windows in the subject's environment.
Positional persistence across the subject's cycle — the actor sustains or re-establishes the vantage point across the subject's recurring schedule, so a window recurs rather than passing once.
Reach from cover — the concealed position keeps the actor close enough to act while remaining unobserved, combining proximity with the protection that makes acting feasible.
low_signal_anchors: Position defeated by hardened posture — protective countermeasures detected and displaced the actor from the vantage point, and the actor's approach was actively blocked. Durable signal: the low-opportunity reading holds unless the actor finds a new position or posture drops.
Institutional denial of the vantage — the location was formally secured, swept, or access-controlled so the commanding position is no longer available, not merely unused. High-confidence reduction.

Structural loss of position access — the actor's pathway to the vantage point ended (venue closed, seat removed, parking restricted, relocation). Distinct from a temporary miss: a durable change in whether the position can be reoccupied.
Displaced without adaptation — the actor left after being challenged or noticed at the spot and did not return or find an alternate vantage. Transient signal: may flip if the actor re-positions.

Sightline or window not closed — the vantage point does not actually reach the subject, or the actor holds it when the subject is never present; distance in space or time remains uncrossed. Transient: may close if the actor adjusts.

Subject's pattern denies a window — the subject varies routine, hardens the venue, or is protectively screened so the held position yields no predictable presence. Transient unless the change is sustained.

false_positive_context.criteria: Sustained static presence at a vantage point looks, on the surface, like ordinary stationary behavior — a patron at a window seat, a driver waiting in a parked car, a rider at a stop, a worker on a break. What separates a benign held position from a threat actor's established position is whether the stationary presence has a verifiable reason to be there, a transparent identity behind it, or institutional accountability that can be checked — and whether its sightline and timing actually orient to a targeted subject.
contexts: Ordinary stationary use of the location — patrons lingering over coffee or work, riders waiting for transit, drivers parked while waiting for a passenger, people resting or on the phone, all with routine reasons to remain in place.

Verified work presence — delivery, rideshare, and service drivers idling between jobs; tradespeople, surveyors, and maintenance staff stationed on assignment; security or facilities personnel holding a post.
Legal or authorized observation — law-enforcement or licensed investigators conducting lawful surveillance from a fixed position; authorized protective or event-security teams holding overwatch.

Personal or community presence — residents, regulars, and neighbors habitually occupying the same spot; someone meeting or waiting for a specific person; a new resident or employee orienting to the area.
Non-threatening attention — fans, photographers, or media staged near a public figure's expected route out of interest rather than hostile intent, invasive but not oriented to harm.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Because Position Establishment is the final precondition before execution, a credible held position that co-occurs with any staging-class signal — a weapon or equipment present, an observed approach rehearsal, or occupation aligned to a known action window — warrants immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier; at this phase the assumption should favor imminence. Escalation tier-determination for this tactic's findings otherwise rests on three factors: credibility of the positional indicator per the credibility criteria, breadth across observation modes, and persistence or recurrence of the hold. A single low-credibility, unrepeated stationary sighting with an available mundane explanation sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility held position with a sightline oriented to the subject and window coincidence sits at the investigation tier — and because this is a Mobilization-phase tactic, that investigation is time-urgent, not deferrable. Cross-modal corroboration — the same actor's commanding position confirmed against the same subject across two or more modes, or recurring across the subject's schedule — sits at the elevation tier and should be treated as an actor who has reached position. A position held or re-established despite implemented countermeasures sits at the committed-actor tier and indicates an actor pressing toward execution. Multiple lower-priority indicators correlating temporally or by sightline may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding warrants; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit, and at this phase composition should resolve upward under uncertainty. Tier-triggered response actions: the monitoring tier triggers logging and cross-camera pattern-detection; the investigation tier triggers urgent actor-identification, subject-notification, and protective-posture review; the elevation tier triggers immediate countermeasure activation and movement of the subject away from the actor's established sightline; the committed-actor tier triggers defensive-posture upgrade and pre-positioned response. Confirmed actor identity matching a known threat actor profile at any tier warrants immediate law-enforcement coordination.

tactics.name: Position Establishment
tactics.notes: Achieving and holding the physical position required to execute the planned action against the subject. Position establishment may be brief (a sniper position held for minutes) or sustained (a surveillance position maintained over days). The position is the final precondition before Phase 3 can begin.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor is observed in a static position at a location offering line-of-sight, approach angle, or proximity to the target — a subject's anticipated arrival, departure, or routine location, or a targeted venue, gathering, or crowd
Threat actor has positioned a vehicle, equipment, or staging materials at the position consistent with sustained occupation rather than transient presence

Threat actor's position is held over a duration inconsistent with normal routine activity at that location — a person at a coffee shop window for three hours, a vehicle in a parking spot with no occupants for an extended period

Threat actor's position is selected for line-of-sight to a known route, residence, vehicle, or appointment of the targeted subject, or to a targeted site, venue, or gathering, with the position itself offering concealment or visual cover
Threat actor's position behavior shows operational alertness — repeated horizon scanning, watch-checking, repeated phone glances, or device-monitoring behavior — inconsistent with passive presence

countermeasures.measure: Conduct surveillance detection sweeps of known approach corridors and vantage points at consistent intervals, particularly during the targeted subject's routine arrival, departure, and known appointment windows
countermeasures.limitations: Sweep schedules may themselves become observable to the threat actor; trained operators are required to distinguish operational alertness from routine waiting

countermeasures.measure: Deploy CCTV coverage of approach angles and likely vantage points associated with the protected environment, with automated alerting for sustained presence beyond a threshold duration
countermeasures.limitations: Sustained-presence thresholds must balance false positives against missing brief positions; coverage gaps in adjacent public space limit effectiveness

countermeasures.measure: Train reception, lobby personnel, parking attendants, and adjacent business staff (coffee shops, retail tenants) on indicators of operationally-alert presence inconsistent with patron behavior
countermeasures.limitations: Awareness fades without reinforcement; adjacent business cooperation requires established relationships and may be subject to staff turnover

countermeasures.measure: Vary the targeted subject's routine timing and route across observable schedule periods to deny the threat actor a stable position-establishment opportunity
countermeasures.limitations: Route variation has operational and personal cost for the targeted subject; sophisticated threat actors infer the variation pattern given enough observations

response_protocols.trigger: Single Position Establishment indicator detected (sustained presence at a vantage point, staged vehicle with no occupant, operationally-alert behavior at proximity to the targeted subject's routine)
response_protocols.action: Document the indicator. Conduct same-business-day verification through additional observation, CCTV review, and cross-camera correlation. Notify the threat assessment team. Activate enhanced surveillance detection at adjacent vantage points. Brief the targeted subject on observed indicator and consider route variation.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Sustained presence confirmed across multiple observations OR position is selected for line-of-sight to the targeted subject's routine.
response_protocols.legal_notes: Observation of an unidentified person in public space generally requires no legal pre-clearance. Investigative escalation carries jurisdiction-specific privacy implications. Document factually. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

response_protocols.trigger: Confirmed Position Establishment with operational alertness OR position coupled with capability acquisition, rehearsal, or pathway-stage progression
response_protocols.action: Convene the threat management team within 24 hours. Conduct full risk assessment. Implement enhanced protective posture including immediate route variation and on-site response capability deployment. Coordinate with law enforcement; sustained position with apparent operational intent is a high-confidence pre-execution signal.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Threat actor identified with means and demonstrates intent to act OR transitions from position to approach.
response_protocols.legal_notes: Pre-execution interruption at Position Establishment carries the highest preventive leverage in the late mobilization window. Document the indicator constellation thoroughly. This guidance does not constitute legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for jurisdiction-specific requirements.

tactics.field_notes: Position Establishment is the final precondition before execution — the threat actor has reached the location, achieved the angle, the proximity, the line-of-sight, and now waits for the final commitment trigger. Everything before this point was movement; everything after is action. The position can be brief (a sniper position held for minutes) or sustained (a surveillance position maintained over days), and the duration shapes detection: brief positions leave little signal, sustained positions create the encounter window where presence becomes observable. The threat actor at this stage is increasingly committed and decreasingly mobile. What an analyst is looking for is the person who has stopped, who has chosen a vantage point, and whose proximity to the targeted subject's environment cannot be explained by routine.
observed_contexts: executive protection case where the threat actor occupied a coffee shop window seat across from the targeted subject's office for three consecutive mornings, identified by the cashier through baseline-awareness training
domestic case where the threat actor staged a vehicle at a vantage point overlooking the targeted subject's residence for multiple nights, recognized through cross-camera correlation in retrospect
active shooter event where the threat actor held a position in a parking garage stairwell with line-of-sight to the building entrance for nearly forty minutes before the kinetic moment
[literature: NTAC-MASS-2021 — pre-attack pattern of static-position observation prior to mass attacks against public spaces]

facility attack where the threat actor's operational alertness behaviors (horizon scanning, watch-checking) were captured on CCTV but not aggregated to a threat assessment trigger until after-action review

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises when the pause is documented as a persistent, recurring presence pattern corroborated across observation modes rather than inferred from a single sighting, and when the actor's continued operational tempo during the physical lull is materially evidenced. Credibility falls when the reading rests on one ambiguous sighting, when the 'pause' is really a gap in collection rather than an observed stand-down, and when a routine reason for the recurring presence was never ruled out.
high_signal_anchors: Recurring-presence corroboration — the same actor placed at the same vantage on multiple days by more than one witness, camera, or log source, establishing the presence as an observed pattern rather than a one-off.

Documented return-after-withdrawal — recoverable evidence (access logs, license-plate reads, camera timestamps) showing the actor left and returned under changed conditions, not a single continuous loiter that admits a mundane read.

Material operational-tempo evidence — recovered communications, procurement records, or search history showing the actor continued target-relevant activity during the physical lull; this survives poor witness recall.

Named first-hand reporting on the standing-down actor — a witness who directly observed the actor waiting, describing vehicle, equipment, posture, timing, and the absence of any completed transaction or errand.
Behavioral specificity of the pause — the actor is tied to a specific target-associated location and a specific vantage on the target, not vaguely 'in the area.'
Aligned reporting source — trained protection detail, patrol, or analyst reporting the anomaly through a formal channel, motivated toward accuracy rather than an informal tip with an agenda.
low_signal_anchors: Single-sighting weakness — one observation of the actor near the environment, with no established recurrence or return pattern to confirm a deliberate pause.
Collection-gap confusion — the 'pause' is an absence of data, not an observed stand-down; the actor may simply be out of view rather than deliberately waiting in place.
Content-specificity weakness — presence described so generically ('a man sitting in a car') that it fits countless benign explanations near the location.
Source-motivation misalignment — reporter has structural reason to read menace into a recurring presence (neighbor dispute, custody conflict, business rivalry).
Unrebutted routine explanation — the recurring presence admits a plausible benign pattern (commuter, rideshare driver, dog-walker) that investigation did not rule out.
Reconstructive memory — the pause is asserted only in hindsight after a separate trigger, with presence details possibly retrofitted to the threat narrative.

capability.criteria: Capability rises with the operational discipline that lets an actor hold position and wait without abandoning the operation — sustained cover maintenance, cached means kept ready, counter-surveillance awareness that drives the timing of returns, and tempo that is managed rather than lost. Capability falls when the standing-down actor is conspicuous, when artifacts decay toward abandonment, when the pause looks like drift rather than a managed risk decision, and when there is no evidence the actor retained the means to resume.
high_signal_anchors: Sustained cover maintenance — the actor keeps a cover identity, pretext, or routine plausible across the full duration of the pause, so repeated presence does not read as anomalous to casual observers.
Ready-state artifact discipline — vehicle staged, equipment cached, or means retained in a condition that indicates the actor can resume quickly; maintenance over time rather than dormancy.

Counter-surveillance-driven timing — returns are timed to changed shift, day-of-week, or security posture, showing the actor reads defender conditions and waits for a favorable window rather than acting blindly.
Tempo management during the lull — target-relevant research or procurement continues at a controlled cadence, indicating the pause is a deliberate hold with the operation still resourced.
Footprint minimization while waiting — the actor varies vantage, rotates vehicles, or spaces returns to reduce the surveillance signature that prolonged presence would otherwise create.

Environmental-trigger literacy — the actor demonstrably tracks external conditions (public attention, enhanced posture, an unrelated similar attack) and calibrates the stand-down to them, evidencing tactical patience.
low_signal_anchors: Conspicuous waiting — the actor loiters at an obvious sightline with no cover for the recurring presence, generating the exact footprint disciplined tradecraft would avoid.
Artifact decay toward abandonment — staged vehicle ticketed and untouched, cache degrading, cover identity lapsed; the state suggests the operation was dropped, not paused.
Undifferentiated returns — the actor reappears with no relationship to changed conditions, indicating routine or compulsion rather than a managed risk decision.
Tempo loss — no target-relevant activity of any kind during the lull; the record is consistent with disengagement rather than a resourced hold.
Cover failure during the pause — the actor's presence was immediately read as out-of-place by observers, showing the discipline needed to hold position is absent.
No evidence of retained means — nothing indicates the actor kept the capability to resume; the pause cannot be distinguished from having stood down permanently.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when the pause is demonstrably tactical rather than terminal — the actor holds position on a specific target, returns as conditions improve, and keeps the operation warm through continued target-directed activity. Intent falls when the recurring presence has a verifiable benign purpose, when returns show no relationship to the target's exposure, and when the lull is indistinguishable from abandonment.
high_signal_anchors: Target-anchored waiting — the pause is spent on or near one named target and a specific target-associated location, not ambient presence in a general area.
Condition-responsive return — the actor resumes proximity when the target's exposure improves or defender posture relaxes, showing the wait is a search for a better window rather than idleness.
Operation kept warm — target research, surveillance updating, or operationally-relevant procurement continues during the physical lull, inconsistent with a routine waiting period.

Patience keyed to hostile conditions — the stand-down aligns with heightened attention or posture around the target and ends when that heat clears, evidencing a deliberate hold rather than a lost trail.
Retention of readiness — means, notes, and cover are preserved through the pause, pointing to intended later use rather than passing presence.

Grievance paired with a maintained hold — the actor has expressed blame or hostile attribution toward the target AND is observed sustaining a positioned pause against target-associated locations; the combination is intent-diagnostic in a way neither indicator is alone.
low_signal_anchors: Verifiable legitimate presence — the recurring proximity resolves to a benign, checkable purpose (commute, employment, residence, service route) on inquiry.
Exposure-blind returns — reappearances track the actor's own schedule and bear no relationship to when the target is present or vulnerable.
No warm-operation evidence — no target-directed activity accompanies the lull; the pattern fits disengagement rather than a tactical hold.
Target ambiguity — presence spans several locations or people without concentrating on one, fitting geographic habit rather than person-targeting.
Indistinguishable-from-abandonment — the presence simply stops with no return, no retained readiness, and no later target-directed behavior.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the standing-down actor is already in position to act the moment the window opens — holding proximity, mastering the target's pattern-of-life through the wait, tracking the specific condition that must change, and keeping means staged within reach. Opportunity falls when defensive friction is what forced the pause, when the actor's positional or access advantage has degraded during the lull, or when the target's posture has durably closed the window the actor is waiting for.
high_signal_anchors: In-position hold — the actor is already physically present at the target's environment and merely waiting, so the transition from pause to action requires no travel or repositioning.

Pattern-of-life mastery accrued through waiting — the extended presence itself yields detailed knowledge of when and where the target is predictably exposed, sharpening the actionable window the actor is waiting for.

Tracked triggering condition — the actor knows precisely which change (shift rotation, posture relaxation, distraction event) opens the window and is monitoring for it, indicating a specific action-window has been identified.
Staged means within reach — vehicle, equipment, or weapon cached near the environment and kept ready, so resumption is immediate once conditions favor it.

Exploited insider or access advantage sustained through the pause — a current relationship, role, or access pathway the actor keeps alive during the lull to know when to resume; dormant connections are only potential.
Environmental window forming — the very trigger the actor waited for is materializing (public-attention distraction, posture normalizing after an event), collapsing the gap between pause and action.
low_signal_anchors: Pause forced by hardened posture — the actor stood down because countermeasures defeated the approach; a durable low-opportunity reading that will not reconstitute without major actor adaptation or a posture change.
Access degraded during the lull — the actor's prior pathway ended over the wait (role terminated, relationship severed, relocation); a structural change distinct from temporary distance.

Positional advantage not held — the pause was spent away from the environment with no staged proximity; resuming requires re-closing distance not yet closed. Transient: may close if the actor commits.
Institutional rule-out of the standing-down actor — formal access or presence audit actively cleared the recurring presence rather than merely failing to find cause; high-confidence absence.
Window durably closed — the target changed pattern-of-life or hardened venues during the pause such that the specific condition the actor was waiting for can no longer occur.
Friction encountered without adaptation — the actor was challenged during a return and did not come back or alter approach; transient signal that may flip if the actor adapts.

false_positive_context.criteria: A person who is simply, benignly present near a location on a recurring basis is the single largest source of false positives for this tactic — a commuter, a resident, a shift worker, or a service provider produces exactly the multi-day, return-after-absence presence pattern that a deliberate operational pause produces. What distinguishes a false positive from a genuine stand-down is whether the recurring presence has a verifiable everyday purpose, a transparent identity behind it, and returns that track the person's own routine rather than the target's exposure or the defender's posture.
contexts: Routine legitimate presence — commuters, residents, shift workers, rideshare and delivery drivers, dog-walkers, and regulars whose schedules naturally place them at the same vantage repeatedly.

Verified professional business — contractors, vendors, surveyors, inspectors, and appraisers with recurring site work; real-estate and construction staging that leaves vehicles or equipment in place over days.
Legal authority — authorized law-enforcement or licensed-investigator surveillance conducting its own extended, intermittent observation with lawful basis.
Personal or community connection — a current or former employee, neighbor, family member, or acquaintance with an ordinary reason to be near the location intermittently.
Genuine abandonment misread as pause — an operation the actor actually dropped, or an unrelated person's forgotten or ticketed vehicle, mistaken for a maintained ready-state hold.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Because an operational pause places a positioned actor one favorable window away from action, findings that correlate with staging-class behaviors elsewhere — cached means confirmed ready, a dry run, or return timing aligning with an identified action window — warrant immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Escalation tier-determination for this tactic's findings depends on three factors: credibility of the presence pattern per the credibility criteria, breadth across observation modes, and persistence over time. A single low-credibility sighting with an available routine explanation sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility recurring presence anchored to a specific target, with any evidence of maintained readiness, sits at the investigation tier. Cross-modal corroboration — recurring presence confirmed across two or more observation modes against the same target, especially paired with continued operational tempo during the lull — sits at the elevation tier and should be treated as a positioned actor in a tactical hold. A pause with documented return-after-withdrawal keyed to changed conditions, or continued target-directed activity through the lull, sits at the committed-actor tier: this is an actor waiting for a window, not one who has disengaged, and it is the tactic's diagnostic high-risk state. Multiple lower-priority indicators correlating temporally or modally may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding warrants in isolation — a caution that matters acutely here, since the defining risk of this tactic is a quiet, low-severity presence pattern that is dangerous precisely in aggregate; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit and should resist down-weighting the pattern for its apparent inactivity. Tier-triggered response actions: the monitoring tier triggers logging and baseline-anomaly detection against the recurring presence; the investigation tier triggers actor identification and mapping of the specific window the actor appears to be waiting for; the elevation tier triggers countermeasure activation and hardening of the target's predictable exposure to deny the awaited window; the committed-actor tier triggers a defensive-posture upgrade and preparation for imminent resumption. Confirmed actor identity matching a known threat-actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination. Finally, treat an unexplained end to the pause with heightened, not reduced, concern: a stand-down that stops without a benign resolution may be an aborted operation or a shift to execution, and the absence of a kinetic event should not be allowed to close the case without after-action review.

tactics.name: Operational Pause
tactics.notes: Deliberate stand-down to allow counter-surveillance conditions to clear, security posture to relax, an environmental opportunity to materialize, or to adapt to changes such as shifts in resource availability or information gathered during Target Development becoming no longer viable. Operational pause is a risk management decision — the actor may choose to wait due to internal or external factors that may not surface until later. Generates cold trails that complicate later investigation.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor maintains observable presence near the target environment over multiple days or weeks without apparent purpose and without proceeding to action

Threat actor's presence pattern shows return-after-withdrawal behavior — leaving the area, then returning at a later time matching changed conditions (different shift, different day-of-week, different security posture)
Threat actor maintains operational artifacts (vehicle staged, equipment cached, cover identity active) over a duration that suggests sustained pause rather than abandonment

Threat actor's communications, financial activity, or online behavior shows continued operational tempo — research on the target, operationally-relevant procurement — inconsistent with a routine waiting period

Threat actor's pause coincides with observable environmental triggers — increased security posture, public attention to the target, news of an unrelated similar attack — indicating tactical patience rather than abandonment

countermeasures.measure: Maintain elevated surveillance detection posture for an extended period after any concerning indicator surfaces; the threat actor's response to detection may be pause rather than abandonment
countermeasures.limitations: Sustained elevated posture has high resource cost; threat assessment teams cannot maintain peak alertness indefinitely without burnout

countermeasures.measure: Track cases through the threat assessment caseload over time rather than closing them prematurely on absence of activity; Operational Pause is one of the most common reasons a case appears to close and then re-emerges
countermeasures.limitations: Caseload size constraints force closure decisions; analyst attention is finite and case re-emergence may not be recognized as the same threat actor without caseload-management discipline

countermeasures.measure: Implement variable security posture across observable schedule periods to deny the threat actor a stable assessment of conditions to wait out
