Academic and research purpose — students and researchers in architecture, structural engineering, urban planning, or historic preservation with legitimate document needs.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Findings correlating with staging-class facility behaviors elsewhere — accelerant or explosive-precursor acquisition, observed dry runs against the site, emplacement of materiel, or alignment with an occupancy or anniversary window — warrant immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Tier-determination for this tactic's findings depends on three factors: credibility of the indicator, breadth across modalities, and persistence over time. A single low-credibility indicator with an available legitimate explanation — a public permit pulled once — sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility indicator with operational specificity about the structure — acquisition of non-public structural drawings paired with weak-point inquiry — sits at the investigation tier. Cross-modal corroboration — grievance plus document acquisition plus technical study against the same site — sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating as coordinated facility target development. Indicators persisting despite implemented document controls sit at the committed-actor tier, suggesting potential entry into mobilization. Multiple lower-priority indicators correlating temporally or modally may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding warrants; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered actions: monitoring triggers logging and pattern-detection; investigation triggers actor-identification and a structural-vulnerability review of the exposed elements; elevation triggers countermeasure activation appropriate to the building's posture; the committed-actor tier triggers a defensive-posture and structural-hardening review; a confirmed actor matching a known threat-actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor obtains floor plans, architectural drawings, or building permits for a specific facility through public permitting portals, FOIA requests, or assessor and code-enforcement records

Threat actor acquires non-public engineering documentation — structural drawings, as-builts, load-bearing and column details — through insider elicitation, contractor channels, or theft rather than public sources
Threat actor studies the facility's utility risers, HVAC pathways, and fire-suppression schematics, focusing on service chokepoints and system-defeat rather than layout

Threat actor demonstrates engineering literacy about the structure, reasoning about load-bearing walls, transfer columns, standoff, and progressive-collapse points where the building would fail catastrophically
Threat actor references structural vulnerabilities of a specific facility in communications, describing where the building is weakest or how it could be brought down

countermeasures.measure: Reduce publicly exposed structural detail — remove or redact full drawing sets, structural sheets, and fire-suppression schematics from permitting portals and FOIA releases where legally and operationally feasible
countermeasures.limitations: Much permit and assessor material is public by law and cannot be withdrawn; redaction raises the cost of research without eliminating access to structural information

countermeasures.measure: Monitor permitting-portal access, FOIA requests, and vendor or contractor record requests for the facility's structural and mechanical drawings, flagging repeated or targeted pulls of sensitive sheets
countermeasures.limitations: Requesters may use cut-outs or public terminals; anonymized and third-party requests defeat attribution, and public-portal downloads may leave no reviewable log

countermeasures.measure: Classify and control sensitive engineering documents — enforce need-to-know distribution, watermark drawing sets, and require secure handling and return by contractors and vendors with access to as-builts and structural plans
countermeasures.limitations: Legitimate projects require broad drawing distribution; controls depend on contractor discipline and cannot recover documents already released into circulation

countermeasures.measure: Conduct a structural vulnerability and progressive-collapse assessment of the facility, hardening standoff, load paths, and utility- and fire-system access to reduce the value of acquired drawings to an attacker
countermeasures.limitations: Structural hardening and standoff improvements are capital-intensive and constrained by existing construction; reduces but cannot eliminate exploitable collapse or system-defeat points

response_protocols.trigger: One or more Structural & Blueprint Study indicators reported (records requests for the facility's drawings, study of risers or fire-suppression schematics, references to structural weak points)
response_protocols.action: Open or update the facility threat case. Conduct a 24-hour preliminary assessment: (a) corroborate the observation, (b) determine which structural documents were exposed and through what channel, (c) review permitting-portal and records-request logs for the facility, (d) brief facility engineering and security leadership on the structural risk picture. Document all sourcing.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Actor identified acquiring non-public engineering documents, OR indicators across other facility tactics surface for the same actor
response_protocols.legal_notes: Monitoring of an identified actor and records-request auditing may implicate privacy, public-records, and anti-stalking statutes that vary by jurisdiction. Consult counsel before active monitoring; document the investigative basis for any action.

response_protocols.trigger: Actor acquires non-public structural documentation or demonstrates engineering literacy about the facility's load paths, standoff, or progressive-collapse points
response_protocols.action: Elevate the case. Convene an engineering-informed vulnerability review of the exposed elements, tighten distribution and monitoring of the affected drawing sets, evaluate interim structural- and system-hardening options, and coordinate with law enforcement given the collapse-relevant nature of the study. Reassess posture on a defined cadence.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Structural study pairs with capability acquisition, dry runs, or a date-certain or occupancy-window signal
response_protocols.legal_notes: Structural-hardening and document-control actions are within facility authority; document the threat basis to support resource requests and to defend proportionality. Coordinate disclosure of vulnerability findings on a need-to-know basis.

tactics.field_notes: Structural study is the tactic where a plot stops being about a place and starts being about a structure. The tell is not that someone has the floor plan — plenty of legitimate people do — but that the interest runs to where the building fails: the load-bearing walls, the transfer columns, the standoff, the riser and fire-suppression chokepoints. Most of the acquisition is lawful and quiet; permits, assessor records, and contractor bid sets are public or semi-public, and a determined actor can assemble a serviceable picture of a structure without ever touching a restricted document. The signal sharpens when public material is supplemented by non-public engineering drawings pulled through an insider or contractor, and when the actor can actually read them — reasoning correctly about collapse mechanics rather than just collecting sheets. That combination, especially paired with a grievance against the place, is what separates a curious records pull from target development.
observed_contexts: actor who filed successive public-records requests for a government building's permit set and structural sheets, then asked a contractor acquaintance about the load-bearing walls
insider case where an employee copied as-built drawings and fire-suppression schematics for a facility outside any work assignment
arson-and-collapse plot in which the actor studied a building's utility risers to identify where a fire would spread fastest and disable suppression
[literature: FEMA-426-2011 / DOD-UFC4010-2018 pattern — structural standoff and progressive-collapse vulnerabilities as target-development focus preceding facility attacks]

tactics.name: Security Posture Assessment
tactics.notes: Mapping and probing of the targeted facility's physical protection system (PPS) to locate where it fails: camera coverage and blind spots, guard-force size, posture, and patrol timing, access-control type, alarm and lock systems, standoff distance, and response-force timing. Includes deliberate low-level probing — testing a door, attempting a tailgate, inducing a false alarm — to measure detection and reaction. Distinct from Physical Reconnaissance (TF0103), which cases the site itself, and from Structural & Blueprint Study (TF0104), which reads the building's construction. It is also distinct from Surveillance Detection (TF0110): 0110 is the actor defeating observation of the actor, while 0105 catalogs the defenders' system and its gaps. The object here is the protective system's weaknesses, not evading the defenders' gaze.
tactics.cpn_notes: Security-posture assessment is increasingly informed by public and semi-public sources before any physical probe — vendor case studies naming a facility's access-control or camera platform, procurement and bid records exposing alarm and guard-service contracts, installer reviews, and social posts by staff or visitors that reveal patrol routines, badge types, and camera placement.

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises with corroboration across modalities, persistence over time, and recoverable evidence that the actor is cataloging the facility's protective system rather than passing through it. Credibility falls when the source, the content, or the temporal pattern is thin, and when a plausible legitimate interest in the security posture — a vendor, an auditor, a curious patron — was never ruled out.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-modal corroboration — probing behavior at the site, questions to staff about security, and saved notes on cameras or guards against the same facility within overlapping timeframes.
Temporal persistence — repeated attention to the facility's countermeasures observed across weeks, not a single pass.
Material evidence — recovered diagrams of camera arcs, annotated guard-patrol timings, or notes on alarm and lock types that physically tie the actor to the named site's PPS.
First-hand witness fidelity — a named guard or employee who observed the actor testing a door, tailgating, or timing a patrol, reported with resolution on the act, context, and timing.
Behavioral specificity — the actor mapped specific detection gaps (a named blind spot, a shift-change window) rather than expressing vague security curiosity.
Source motivation aligned with accuracy — a trained security officer reporting through a formal channel, not an informal tip with a competing agenda.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — single anonymous report of someone 'looking at the cameras,' reporter cannot be re-contacted.
Content-specificity weakness — a vague observation that a person seemed interested in security, fitting many ordinary visitors.
Temporal-pattern weakness — one-time glance at a camera or door with no follow-through.
Source-motivation misalignment — reporter has a structural reason to embellish (labor dispute, rivalry with a contractor, litigation over the guard service).
Unrebutted legitimate explanation — the interest in the posture admits a benign reading (security vendor, insurance inspector, new employee) that investigation did not exclude.
Reconstructive memory — reporting delay long enough that a mundane act near an entrance may be retrofitted to a probing narrative.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when engagement with the facility's protective system shows operational discipline — covert observation of coverage and timing, acquisition of non-public security information, durable pretexts for probing, and the technical literacy to read a PPS and reason about its gaps. Capability falls with conspicuous behavior, OSINT-only reach, and probes that fail on first contact.
high_signal_anchors: Covert observation tradecraft — patrol timing and camera arcs recorded from concealment or across varied vantage points, no obvious return pattern.
Multi-modal coordination — physical probing, elicitation of staff, and research into the security vendor coordinated across overlapping timeframes.

Restricted-material acquisition — the actor obtains non-public PPS information such as camera-placement diagrams, guard-post orders, alarm-zone maps, or access-control specifications for the facility.
Pretext durability — cover stories for probing (delivery driver, prospective vendor, lost visitor) survive guard scrutiny during a challenge.
Graduated probing discipline — low-level tests (a rattled door, a brief tailgate, a triggered sensor) staged to measure reaction while preserving deniability and avoiding commitment.
Demonstrated technical literacy — the actor interprets what is observed, distinguishing real detection from deterrent signage and reasoning about response-force timing and blind spots.
low_signal_anchors: Conspicuous posture — openly staring at cameras, pacing entrances, lingering at a guard post past any plausible purpose.
No-concealment repetition — repeated probing with no pretext or concealment.
Pretext failure on initial contact — a guard immediately recognized the probe as unusual and the actor had no fallback.
OSINT-only reach — all posture knowledge is from public vendor pages or reviews; no operational reach beyond the browser.
Single-modality engagement — only watching or only asking; no coordination across probing methods.
Reaction-provoking clumsiness — the actor triggered alarms or challenges without any apparent measurement objective, breaching operational discipline about exposure.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when engagement with the protective system progresses from broad interest toward gap-specific detail, when the actor retains what is learned, and when probing is paired with stated grievance against the facility or what it represents. Intent falls with generic security curiosity, encounters that do not escalate, and a verifiable benign purpose.
high_signal_anchors: Behavioral progression broad-to-narrow — an observable funnel from general security interest to gap-specific measurement of the facility's detection and response.
Countermeasure-specific behavior — attention concentrates on where the PPS fails: a specific blind spot, a shift-change gap, an unmonitored door, a slow response window.
Operational specificity in probing or inquiry — testing which doors are alarmed, timing how long a guard takes to respond, asking after-hours coverage or camera recording retention.
Sustained attention to defender posture — the actor tracks the facility's countermeasures over time and adapts probing as posture changes.
Retention of acquired detail — guard timings logged, blind spots mapped, alarm behavior noted and organized, suggesting later operational use.

Hostile attribution paired with probing — the actor has expressed grievance toward the facility AND is observed probing its protective system; the combination is intent-diagnostic in a way no single indicator captures.
low_signal_anchors: Generic-interest behavior — broad curiosity about security in general, not pinned to defeating a specific facility's system.
One-time encounter without escalation — a single door test or camera glance with no follow-through or pattern.
Verifiable legitimate purpose — a security-vendor, audit, inspection, or new-employee relationship surfaces and checks out.
No retention behavior — posture observed casually but not recorded or organized.
Target ambiguity — attention to several sites' security without narrowing to one facility's gaps.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the actor can exploit knowledge of the protective system — combining mastery of patrol and coverage patterns, awareness of detection gaps, exploited insider access to security detail, and the positional ability to reach the site during its weak windows. Opportunity falls with defensive friction not adapted to, distance not closed, or a hardened posture that blocks the actor's known probing; when opportunity appears reduced, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: No defensive friction encountered — probing continues unimpeded; tests go undetected or unaddressed despite the facility's posture.
PPS pattern-of-life mastery — the actor reliably knows patrol timing, shift changes, camera coverage arcs, and the site's low-security periods. The informational dimension of opportunity.
Detection-gap knowledge — the actor knows specific camera blind spots, unalarmed doors, standoff weaknesses, or the true response-force timing for the facility.

Insider connection being exploited — an identified guard, contractor, or security-vendor relationship the actor is actively leveraging for post orders, alarm-zone maps, or access. Dormant connections are potential, not realized; the exploitation pattern is what is high-signal.
Geographic-temporal proximity — the actor lives or works near the facility and is present during the windows its posture is weakest.
Direct facility access — the actor has unsupervised access through a legitimate role, able to test doors and sensors without challenge.
low_signal_anchors: Approach defeated by hardened posture — the facility's countermeasures actively caught and stopped the probing. Durable signal: sticky unless the actor materially adapts or the posture drops.
Institutional rule-out of insider access — access audits or process actively cleared the security-detail exposure, not merely failed to find it.
Structural access degradation — the actor's prior access pathway terminated (role ended, contract lapsed, relocation).
Defensive friction encountered without adaptation — the actor left after a guard challenge and did not return or adapt the probe. Transient: may flip if the actor adapts.
Geographic distance not closed — the actor is remote and probing requires a major travel investment not yet made.
Facility posture change created barriers — randomized patrols, closed blind spots, or new detection blocks the actor's known probing methods; transient unless sustained.

false_positive_context.criteria: Many legitimate activities resemble security-posture assessment on the surface — a licensed penetration tester probing doors looks similar to an actor measuring reaction; a security-system salesperson studying camera placement looks similar to reconnaissance of the PPS. What distinguishes a false positive is whether the underlying interest has a verifiable legitimate purpose, a transparent identity behind it, or institutional accountability that can be checked.
contexts: Authorized security work — licensed vulnerability assessors and penetration testers under contract; security integrators, alarm and camera technicians, and locksmiths on service calls; guard-force supervisors auditing their own posts.

Legal authority — authorized law-enforcement activity with proper basis; fire marshals and code inspectors checking egress, alarms, and life-safety systems; regulators auditing physical-security compliance.
Verified professional purpose — insurance risk engineers, loss-prevention staff, and corporate security assessing their own or a client's facility with site-visit business.
Personal or community connection — employees and vendors familiar with routine security procedures; visitors who notice a propped door or a camera without intent.
Non-threatening attention — hobbyists and enthusiasts of access-control or CCTV technology, and photographers whose interest in a building incidentally captures its security features.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Findings correlating with staging-class facility behaviors elsewhere — accelerant or explosive-precursor acquisition, observed dry runs against the site, emplacement of materiel, or alignment with an occupancy or anniversary window — warrant immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Tier-determination for this tactic's findings depends on three factors: credibility of the indicator, breadth across modalities, and persistence over time. A single low-credibility indicator with an available legitimate explanation — one door glance, one camera photograph — sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility indicator with operational specificity about the facility's detection gaps or response timing sits at the investigation tier. Cross-modal corroboration — grievance plus probing plus insider elicitation against the same site — sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating as coordinated facility target development. Probing that persists despite implemented countermeasures, or that adapts to posture changes, sits at the committed-actor tier, suggesting potential entry into mobilization. Multiple lower-priority indicators correlating temporally or modally may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding warrants; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered actions: monitoring triggers logging and pattern-detection across security incidents; investigation triggers actor-identification and a facility-vulnerability assessment; elevation triggers countermeasure activation and PPS hardening appropriate to the probed gaps; the committed-actor tier triggers a defensive-posture upgrade; a confirmed actor matching a known threat-actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor covertly maps camera coverage and blind spots at the targeted facility — noting field of view, mounting height, recording versus deterrent devices, and unmonitored approaches
Threat actor observes and records the guard force — headcount, armament, posture, and patrol timing — identifying shift changes and low-coverage windows

Threat actor identifies the access-control, alarm, and lock systems in use — badge and reader type, alarm zones, sensor placement, and after-hours recording behavior — through observation, elicitation, or vendor and procurement records

Threat actor measures response-force timing and standoff — clocking how long guards or police take to reach a point, mapping standoff distance and vehicle approach, and timing the interval between a stimulus and a reaction

Threat actor conducts deliberate low-level probing to measure detection and reaction — testing a door, attempting a tailgate, inducing a false alarm, or breaching a boundary to see who responds and how fast

countermeasures.measure: Conduct authorized red-team and vulnerability assessments of the facility's own PPS to find the same camera blind spots, unalarmed doors, patrol gaps, and response-timing weaknesses an actor would probe, and remediate them
countermeasures.limitations: A point-in-time assessment captures the posture as tested; gaps reopen as equipment ages, staffing changes, or procedures drift, so single assessments decay without a recurring cadence

countermeasures.measure: Instrument for probing detection — treat repeated door tests, tailgate attempts, false alarms, and boundary breaches as intelligence events, correlate them across access logs and cameras, and investigate patterns rather than clearing each in isolation
countermeasures.limitations: Low-level probes are individually mundane and easily dismissed as nuisance alarms; correlation depends on retention, disciplined logging, and analysts empowered to connect events across shifts

countermeasures.measure: Randomize and vary the observable posture — patrol routes and timing, shift changes, and response drills — so an actor cannot reliably map coverage windows or response intervals from repeated observation
countermeasures.limitations: Randomization raises the cost of pattern mapping but cannot conceal fixed infrastructure (camera mounts, door hardware, standoff); determined observation over time still recovers averages

countermeasures.measure: Close and layer detection — overlap camera fields to eliminate blind spots, alarm previously unmonitored doors, and add defense-in-depth so no single observed gap defeats the whole system
countermeasures.limitations: Coverage upgrades are capital-intensive and slow to field; new equipment introduces its own configuration gaps and requires trained monitoring to convert detection into response

response_protocols.trigger: One or more Security Posture Assessment indicators reported — observed camera or guard mapping, elicitation about alarms and access control, response-timing measurement, or a low-level probe (door test, tailgate, induced false alarm)
response_protocols.action: Open or update the facility threat case. Conduct a 24-hour preliminary assessment: (a) corroborate the observation against access logs and camera footage, (b) review the digital and vendor footprint of any identified actor, (c) assess whether the probed gap is real and remediable, (d) brief facility security leadership and adjust posture over the probed weakness. Document all sourcing.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Probing persists or adapts after a countermeasure change, OR the actor is identified with apparent means and proximity, OR indicators across other facility tactics surface for the same actor
response_protocols.legal_notes: Monitoring of an identified actor may implicate privacy and anti-stalking statutes that vary by jurisdiction. Detaining or questioning a suspected prober raises trespass and false-imprisonment exposure; consult counsel and document the investigative basis before action.

response_protocols.trigger: A pattern of repeated low-level probes (recurring door tests, tailgate attempts, or false alarms) against the same facility, with or without a named individual actor
response_protocols.action: Treat the probing pattern as active target development. Correlate the events across shifts and systems, close or alarm the tested gap, randomize the observable posture over the affected window, run a response drill against the measured interval, and coordinate with local law enforcement on suspicious-activity patrol emphasis. Reassess after remediation.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Probing resolves to a specific actor, or the tested gap aligns with an occupancy or anniversary window
response_protocols.legal_notes: Posture changes are within facility authority; document the threat basis to support resource requests and to defend proportionality. Preserve access logs and footage of probes as potential evidence per retention policy.

tactics.field_notes: Posture assessment is the tactic where an actor stops studying the place and starts studying its guardians. The tell is not interest in the building but interest in the system that protects it — where the cameras don't reach, when the guard is elsewhere, how long help takes to arrive. Passive mapping (camera arcs, patrol timing) is nearly invisible and looks like waiting; the covert version scores higher precisely because detectability is low. Active probing is louder — a tested door, a tailgate, a tripped sensor — and each probe is individually forgivable as a nuisance, which is exactly why they slip past. The discipline that catches this is treating probes as intelligence: logging them, correlating them across shifts, and asking not 'did we clear it' but 'is someone measuring us.' A single false alarm is noise; a pattern of them against one facility is reconnaissance.
observed_contexts: actor timing guard patrols and photographing camera mounts across several unhurried visits before a planned forced entry
series of after-hours door tests and one induced fire-alarm evacuation, later assessed as response-timing measurement rather than nuisance
insider-adjacent case where a former contractor elicited badge-reader type and alarm-zone layout from current staff
[literature: SANDIA-GARCIA-VAPPS-2006 / DHS-ISC-RMP-2021 pattern — adversary path analysis and PPS gap-mapping preceding facility intrusion]

tactics.name: Capability Acquisition
tactics.notes: Obtaining the physical means to attack a chosen facility — accelerants and ignition sources, explosive precursors or components, breaching and forced-entry tools, a vehicle suitable for ramming, protective equipment, or the funds to procure them. Distinct from Structural & Blueprint Study and Site Profiling (which acquire information about the place) and from Network Development (which assembles the people). The acquisition logic here is about materiel: securing the objects and money that convert a plan against the site into a deliverable method. Because a method reveals itself in what is bought, an incendiary or explosive acquisition against a facility carries more signal than a plan alone.
tactics.cpn_notes: Capability acquisition is increasingly mediated online — marketplaces and hobbyist suppliers, cryptocurrency and stored-value payment rails, and shipping to drop addresses let an actor assemble accelerants, precursors, components, tools, or protective equipment for a facility attack with reduced face-to-face exposure, though purchase and financial records create a durable detection surface.

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises with corroboration across modalities, persistence over time, and recoverable evidence — receipts, shipping records, recovered materiel, or first-hand reports — that the actor is assembling attack means rather than pursuing a legitimate use. Credibility falls when the source, the content, or the temporal pattern is thin, and when a plausible lawful purpose for the acquisition was never ruled out.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-modal corroboration — grievance statements, facility research, and materiel acquisition against the same site within overlapping timeframes.
Temporal persistence — acquisition observed across multiple purchases or sessions, not a single ambiguous buy.
Material evidence — receipts, shipping confirmations, financial records, or recovered items that physically tie the actor to attack-relevant materiel.
First-hand witness fidelity — a named witness who saw or was told of the acquisition and its intended use; high-resolution reporting of the item, quantity, and timing.
Behavioral specificity — the actor acquired items in a combination or quantity inconsistent with any stated benign use.
Source motivation aligned with accuracy — a merchant, shipper, or trained reporter through a formal channel rather than an informal tip with a competing agenda.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — single anonymous tip, reporter cannot be re-contacted.
Content-specificity weakness — a report of a common, dual-use purchase that fits countless lawful uses.
Temporal-pattern weakness — one isolated acquisition with no supporting behavior.
Source-motivation misalignment — reporter has a structural reason to embellish (personal dispute, commercial rivalry, litigation).
Unrebutted legitimate explanation — the purchase admits a benign reading (trade, hobby, agriculture, ordinary transport) that investigation did not exclude.
Reconstructive memory — reporting delay long enough that an ordinary purchase may be retrofitted to a threat narrative.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when acquisition shows operational discipline and technical literacy — sourcing controlled or component materials through cut-outs, aggregating items into a working method, testing what was acquired, and defeating point-of-sale scrutiny. Capability falls with conspicuous single purchases, reliance on items that require expertise the actor lacks, and acquisition that fails at the counter.
high_signal_anchors: Covert sourcing tradecraft — split purchases across vendors, cash or stored-value payment, drop addresses, or cut-outs to avoid a traceable pattern.
Multi-modal coordination — procurement, facility research, and rehearsal coordinated across overlapping timeframes.
Component aggregation — the actor obtains items that individually appear benign but combine into a deliverable method against the site.
Demonstrated technical literacy — the actor selects correct components and handles or stores them in a manner indicating working knowledge.
Counter-scrutiny behavior — the actor spreads quantities below reporting thresholds or fabricates a use to satisfy a merchant.
Observed testing — the actor is reported to have trialed an accelerant, ignition source, tool, or device consistent with the acquired materiel.
low_signal_anchors: Conspicuous single purchase — one open, attributable buy of a flagged item with no concealment.
Capability-expertise gap — acquired items require handling or assembly skill the actor has no evidence of possessing.
Point-of-sale failure — a merchant refused the sale or flagged it, and the actor did not adapt.
Dual-use-only reach — everything acquired is freely available and individually innocuous, with no aggregation.
Single-modality engagement — acquisition with no accompanying research, rehearsal, or planning behavior.
Abandoned acquisition — the actor sought materiel but did not complete or retain it.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when acquisition progresses from general interest toward a specific method matched to the facility, when materiel is retained and organized, and when procurement is paired with stated grievance against the place or its function. Intent falls with isolated dual-use purchases, acquisitions that do not escalate, and a verifiable lawful purpose.
high_signal_anchors: Behavioral progression broad-to-narrow — an observable funnel from browsing methods to acquiring a specific one keyed to the site's vulnerabilities.
Method-facility fit — the materiel acquired matches the facility's exposure (accelerants for a combustible structure, a vehicle for a crowded approach, breaching tools for a hardened entry).
Acquisition of a mass method — obtaining incendiary or explosive means whose only coherent purpose against a populated building is mass harm.
Retention and organization — materiel stored, staged, or inventoried rather than consumed, suggesting reservation for later use.
Threshold-evading pattern — deliberate under-buying or vendor-splitting that indicates awareness the purchase is illegitimate.

Hostile attribution paired with acquisition — the actor has expressed grievance toward the facility AND is observed acquiring attack means; the combination is intent-diagnostic in a way no single indicator captures.
low_signal_anchors: Generic dual-use purchase — a common item with broad lawful application and no facility linkage.
One-time acquisition without escalation — a purchase surfaced but no follow-through or pattern.
Verifiable legitimate purpose — occupational, agricultural, hobby, or transport need surfaces and checks out.
No retention behavior — items acquired and consumed for an evident ordinary use, not stored.
Method ambiguity — acquisitions do not converge on any coherent method against a specific site.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the actor can convert acquired materiel into action against the facility — combining the means with access to the site, funds sufficient to complete procurement, and freedom from regulatory or supply friction. Opportunity falls when controls interdict the acquisition, funds fall short, or supply is denied; when opportunity appears reduced, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: Unobstructed supply — the actor sources attack means without encountering regulatory reporting, merchant refusal, or licensing barriers.
Financial sufficiency — the actor has, raises, or reallocates funds adequate to complete acquisition of the intended method.
Materiel-to-site pairing — the acquired means is compatible with a known access pathway or vulnerable window at the facility.
Insider or vendor channel exploited — an identified employee, contractor, or supplier relationship the actor is actively leveraging to obtain restricted items or bypass controls.
Storage and staging capacity — the actor controls a location to hold and assemble materiel near enough to the site to act.
Regulatory blind spot — the actor exploits a jurisdiction, threshold, or channel where the specific materiel draws no scrutiny.
low_signal_anchors: Acquisition interdicted by controls — a reporting requirement, watch-list, or merchant refusal actively blocked the purchase. Durable signal: sticky unless the actor finds an alternate channel.
Institutional rule-out of supply access — a supplier audit or process actively cleared the possibility of restricted-item diversion, not merely failed to find it.
Financial shortfall — the actor lacks the funds to complete the intended method and has no observed means to raise them.
Supply friction encountered without adaptation — the actor abandoned an acquisition after a barrier and did not seek another route. Transient: may flip if the actor adapts.
No storage or staging capacity — the actor has nowhere to hold or assemble materiel, and physical action would require capacity not yet obtained.
Regulatory tightening created barriers — new licensing, tracking, or threshold controls block the actor's known sourcing method; transient unless the actor is blocked durably.

false_positive_context.criteria: Many lawful activities resemble capability acquisition on the surface — a farmer buying fertilizer, a contractor buying pry bars and saws, a hobbyist buying solvents, or a commuter buying a used van all look similar to an actor assembling attack means. What distinguishes a false positive is whether the acquisition has a verifiable lawful purpose, a transparent identity and accountable channel behind it, and a quantity and combination consistent with that stated use.
contexts: Occupational and trade purpose — contractors, tradespeople, demolition and locksmith professionals, farmers, and industrial buyers acquiring tools, accelerants, or bulk chemicals for licensed or documented business use.

Legal authority — authorized law-enforcement or military procurement; licensed dealers and explosives handlers operating under permit; security professionals acquiring breaching or protective equipment for authorized assessments.
Hobby and recreation — reloaders, pyrotechnics hobbyists, chemists, machinists, and off-road or motorsport enthusiasts making ordinary supply purchases within normal quantities.
Ordinary consumer transactions — routine vehicle purchase or rental, household fuel and solvent purchases, and common hardware acquisition for home use.
Agricultural and institutional supply — farms, schools, laboratories, and facilities buying regulated inputs through established, documented supply relationships.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Findings correlating with staging-class facility behaviors elsewhere — observed dry runs against the site, emplacement or staging of materiel, alignment with an occupancy or anniversary window, or leakage naming the target — warrant immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier, because acquisition places a deliverable method within reach. Tier-determination for this tactic's findings depends on three factors: credibility of the indicator, breadth across modalities, and persistence over time. A single low-credibility indicator with an available legitimate explanation sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility indicator — acquisition of a mass method, or a combination and quantity inconsistent with any stated use — sits at the investigation tier. Cross-modal corroboration — grievance plus facility research plus materiel acquisition against the same site — sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating as coordinated facility target development approaching mobilization. Acquisition persisting despite interdiction attempts, or completed acquisition of an attack method, sits at the committed-actor tier. Multiple lower-priority indicators correlating temporally or modally may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding warrants; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered actions: monitoring triggers logging and pattern-detection; investigation triggers actor-identification, financial and supply-record review, and a facility-vulnerability assessment matched to the acquired method; elevation triggers countermeasure activation and supplier liaison; the committed-actor tier triggers a defensive-posture upgrade and law-enforcement coordination. A confirmed actor matching a known threat-actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor acquires accelerants, fuels, or ignition sources in quantities or combinations inconsistent with any stated use, consistent with preparing an incendiary attack on the facility
Threat actor acquires explosive precursor materials or device components, or obtains them in split purchases across vendors, in a pattern inconsistent with any documented lawful use
Threat actor acquires breaching, cutting, or forced-entry tools matched to the facility's access barriers, beyond any evident occupational or household need
Threat actor acquires or modifies a vehicle suitable for ramming or for transporting materiel to the site, or obtains protective equipment such as body armor inconsistent with a stated lawful role
Threat actor raises, reallocates, or liquidates funds to finance procurement of attack means, evidenced by unusual withdrawals, asset sales, or payments to suppliers of relevant materiel

countermeasures.measure: Establish supplier and merchant liaison for the facility's threat picture — brief local retailers, chemical and agricultural suppliers, tool and equipment vendors, and shippers on suspicious-acquisition indicators and reporting channels
countermeasures.limitations: Depends on merchant participation and recall; online and out-of-area sourcing bypasses local liaison, and split purchases below thresholds may draw no attention

countermeasures.measure: Integrate suspicious-purchase and financial-anomaly reporting into the facility threat case, correlating acquisition indicators from records reviews with grievance and reconnaissance signals against the site
countermeasures.limitations: Financial and purchase records are access-restricted and require legal basis; cash, cryptocurrency, and third-party procurement reduce visibility

countermeasures.measure: Harden the facility against the acquired-method classes most credible for the site — vehicle standoff and barriers, ignition-source and combustible-load controls, and reinforced access points — informed by a method-matched vulnerability assessment
countermeasures.limitations: Capital-intensive and slow; hardening one method class can displace an actor to another, and legacy structures constrain retrofits

countermeasures.measure: Control internal access to restricted materiel and equipment — inventory and reconcile fuels, chemicals, tools, keys, and credentials, and audit vendor and contractor supply channels to prevent diversion toward an attack on the site
countermeasures.limitations: Addresses insider diversion but not external procurement; effective only with sustained reconciliation discipline and cannot cover items sourced outside the facility

response_protocols.trigger: One or more Capability Acquisition indicators reported (suspicious purchase of accelerants, precursors, components, tools, or a ramming-suitable vehicle; financial anomalies consistent with procuring attack means against the facility)
response_protocols.action: Open or update the facility threat case. Conduct a preliminary assessment: (a) corroborate the acquisition report and identify the actor, (b) review available purchase, shipping, and financial records under proper legal basis, (c) determine which attack method the materiel enables and match it to the facility's vulnerabilities, (d) brief facility security leadership on posture against that method. Document all sourcing and the investigative basis.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Acquisition of a mass method (incendiary or explosive means) confirmed, OR acquisition indicators surface alongside reconnaissance, grievance, or staging signals for the same actor and site
response_protocols.legal_notes: Access to financial, purchase, and shipping records is governed by privacy statutes and typically requires legal process; regulated-precursor reporting regimes vary by jurisdiction. Consult counsel before records review; document the investigative basis for any action.

response_protocols.trigger: Confirmed acquisition of an attack method against the facility, or acquisition persisting despite interdiction attempts, indicating a committed actor with means in hand
response_protocols.action: Initiate urgent law-enforcement coordination and elevate facility posture against the confirmed method for the exposure window: activate method-matched countermeasures (vehicle standoff, combustible-load controls, access hardening), increase visible presence, brief staff on reporting, and prepare for a potential mobilization-phase transition. Reassess continuously until the materiel is accounted for or the threat is resolved.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Materiel observed staged near the site, or leakage indicating imminent use
response_protocols.legal_notes: Interdiction of materiel and any seizure require law-enforcement authority and proper process; posture changes are within facility authority but should be documented to support resource requests and defend proportionality.

tactics.field_notes: Acquisition is where a plan against a place becomes a method you can point at. The tell is rarely a single flagged purchase — it is combination and quantity that no stated use explains: accelerants beyond any household need, components bought a few at a time across vendors, breaching tools matched to a specific door, a van bought cash by someone with no evident use for it. The method reveals itself in the cart, which is why an incendiary or explosive acquisition carries more weight than words alone. The hard part is that almost every item is dual-use and lawful in isolation; the signal lives in the pattern, the pairing with a named site, and the money moving to pay for it. Financial and purchase records raise detectability sharply once you have legal basis to look — but cash, crypto, and third-party sourcing pull it back down.
observed_contexts: arson case in which the actor accumulated accelerants and ignition sources over several weeks before an incendiary attack on a targeted clinic
plot in which explosive precursors were sourced in split purchases across multiple vendors to stay below any single reporting threshold
actor who bought a used cargo vehicle for cash and acquired breaching tools matched to a hardened facility entrance
[literature: ATF-EIR-2024 / NFPA-INTENTIONAL-2021 pattern — precursor and accelerant acquisition preceding incendiary and explosive attacks on facilities]

tactics.name: Network Development
tactics.notes: Assembly of the human system required to attack a facility: recruiting or coordinating co-conspirators, cultivating or tasking an insider (employee, contractor, or vendor) with access to the targeted site, dividing operational roles, moving a group from shared grievance toward operational tasking (radicalization-to-action within a cell), or soliciting material and financial support for the operation. Distinct from Capability Acquisition (which obtains materiel and things) and from Cover Construction (which fabricates a false identity or legend for the actor). The organizing distinction is that Network Development builds a network of real people bound to the operation; insider cultivation lives here, whereas a fabricated vendor identity the actor invents for themselves lives in Cover Construction.
tactics.cpn_notes: Recruitment and coordination are increasingly conducted online — closed forums, encrypted group chats, and ideological communities that let an actor find co-conspirators, solicit support, and task participants against a facility without ever meeting in person. Insider cultivation likewise migrates to direct messaging, where grooming of an employee or contractor can proceed under the cover of ordinary contact.

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises with corroboration across modalities, persistence over time, and recoverable evidence that the actor is binding other people to an operation against a specific facility. Credibility falls when the source, the content, or the temporal pattern is thin, and when a plausible legitimate association among the people involved was never ruled out.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-modal corroboration — recruitment communications, financial movement, and observed meetings against the same facility within overlapping timeframes.
Temporal persistence — a coordinated relationship built and tasked across weeks to months, not a single conversation.
Material evidence — recovered messages, membership records, tasking notes, or transfers that physically tie named participants to the operation and the named site.
First-hand witness fidelity — a named witness who was solicited, or who heard the actor task others against the facility, with high-resolution reporting of the request, context, and timing.
Behavioral specificity — the actor named the specific facility and assigned specific roles rather than voicing a vague collective grievance.
Source motivation aligned with accuracy — a trained reporter or a solicited participant reporting through a formal channel, not an informal tip with a competing agenda.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — single anonymous tip about a 'group,' reporter cannot be re-contacted.
Content-specificity weakness — a vague claim of shared anger that could describe any grievance community.
Temporal-pattern weakness — one-time expression of collective sentiment with no follow-through or tasking.
Source-motivation misalignment — reporter has a structural reason to embellish (falling-out with the group, custody or employment dispute, informant incentive).
Unrebutted legitimate explanation — the association admits a benign reading (activist organizing, union activity, faith community, family or business tie) that investigation did not exclude.
Reconstructive memory — reporting delay long enough that ordinary contacts may be retrofitted into a conspiracy narrative.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when the actor's network-building shows operational discipline — covert recruitment, compartmented tasking, durable control over an insider, and the reach to convert grievance into assigned roles. Capability falls with conspicuous solicitation, a network that exists only as talk, and cultivation attempts that collapse on first refusal.
high_signal_anchors: Covert recruitment tradecraft — vetting of prospects, compartmentation, use of cut-outs, no open solicitation trail.
Multi-modal coordination — online recruitment, financial support, and in-person meetings coordinated across overlapping timeframes.
Insider control being established — the actor is grooming or coercing a named employee, contractor, or vendor into providing access or intelligence, and the relationship is deepening.
Role differentiation — the actor assigns and sustains distinct functions (finance, access, logistics, action) across participants, evidencing operational structure.
Counter-detection behaviors — the network migrates to encrypted channels, adopts operational security norms, and screens new members.
Demonstrated mobilizing reach — the actor productively converts expressed grievance in a group into tasked, willing participants rather than mere sympathizers.
low_signal_anchors: Conspicuous solicitation — open recruitment posts, public calls for co-conspirators, no vetting or concealment.
Talk-only network — expressed collective intent with no tasking, no roles, and no material or financial movement.
Cultivation failure on initial contact — the approached insider refused, reported the contact, or disengaged.
Sympathizer-only reach — the actor has an audience that agrees but none who have accepted operational tasking.
Single-modality engagement — only online chatter or only a lone associate; no coordination across people or channels.
Direct-exposure attempts — the actor solicited widely and indiscriminately, breaching operational discipline about exposure.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when a network progresses from shared grievance toward operationally specific tasking against a facility, when the actor retains membership and tasking structure, and when recruitment is paired with stated hostility toward the place or what it represents. Intent falls with generic collective sentiment, associations that do not escalate, and a verifiable benign purpose for the group.
high_signal_anchors: Behavioral progression grievance-to-tasking — an observable funnel from shared anger to assigned operational roles against the specific facility.
Facility-specific coordination — the network's attention concentrates on the named site and its specific access, occupancy, or insider pathways.
Operational specificity in solicitation or tasking — asking a participant to obtain access credentials, map after-hours entry, provide staffing schedules, or move funds for the operation.
Sustained cultivation of an insider — the actor tracks and deepens a relationship with facility-access personnel over time, not a one-time ask.
Retention of network structure — membership lists, tasking records, and support arrangements maintained, suggesting durable operational use.

Hostile attribution paired with recruitment — the actor has expressed grievance toward the facility or its function AND is observed building or tasking a network against it; the combination is intent-diagnostic in a way no single indicator captures.
low_signal_anchors: Generic collective-grievance behavior — broad shared anger at an institution or cause, not converted into tasking against a specific site.
One-time association without escalation — contact surfaced but produced no roles, tasking, or follow-through.
Verifiable legitimate purpose — activist, union, faith, employment, or family relationship surfaces and checks out.
No retention behavior — loose contacts that are not organized, tasked, or sustained.
Target ambiguity — collective animus expressed without narrowing to one facility as the objective.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the network can act on its reach — combining an exploited insider at the facility, participants positioned near the site, control over material and financial support, and the coordination to converge on a vulnerable window. Opportunity falls with cultivation defeated by vetting, participants unable to reach the site, or a hardened personnel-security posture that blocks the network's known access pathway; when opportunity appears reduced, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: Insider access being exploited — an identified employee, contractor, or vendor the network is actively leveraging for site intelligence or entry. Dormant sympathy is potential; the exploitation pattern is what is high-signal.
Positioned participants — members live or work near the facility and can be present during its vulnerable windows.
Coordinated convergence capacity — the network can assemble multiple participants at the site at a chosen time without detection.
Material and financial support secured — funds, safe locations, or logistics are in hand to sustain the operation.
No vetting friction encountered — cultivation of insiders or recruitment of members continues unimpeded despite the facility's personnel-security posture.
Facility pattern-of-life mastery through insiders — the network reliably knows occupancy cycles, service windows, and low-security periods via a cultivated source.
low_signal_anchors: Cultivation defeated by vetting — the facility's personnel-security controls detected and blocked the insider approach. Durable signal: sticky unless the actor materially adapts or the posture drops.
Institutional rule-out of insider compromise — access audits or investigations actively cleared the possibility, not merely failed to find it.
Structural access degradation — the cultivated insider's role ended, contract lapsed, or the participant relocated, terminating the access pathway.
Recruitment friction encountered without adaptation — approached prospects refused and the actor did not adapt or seek others. Transient: may flip if the actor adapts.
Geographic dispersion not closed — participants are remote from the facility and convergence requires a major travel investment not yet made.
Personnel-security change created barriers — expanded background screening, insider-threat monitoring, or reporting culture blocks the network's known approach; transient unless sustained.

false_positive_context.criteria: Many legitimate associations resemble network development on the surface — an activist group organizing a protest looks similar to a cell tasking an operation; an employee befriended by an outsider looks similar to an insider being cultivated. What distinguishes a false positive is whether the association has a verifiable legitimate purpose, transparent identities behind it, or institutional accountability that can be checked.
contexts: Protected collective activity — lawful activists, organizers, union members, and advocacy groups coordinating protest, boycott, or civil action; shared grievance expressed without operational tasking against a site.
Faith and community organizing — congregations, mutual-aid networks, and community groups with legitimate collective purpose and familiarity with a facility.
Ordinary workplace and vendor relationships — employees, contractors, and vendors with legitimate access and normal social contact, including new acquaintances that are entirely benign.
Family and personal networks — relatives, friends, and personal associates whose contact has an ordinary explanation.
Legal authority and research — journalists, researchers, and organizers studying a movement or building sources, and authorized investigators mapping networks on lawful bases.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Findings correlating with staging-class facility behaviors elsewhere — insider provision of access credentials or non-public site information, accelerant or explosive-precursor acquisition by a network member, observed dry runs against the site, or alignment with an occupancy or anniversary window — warrant immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Tier-determination for this tactic's findings depends on three factors: credibility of the indicator, breadth across modalities, and persistence over time. A single low-credibility indicator with an available legitimate explanation (an association that admits a benign reading) sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility indicator with operational specificity — a named insider being tasked, a solicited participant given a role against the facility — sits at the investigation tier. Cross-modal corroboration — grievance plus recruitment plus financial or logistical support against the same site — sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating as coordinated facility network development. Indicators persisting despite implemented countermeasures sit at the committed-actor tier, suggesting potential entry into mobilization. Multiple lower-priority indicators correlating temporally or modally may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding warrants; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered actions: monitoring triggers logging and pattern-detection; investigation triggers actor-and-associate identification, an insider-access review, and a facility-vulnerability assessment; elevation triggers countermeasure activation appropriate to the site's posture; the committed-actor tier triggers a personnel-security and defensive-posture upgrade; a confirmed network matching a known threat-actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor recruits or solicits co-conspirators for an operation against a specific facility, seeking others willing to participate in planning or action
Threat actor cultivates, grooms, or coerces an employee, contractor, or vendor with access to the targeted facility to provide site intelligence or access
Threat actor moves a group from shared grievance toward operational tasking against the facility, in language or planning that reveals a mass or public-venue objective
Threat actor solicits material or financial support for a facility operation, requesting funds, safe locations, transport, or logistical assistance from supporters
Threat actor divides operational roles among participants, assigning distinct functions such as finance, access, logistics, or action against the facility

countermeasures.measure: Establish an insider-threat program for the facility — access reviews, behavioral reporting channels, and monitoring for anomalous access by employees, contractors, and vendors with site privileges
countermeasures.limitations: A cultivated insider may act within authorized access, producing no anomaly; programs depend on reporting culture and can generate friction or false positives against ordinary employee behavior

countermeasures.measure: Conduct OSINT monitoring of extremist and grievance communities for recruitment, tasking, and solicitation of support directed at the facility or its class
countermeasures.limitations: Encrypted and closed channels are not visible; recruitment and tasking often migrate to private messaging before a facility is named, limiting coverage

countermeasures.measure: Strengthen vendor and contractor vetting and access governance — background screening, least-privilege access, escorted entry, and periodic re-verification of third-party personnel
countermeasures.limitations: Vetting screens at onboarding but may miss cultivation that occurs after access is granted; determined coercion of an already-cleared insider is not prevented by initial screening

countermeasures.measure: Maintain liaison with fusion centers and law enforcement to receive early warning of network-building and recruitment trends targeting the facility class, and to refer credible conspiracies
countermeasures.limitations: Depends on reporting discipline and fusion-center throughput; category-level warning may not identify the specific network or facility, and referral thresholds are legally constrained

response_protocols.trigger: One or more Network Development indicators reported (recruitment of co-conspirators, insider cultivation, role tasking, or solicitation of support against the facility)
response_protocols.action: Open or update the facility threat case. Conduct a 24-hour preliminary assessment: (a) corroborate the observation, (b) identify the actor and associates and map the emerging network, (c) review insider-access exposure for any implicated employee, contractor, or vendor, (d) brief facility security and personnel-security leadership on posture. Document all sourcing.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: A named insider is confirmed to be cooperating, OR the network shows means and proximity to the facility, OR indicators across other facility tactics surface for the same network
response_protocols.legal_notes: Investigating associations implicates freedom-of-association and privacy protections; lawful collective activity must not be treated as conspiracy. Consult counsel before mapping networks or monitoring an identified insider, and document the investigative basis for any action.

response_protocols.trigger: Credible indication that an insider with facility access is being cultivated or has agreed to provide access or intelligence
response_protocols.action: Initiate a coordinated insider-response: review and, where warranted, restrict the individual's access under established policy; preserve access logs and communications lawfully; conduct an insider-access review of affected systems and entry points; and coordinate with law enforcement on any criminal conspiracy. Protect the process against wrongful adverse action pending assessment.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: The insider has provided access, credentials, or non-public site information, OR staging-class behaviors by the network are observed
response_protocols.legal_notes: Employment action against a suspected insider implicates labor law, due-process, and defamation exposure; access restriction and investigation must follow established policy and counsel guidance. Preserve evidence lawfully and document proportionality.

tactics.field_notes: Network development is usually inferred from who the actor is talking to and what they are asking others to do, not from a single declaration. The clearest early tell is grievance moving from 'I' to 'we' — a group converting shared anger into assigned roles against a place — paired with a specific ask: money, a safe location, or, most consequentially, an employee or contractor being worked to hand over access. Insider cultivation is the covert core of this tactic and the hardest to see, because it can proceed entirely inside ordinary contact and the insider may act within authorized access. The hard part is that most network signal is association, which looks like protected activism, union organizing, or faith community until it pairs with tasking, funding, or an insider approach that reveals the operation underneath.
observed_contexts: ideologically motivated actor recruiting co-conspirators in a closed online forum before assigning roles for an attack on a symbolic facility
clinic-targeting case where an actor cultivated a contractor for after-hours access and staffing schedules over several weeks
aggrieved group whose shared grievance was converted into tasked operational roles, with one member soliciting funds and a safe location
[literature: CTC-INFRATERROR-2026 / NITTF-GUIDE-2017 pattern — online recruitment and insider cultivation preceding coordinated attacks on facilities and infrastructure]

tactics.name: Cover Construction
tactics.notes: Construction of a false legitimacy that lets the threat actor reach or approach the targeted facility without triggering staff scrutiny. The actor fabricates a role that belongs at the site — vendor, contractor, delivery driver, inspector, utility technician, prospective tenant — and builds the supporting apparatus: credentials, uniforms, business cards, work orders, a registered shell business, or actual cover employment with the facility or one of its vendors. Distinct from Network Development (TF0107), which assembles a network of real co-conspirators or cultivates a genuine insider; here the actor manufactures identity and pretext for themselves. Distinct from Physical Reconnaissance (TF0103), which is on-site observation; cover construction is the fabricated legitimacy that makes such access, or later execution, defensible under challenge. The diagnostic question is not what the actor observed but what identity the actor assembled to be present.
tactics.cpn_notes: Cover construction is increasingly assembled online — registered shell entities with a web presence, fabricated business profiles and reviews, purchased or forged uniforms and badge stock, template invoices and work orders, and cover employment histories seeded across professional-networking platforms — so that a pretext survives a defender's quick open-source verification before any physical approach to the facility.

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises with corroboration across modalities, persistence over time, and recoverable evidence that the actor is assembling a false identity or pretext keyed to a specific facility. Credibility falls when the source, the content, or the temporal pattern is thin, and when a legitimate explanation for the identity work — a real new business, a real job, a real vendor relationship — was never ruled out.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-modal corroboration — a fabricated role, acquired credentials or uniform, and physical proximity to the same facility observed within overlapping timeframes.
Temporal persistence — identity-building activity that develops across weeks to months rather than a single anomalous encounter.
Material evidence — recovered forged badges, printed work orders, template invoices, uniform purchases, or shell-entity registration documents tied to the named site.
First-hand witness fidelity — a named staff member who can describe the actor presenting a cover role, with high-resolution reporting of the claimed identity, context, and timing.
Behavioral specificity — the fabricated role maps precisely onto a legitimate access need at the specific facility (its actual waste hauler, its badge format, its permit language).
Source motivation aligned with accuracy — trained reporter through a formal channel, not an informal tip from a party with a competing interest in the vendor or contract.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — single anonymous tip that the actor 'claimed to work for someone,' with no re-contactable reporter.
Content-specificity weakness — a vague impression that an identity felt off, unattached to any observable credential, uniform, or role claim.
Temporal-pattern weakness — one-time presentation of a role with no recurrence and no supporting apparatus.
Source-motivation misalignment — reporter has a structural reason to embellish (a vendor rivalry, an employment dispute, a competing bid).
Unrebutted legitimate explanation — the actor's business, credential, or employment admits a benign reading that investigation did not exclude.
Reconstructive memory — reporting delay long enough that a routine vendor visit is retrofitted into a suspicious-cover narrative.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when the constructed cover shows operational discipline — a durable legend that withstands verification, authentic-looking credentials and uniforms, a registered and web-corroborated shell entity, and role knowledge deep enough to answer staff questions in character. Capability falls with a thin pretext, obviously counterfeit props, and a story that collapses on the first pointed question.
high_signal_anchors: Legend durability — the cover story holds under staff scrutiny and survives a call-back or open-source check because supporting artifacts corroborate it.
Credential authenticity — badges, uniforms, vehicle markings, or high-visibility attire that match the facility's real vendors closely enough to pass casual verification.
Shell-entity depth — a registered business with a functioning web presence, phone tree, and paperwork rather than a bare verbal claim.
Role fluency — the actor answers in-character questions about the claimed trade, scope of work, or dispatch chain without breaking cover.
Verification-resistant sourcing — the actor anticipates and pre-empts the defender's checks (a live callback number, a plausible dispatcher, a work order matching the facility's ticketing language).
Operational compartmentation — the cover identity is kept separate from the actor's true identity, with cut-outs and no traceable overlap.
low_signal_anchors: Pretext failure on initial contact — staff immediately recognized the role claim as inconsistent with the site's real vendors or schedule.
Counterfeit-prop obviousness — a uniform, badge, or work order that is visibly wrong (wrong logo, wrong badge format, wrong paperwork).
Shallow legend — a verbal claim with no supporting business, paperwork, or callable reference.
Role-knowledge gap — the actor could not answer basic in-character questions about the claimed trade or dispatch.
Identity bleed-through — the cover identity is trivially linkable to the actor's real name, vehicle, or phone.
Single-artifact reliance — one prop (a hi-vis vest alone) stands in for a full legend and does not survive a question.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when the identity work is purpose-built for unescorted or after-hours reach into a specific facility, when the cover is retained and refined toward an access objective, and when pretext-building is paired with stated grievance against the site or what it represents. Intent falls with generic entrepreneurial or job-seeking activity, one-off role claims that do not escalate, and a verifiable benign purpose.
high_signal_anchors: Access-directed tailoring — the fabricated role is specifically the one that grants unescorted, delivery-dock, mechanical-space, or after-hours reach at the named facility.
Behavioral progression broad-to-narrow — an observable funnel from a generic cover idea to a facility-specific legend with matching credentials.
Retention and refinement — the actor maintains, updates, and rehearses the cover across time rather than discarding it after one use.
Operational specificity in the pretext — the cover is keyed to real site details (its actual service windows, its real prime contractor, its badge or permit format).
Probing under cover — the actor uses the assumed role to ask about access, keys, alarm codes, occupancy, or restricted spaces beyond what the claimed work requires.

Hostile attribution paired with cover-building — the actor has expressed grievance toward the facility or its function AND is observed constructing a pretext to reach it; the combination is intent-diagnostic in a way no single indicator captures.
low_signal_anchors: Generic-business behavior — legitimate new-venture or job-search activity not pinned to reaching a specific site as an objective.
One-time role claim without escalation — a cover presented once with no follow-through, refinement, or access-seeking.
Verifiable legitimate purpose — a real business registration, real employment, or real vendor contract surfaces and checks out.
No retention behavior — a pretext improvised in the moment and not maintained or reused.
Scope-appropriate inquiry — questions asked under the role stay within what the claimed work plausibly requires.
Target ambiguity — a cover usable at many sites with no narrowing to one facility.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the constructed cover actually converts to reach — matching an existing access channel the facility trusts, exploiting a vendor or delivery relationship, and giving the actor unescorted or recurring presence. Opportunity falls with verification friction the cover cannot beat, access channels the pretext does not fit, or a hardened credentialing posture; when opportunity appears reduced, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: Cover accepted without friction — the actor's role claim is honored and access granted despite the facility's posture.
Access-channel match — the fabricated role maps onto a real, trusted channel (the site's actual courier, waste, HVAC, or inspection relationship) that receives routine unescorted access.
Recurring-presence conversion — the cover yields repeat visits that normalize the actor's presence and reduce later scrutiny.
Credential acceptance — badges, uniforms, or work orders are taken at face value at the point of entry without call-back verification.
Vendor- or dock-window mastery — the actor knows and uses the facility's delivery, service, and low-staffing windows where cover challenges are least likely.
Cover employment secured — the actor holds an actual role with the facility or one of its vendors that confers legitimate standing and access.
low_signal_anchors: Cover defeated by verification — the facility's vendor-verification or call-back process actively blocked the pretext. Durable signal: sticky unless the actor materially upgrades the legend.
Institutional credential rigor — badge issuance, escort rules, or contractor pre-registration actively cleared the access path, not merely failed to catch it.
Access-channel mismatch — no trusted channel corresponds to the claimed role, so the cover offers no reach.
Verification friction encountered without adaptation — the actor left after being challenged and did not return or refine the legend. Transient: may flip if the actor adapts.
Structural access degradation — a prior cover pathway terminated (contract not renewed, badge deactivated, vendor relationship ended).
Posture change created barriers — new call-back verification, escort requirements, or vendor allow-listing blocks the actor's known cover; transient unless sustained.

false_positive_context.criteria: Most facility access by outside identities is legitimate — real vendors, contractors, couriers, inspectors, and new hires present exactly the credentials and roles a fabricated cover imitates. What distinguishes a false positive is whether the identity has a verifiable business behind it, a transparent and callable chain of accountability, and a role that matches a real, expected relationship with the facility.
contexts: Verified vendor and contractor activity — real service technicians, couriers, waste haulers, and trades on scheduled or dispatched work with callable dispatchers and matching work orders.
Legal and official authority — genuine inspectors, code officials, utility personnel, and law-enforcement or licensed-investigator activity with proper basis and verifiable credentials.
Legitimate new business — a newly registered local business genuinely soliciting or servicing the facility, with a real web presence and accountability.
Bona fide employment — real new hires, temps, and vendor staff onboarding into roles that confer legitimate access.
Prospective commercial relationships — real prospective tenants, buyers, or vendors on due-diligence or bid visits, transparently identified.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Findings correlating with staging-class facility behaviors elsewhere — accelerant or explosive-precursor acquisition, observed dry runs against the site, exploitation of the cover for unescorted access to restricted spaces, or alignment with an occupancy or anniversary window — warrant immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Tier-determination for this tactic's findings depends on three factors: credibility of the indicator, breadth across modalities, and persistence over time. A single low-credibility indicator with an available legitimate explanation — a plausible vendor with checkable paperwork — sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility indicator with a facility-specific fabricated role and matching credentials sits at the investigation tier. Cross-modal corroboration — a false identity plus acquired credentials plus proximity against the same site — sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating as coordinated facility target development. A cover that persists or is upgraded despite implemented verification countermeasures sits at the committed-actor tier, suggesting potential entry into mobilization. Multiple lower-priority indicators correlating temporally or modally may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding warrants; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit.
