Tier-triggered actions: monitoring triggers logging and vendor-claim pattern-detection; investigation triggers actor-identification and vendor-verification of the claimed role; elevation triggers credentialing and escort-posture activation appropriate to the site; the committed-actor tier triggers an access-control-posture upgrade; a confirmed actor matching a known threat-actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor fabricates a vendor, contractor, delivery, or inspector identity for the specific facility — presenting business cards, work orders, or a role claim that matches a legitimate access need at the site
Threat actor obtains or forges credentials, badge stock, uniforms, high-visibility attire, or vehicle markings that imitate the facility's real vendors or service providers

Threat actor stages a shell business or seeds a fabricated employment history — registering an entity, standing up a web presence and callback number, or planting a cover role across professional-networking platforms to corroborate a pretext

Threat actor rehearses and tests a pretext narrative against facility staff — probing with the cover story during an initial contact and asking about access, keys, occupancy, or restricted spaces beyond what the claimed role requires
Threat actor takes cover employment with the facility or one of its vendors, securing a genuine role that confers legitimate standing, recurring presence, and unescorted access to the site

countermeasures.measure: Implement vendor and contractor verification at the point of access — call-back confirmation to a known dispatcher, work-order matching against the facility's own ticketing system, and a pre-registered vendor allow-list rather than face-value acceptance of credentials
countermeasures.limitations: Effective only if staff follow the process under time pressure; a well-built legend with a live callback number and matching paperwork can still pass, and social pressure at a busy dock erodes discipline

countermeasures.measure: Issue tamper-resistant, facility-controlled credentials and visibly distinct visitor and contractor badges, and train reception and dock staff to recognize the site's authentic badge, uniform, and vehicle-marking standards
countermeasures.limitations: Raises the cost of forging credentials but cannot stop an actor who secures genuine cover employment or matches an approved vendor closely enough; badge standards leak to determined observers

countermeasures.measure: Train frontline staff in pretext-awareness and challenge culture — recognizing role claims that do not match the schedule, questions that exceed the claimed scope of work, and the authority to verify or escort without fear of offending a legitimate vendor
countermeasures.limitations: Depends on staff confidence and turnover; awareness fades without reinforcement, and a durable, well-rehearsed legend is specifically designed to survive a routine challenge

countermeasures.measure: Apply pre-employment and pre-engagement screening for roles and vendor relationships that confer site access — identity verification, reference and history checks, and periodic re-verification of standing vendor accounts
countermeasures.limitations: Screening reduces but does not eliminate cover employment; seeded histories and shell entities can pass a check, and screening reaches employees and prime vendors more reliably than subcontractors and temporary labor

response_protocols.trigger: One or more Cover Construction indicators reported (a fabricated vendor or contractor role at the site, acquired or forged credentials or uniforms, a suspicious pretext presented to staff)
response_protocols.action: Open or update the facility threat case. Conduct a 24-hour preliminary assessment: (a) corroborate the observation, (b) verify the claimed identity and role against known vendors, dispatch records, and public registration, (c) review credential and access logs for the presented identity, (d) brief reception, dock, and security staff to challenge and escort the role on any return. Document all sourcing.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: The cover is confirmed fabricated and tied to an identified actor with apparent means and proximity, OR indicators across other facility tactics surface for the same actor or identity
response_protocols.legal_notes: Verifying a vendor claim and denying access are within facility authority; investigation of an identified actor may implicate privacy and employment statutes that vary by jurisdiction. Consult counsel before adverse action against a cover employee; document the investigative basis.

response_protocols.trigger: Verification reveals a shell entity, seeded employment history, or cover role with no legitimate business behind it, keyed to accessing the facility
response_protocols.action: Elevate access-control posture: suspend the identity's credentials, add it to a watch and deny list, require escort for the associated vendor category, and re-verify standing vendor accounts. Preserve credential artifacts and logs as evidence and coordinate with law enforcement on the fabricated-identity findings.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: The cover resolves to a known threat-actor profile or is paired with staging behaviors from other facility tactics
response_protocols.legal_notes: Adverse action against a cover employee or vendor should be counsel-reviewed to manage wrongful-termination and defamation exposure; preserve evidence and document the threat basis to support proportionality.

tactics.field_notes: Cover construction is rarely caught in the building of it; it is inferred when a role claim does not survive a call-back or when a badge, uniform, or work order is a shade wrong. The clearest early tell is a pretext that maps too neatly onto the exact access an attacker would want — the after-hours HVAC tech, the courier with dock access, the inspector who needs the mechanical room — paired with questions that run past the claimed job. Good cover is cheap to fake at the prop level (a vest and a clipboard) and expensive to fake at the verification level (a live dispatcher and a matching ticket), so the single most productive defense is a habit of call-back verification against the facility's own records rather than face-value acceptance. The hard case is cover employment: an actor in a genuine role has legitimate standing, and the tell shifts from credential-checking to scope-of-behavior — access sought beyond the job.
observed_contexts: actor presenting as a utility or fire-inspection technician with a plausible clipboard and hi-vis vest to gain unescorted interior access to a facility
registration of a shell contracting entity with a thin web presence used to solicit a walkthrough of a targeted site
actor taking a genuine janitorial or delivery role with a facility vendor to obtain recurring after-hours access
[literature: CISA-SOFTTARGETS-2019 / DOD-UFC4022-2017 pattern — impersonation of trusted vendors and inspectors to defeat access control at soft targets]

tactics.name: Pathway / Escalation Indicators
tactics.notes: Behavioral leakage and mobilization-to-action signals that reveal a threat actor is moving from planning toward execution against a specific place. This tactic aggregates the pathway-to-violence warning behaviors (Meloy/NTAC) as they attach to a facility target: leakage that names or alludes to the site, countdown and time-imminence language, last-resort and final-act framing, farewell and legacy behaviors, and an observable acceleration — an energy burst or end-of-planning surge — in activity directed at the place. Distinct from Facility Target Selection (TF0101), which is the discrete grievance-and-selection logic about which building; this tactic is the trajectory signal that the actor has fixed on a site and is closing the distance to action. It is the latest-pathway, most mobilization-adjacent tactic in target development, and its indicators are read as tempo and direction, not as isolated recon acts.
tactics.cpn_notes: Leakage increasingly appears in online posts — public and semi-public social media, forum threads, livestreams, and messaging channels where actors telegraph time-imminence, last-resort framing, and farewell behaviors before a facility attack. Countdown language and legacy tokens (manifestos, final videos) are often uploaded or scheduled in the hours to days before action, making open-source monitoring a primary early-warning surface for this tactic.

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises with corroboration across modalities, persistence and progression over time, and recoverable evidence that the leakage attaches to a specific place and a specific timeframe rather than a diffuse mood. Credibility falls when the source, the content, or the temporal pattern is thin, and when the leakage admits a plausible non-mobilization reading (venting, dark humor, crisis distress) that assessment did not rule out.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-modal corroboration — leakage statements, farewell behaviors, and an observed acceleration toward the same facility within overlapping timeframes.
Temporal progression — the warning behaviors sharpen and compress over time rather than surfacing as a single remark, consistent with movement along a pathway.

Material evidence — saved final statements, drafted manifestos, scheduled posts, recovered messages, or given-away possessions that physically anchor the leakage to a named site and a near-term horizon.
First-hand witness fidelity — a named witness who heard the actor speak of a last act against the place, with high-resolution reporting of the words, context, and timing.
Behavioral specificity — the leakage names or unmistakably alludes to the specific facility and to imminence ('soon,' 'before Friday,' 'you'll see') rather than a vague category.
Source motivation aligned with accuracy — trained reporter through a formal channel, not an informal tip with a competing agenda.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — single anonymous tip, reporter cannot be re-contacted.
Content-specificity weakness — generalized despair or hostility with no place and no timeframe attached.
Temporal-pattern weakness — one-time remark with no progression, acceleration, or follow-through.
Source-motivation misalignment — reporter has a structural reason to embellish (dispute with the actor, custody or employment conflict, litigation).
Unrebutted non-mobilization explanation — the statement admits a benign reading (venting, gallows humor, acute mental-health crisis without directed intent) that assessment did not exclude.
Reconstructive memory — reporting delay long enough that farewell or countdown language may be retrofitted to a threat narrative after the fact.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when the mobilization signals are backed by evidence the actor can actually reach and act against the place — leakage paired with acquired means, demonstrated site knowledge, durable pretexts, and the discipline to compress planning into action. Capability falls when the leakage is expressive only, unaccompanied by any operational substrate, or contradicted by the actor's demonstrated inability to close the distance to the facility.
high_signal_anchors: Leakage paired with acquisition — final-act framing surfaces alongside evidence the actor has obtained a weapon, accelerant, or breaching means for the site.
Demonstrated site knowledge behind the countdown — the imminence language references real occupancy windows, access points, or timing the actor could only know from prior reconnaissance.
Operational compression — the actor collapses remaining planning steps quickly and purposefully, indicating rehearsal or a settled method rather than ideation.
Pretext and staging readiness — cover, transport, or approach arrangements for the facility appear finalized alongside the leakage.
Counter-surveillance and OPSEC around the final phase — the actor sanitizes devices, closes accounts, or times posts to limit interdiction while still telegraphing intent.
Demonstrated capacity to execute the stated timeline — the actor has the mobility, health, and resources to act within the horizon the countdown names.
low_signal_anchors: Expressive-only leakage — statements of finality with no acquired means, no site knowledge, and no observable preparation.
Timeline the actor cannot meet — countdown language attached to a facility the actor has no demonstrated way to reach.
No-concealment repetition — repeated final-act talk broadcast openly with no OPSEC, more consistent with distress signaling than a disciplined final phase.
Contradicted preparation — the actor speaks of imminence while visibly lacking transport, means, or access that has not been arranged.
Single-modality signal — leakage in words only, with no behavioral acceleration or material substrate to corroborate capability.
Help-seeking embedded in the leakage — the statement is directed at obtaining intervention or rescue rather than concealing an operational plan.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when the warning behaviors converge and sharpen toward a settled decision to act against the place — leakage naming the site, last-resort framing that forecloses alternatives, farewell and legacy behaviors that presuppose an endpoint, and an acceleration that treats the attack as decided rather than considered. Intent falls with diffuse distress, statements that do not progress, and a verifiable resolution of the underlying crisis.
high_signal_anchors: Behavioral convergence toward finality — multiple pathway signals (leakage, last-resort framing, farewell behavior, acceleration) align on the same place within a compressed window.
Site-anchored leakage — the mobilization language names or unmistakably alludes to the specific facility as the endpoint, not a generalized grievance.
Last-resort and foreclosure framing — 'nothing left to lose,' 'the only way,' 'they left me no choice' — language that treats action as decided and alternatives as exhausted.
Legacy and farewell behaviors — drafting a manifesto or final message, giving away possessions, settling affairs, recording a legacy statement tied to the act against the place.
Energy-burst acceleration — an observable surge from deliberate planning tempo into end-of-planning activity directed at the site, the pathway's late-stage tell.
Time-imminence signaling — countdown or date-certain language ('soon,' 'before the anniversary,' 'this week') that fixes action to a near horizon against the facility.
low_signal_anchors: Diffuse distress without direction — despair or hopelessness not attached to a place or an act against it.
Non-progressing statements — final-sounding language surfaces once and does not sharpen, converge, or accelerate.
Verifiable crisis resolution — the precipitating grievance or stressor is addressed and the leakage subsides without displacement to a new target.
Target ambiguity under the countdown — imminence language with no place named and no facility narrowed from among candidates.
Ambivalence and approach-avoidance — the actor voices finality but repeatedly defers, negotiates, or signals for intervention rather than committing.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the actor can act on the settled intent within the horizon the leakage names — combining proximity to the place, mastery of its vulnerable windows, an unobstructed approach, and a countdown timed to a real occupancy or anniversary window. Opportunity falls with defensive friction not adapted to, distance not closed within the stated timeline, or a hardened posture that blocks the actor's known methods; when opportunity narrows, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: Countdown aligned to a real window — the imminence language coincides with a known occupancy peak, event, or symbolic anniversary at the facility.
No defensive friction encountered — the actor's late-phase movement toward the site continues unimpeded despite the facility's posture.
Facility pattern-of-life mastery — the actor reliably knows the site's occupancy cycles and low-security periods and the countdown maps onto them.
Geographic-temporal proximity — the actor is near the facility and present during its vulnerable windows within the horizon the leakage names.
Direct or arranged access — the actor holds, or has staged, a means of reaching the site (role, credential, insider relationship, transport) as the countdown runs.
Interdiction-resistant timing — the actor has scheduled or compressed the final phase to reduce the window in which defenders could act.
low_signal_anchors: Approach defeated by hardened posture — the facility's countermeasures actively blocked the actor's late-phase movement. Durable signal: sticky unless the actor materially adapts or the posture drops.
Timeline outruns reach — the countdown names a horizon the actor cannot meet given unclosed distance to the site.
Structural access degradation — the actor's prior access pathway to the facility terminated (role ended, contract lapsed, relocation) before the stated window.
Defensive friction encountered without adaptation — the actor was challenged near the site and did not return or adapt. Transient: may flip if the actor adapts.

Facility posture change created barriers — hardened access, changed schedules, or active surveillance detection blocks the actor's known methods during the countdown window; transient unless sustained.
Intervention closed the window — protective action, hospitalization, or law-enforcement contact interrupted the mobilization before the horizon arrived.

false_positive_context.criteria: Much late-pathway language resembles mobilization on the surface — acute despair, dark humor, artistic or performative expression, and crisis distress can all echo last-resort and farewell framing without any directed intent against a place. What distinguishes a false positive is whether the leakage attaches to a specific facility and timeframe, whether it progresses and converges with other warning behaviors, and whether a verifiable non-mobilization explanation (crisis, catharsis, expression) accounts for it.
contexts: Mental-health crisis without direction — suicidal or hopeless statements reflecting acute distress, self-directed rather than aimed at a place; a clinical, not operational, picture.
Catharsis and venting — heated last-resort talk after a grievance that discharges emotion and subsides without attaching to a site or a timeline.
Performative and artistic expression — song lyrics, fiction, gaming banter, streamer bravado, and gallows humor that borrow apocalyptic or countdown language without intent.
Life-transition farewell behaviors — giving away possessions, settling affairs, or farewell messages driven by relocation, terminal illness, retirement, or religious observance.
Advocacy hyperbole — activist or issue-oriented rhetoric using urgency and ultimatum framing ('now or never') as persuasion, without a facility target or operational preparation.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: This tactic sits closest to mobilization of any target-development behavior, so its findings carry a lower activation threshold than earlier-phase tactics. Leakage that names or unmistakably alludes to a specific facility and attaches to a near-term horizon — a countdown, a date-certain window, an occupancy or anniversary alignment — warrants immediate activation of response protocols regardless of internal tier, particularly where it correlates with staging-class behaviors elsewhere (means acquired, dry runs observed, materiel emplaced). Tier-determination depends on three factors: credibility of the leakage, convergence across warning behaviors, and progression over time. A single low-credibility statement with an available non-mobilization explanation sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility leakage with site specificity and imminence sits at the investigation tier. Convergence — leakage plus last-resort framing plus farewell behavior plus acceleration against the same place — sits at the elevation tier and should be treated as a mobilization-imminent pathway rather than as isolated remarks. Warning behaviors that persist or sharpen despite implemented countermeasures sit at the committed-actor tier and indicate probable entry into mobilization. Multiple lower-priority signals correlating temporally or modally compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding warrants; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit, because the diagnostic value of this tactic is precisely in the aggregation of the pathway, not in any one behavior. Tier-triggered actions: monitoring triggers logging and pattern-detection; investigation triggers actor-identification and a facility-vulnerability assessment; elevation triggers countermeasure activation and protective coordination appropriate to the site's posture; the committed-actor tier triggers a defensive-posture upgrade and interdiction planning; a confirmed actor matching a known threat-actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor leaks intent to a third party in language that names or unmistakably alludes to a specific facility, revealing that the place is the intended object of a coming act

Threat actor uses countdown or time-imminence language tied to the place — 'soon,' 'before Friday,' 'you'll see,' or a date-certain window aligned to the facility's occupancy or a symbolic anniversary

Threat actor voices last-resort or final-act framing about the place — 'nothing left to lose,' 'the only way,' 'they left me no choice' — treating action against the facility as decided and alternatives as exhausted

Threat actor exhibits farewell or legacy behaviors presupposing an endpoint — drafting a manifesto or final message, recording a legacy statement, giving away possessions, or settling affairs in connection with the act against the place
Threat actor shows an energy-burst acceleration and end-of-planning surge — an observable shift from deliberate planning tempo into compressed, action-directed activity aimed at the facility

countermeasures.measure: Establish OSINT and social-media monitoring tuned for pathway leakage — countdown language, last-resort framing, farewell and legacy posts, and manifesto uploads referencing the facility or its class
countermeasures.limitations: Encrypted and closed channels are not visible; leakage may be oblique or private, and performative or crisis language generates false positives that require human triage before action

countermeasures.measure: Stand up and publicize a behavioral-threat reporting pathway (see-something channel, tip line, staff and community briefings) so that leakage and farewell behaviors observed by peers reach the threat-management team quickly
countermeasures.limitations: Depends on bystander recognition and willingness to report; leakage confided to intimates or peers may not reach the channel, and stigma around mental-health crises suppresses some reporting

countermeasures.measure: Operate a multidisciplinary behavioral threat assessment and management (BTAM) capability that can triage leakage, weigh convergence of warning behaviors, and open a managed case with a monitored disposition
countermeasures.limitations: Requires trained personnel and standing authorities across HR, legal, security, and clinical partners; assessment quality depends on information access and can misjudge ambivalent or concealed cases

countermeasures.measure: Pre-plan interdiction and off-ramp options for imminence signals — a decision framework pairing protective posture upgrades and law-enforcement coordination with diversion, welfare-check, and support pathways that can defuse the grievance driving the countdown
countermeasures.limitations: Off-ramps depend on identifying and reaching the actor in time and on the grievance being addressable; a committed actor may not accept diversion, and premature contact can accelerate an ambivalent one

response_protocols.trigger: Leakage, countdown language, last-resort framing, farewell behavior, or an observed acceleration surfaces against a specific facility, singly or in combination
response_protocols.action: Open or update the facility threat case and treat as mobilization-adjacent. Conduct an expedited assessment: (a) corroborate the observation and preserve the leakage artifact, (b) identify the actor and review digital footprint for imminence and means, (c) weigh convergence across warning behaviors and any correlated staging-class findings, (d) assess the facility's current occupancy exposure and posture, (e) brief facility security leadership and, where imminence is present, initiate law-enforcement coordination. Document all sourcing and timing.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Countdown attaches to a date-certain or occupancy window, means or staging appear for the same actor, or warning behaviors converge and sharpen despite intervention
response_protocols.legal_notes: Monitoring and contact of an identified actor may implicate privacy, anti-stalking, and mental-health-privacy statutes that vary by jurisdiction; some interventions (welfare checks, emergency holds, protective orders) carry their own thresholds. Consult counsel before active monitoring or contact and document the investigative and safety basis for any action.

response_protocols.trigger: Time-imminence signal against the facility — countdown or date-certain language aligned to a real occupancy, event, or anniversary window
response_protocols.action: Elevate facility posture for the exposure window and pursue interdiction and off-ramp options in parallel: increase visible security presence, brief staff on reporting and lockdown procedures, tighten access control and standoff, coordinate law-enforcement patrol emphasis and, where the actor is identified, a welfare or interdiction contact paired with available support pathways. Reassess continuously until the window closes or the actor is resolved.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Actor is located in proximity to the site within the named window, or interdiction contact indicates a committed rather than ambivalent actor
response_protocols.legal_notes: Posture changes are within facility authority; interdiction and welfare contacts should be led by law enforcement or qualified clinicians within their authorities. Document the threat basis to support resource requests, defend proportionality, and protect the actor's rights during any intervention.

tactics.field_notes: Pathway and escalation indicators are the closest read to 'this is about to happen' that target development offers, and they are almost never a single line. The diagnostic value is in the aggregation: leakage that names the place, a countdown that fixes it to a window, last-resort framing that forecloses alternatives, farewell behaviors that presuppose an endpoint, and an energy burst where deliberate planning suddenly compresses into action tempo. Any one of these has an innocent twin — venting, dark humor, a mental-health crisis, a life transition, activist hyperbole — so the work is watching for convergence and progression against the same site rather than reacting to one alarming sentence. Leakage now lives mostly online, and the final phase often gets telegraphed there in the hours to days before action, which is both the opportunity and the trap: it is where you get warning, and where you get flooded with performative noise. When the signals converge on a place and a near horizon, treat it as mobilization-imminent, and remember the off-ramp — the same grievance driving the countdown is sometimes the thing an intervention can still defuse.
observed_contexts: fixated actor posting a countdown and a farewell message naming a corporate headquarters in the days before an attempted attack
aggrieved former employee giving away possessions and telling a coworker 'they'll be sorry Monday' about the plant, an acceleration caught by a peer report
extremist livestreaming last-resort framing and uploading a manifesto referencing a place of worship as the intended site hours before mobilizing
[literature: NTAC-MASS-2021 / MELOY-TRAP18-2016 pattern — leakage, last-resort framing, and energy-burst warning behaviors preceding targeted facility attacks]

tactics.name: Surveillance Detection
tactics.notes: Counter-surveillance tradecraft directed at the targeted facility's security apparatus: the threat actor works to detect, characterize, and defeat the site's observation OF THE ACTOR. Behaviors include probing whether cameras and guards are watching the actor, testing guard reaction to a staged stimulus, running decoy or dry-approach passes to see who responds, identifying plainclothes or roving coverage and CCTV fields that capture the actor, varying approach and timing to defeat pattern-detection, and detecting or evading being followed by facility security or law enforcement. The direction of the gaze is defender-to-actor, and the actor is trying to break it. Distinct from Physical Reconnaissance (TF0103), where the actor watches the FACILITY, and from Security Posture Assessment (TF0105), where the actor catalogs the security SYSTEM's gaps. Here the object of interest is the actor's own exposure — whether the site can see, record, follow, or later identify the actor, and how to move so it cannot.
tactics.cpn_notes: Counter-surveillance is increasingly informed by cheap technical aids — RF and camera-detector apps, published guard-schedule leaks, review-site and social posts revealing plainclothes patterns, and mapping tools used to plan surveillance-detection routes — that let an actor characterize a facility's observation coverage before committing to an approach.

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises with corroboration across modalities, persistence over time, and recoverable evidence that the actor is probing or defeating the facility's observation of the actor rather than merely present near the site. Credibility falls when the source, the content, or the temporal pattern is thin, and when a plausible legitimate reason for the evasive or testing behavior was never ruled out.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-modal corroboration — a guard-reaction test on camera, a staff account of a staged distraction, and repeated approach variation against the same facility within overlapping timeframes.
Temporal persistence — counter-surveillance behavior observed across multiple visits over weeks, not a single evasive moment.
Material evidence — recovered notes on camera positions and blind spots, guard-timing logs kept by the actor, RF- or camera-detector tools, or route sketches for defeating coverage of the site.
First-hand witness fidelity — a named guard or officer who watched the actor test a reaction and then withdraw; high-resolution reporting of the stimulus, the response measured, and the timing.
Behavioral specificity — the actor's evasion is keyed to this facility's specific cameras, patrol pattern, or plainclothes coverage rather than generic caution.
Source motivation aligned with accuracy — trained security observer reporting through a formal channel, not an informal tip with a competing agenda.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — single anonymous tip, reporter cannot be re-contacted to confirm the evasive behavior.
Content-specificity weakness — vague 'seemed to be checking the cameras' with no described act that distinguishes probing from ordinary glancing.
Temporal-pattern weakness — one apparently evasive moment with no follow-through or repetition.
Source-motivation misalignment — reporter has a structural reason to embellish (prior dispute with the person, tenant rivalry, litigation).

Unrebutted legitimate explanation — the testing or evasive behavior admits a benign reading (privacy-conscious member of the public, journalist, process server, someone avoiding an ex) that investigation did not exclude.
Reconstructive memory — reporting delay long enough that ordinary movement is retrofitted into a counter-surveillance narrative.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when the actor's counter-surveillance shows operational discipline — accurate reading of camera coverage, correct inference of plainclothes and patrol patterns, controlled testing of guard reaction, and movement designed to defeat pattern-detection and following. Capability falls with clumsy, self-defeating evasion, reliance on public rumor about coverage, and probing that immediately exposes the actor.
high_signal_anchors: Accurate coverage reading — the actor correctly identifies real camera fields, blind spots, and which personnel are plainclothes, demonstrating trained observation of the observers.

Controlled reaction testing — a staged stimulus (dropped package, briefly triggered door, staged distraction) executed to measure response time and posture, then a clean withdrawal without committing.
Surveillance-detection movement — the actor runs a route or timing pattern designed to reveal and shake following coverage, indicating knowledge of surveillance-detection tradecraft.
Counter-pattern discipline — the actor deliberately varies approach, dress, vehicle, and timing across visits to deny the facility a stable pattern-of-life to detect.
Technical-aid literacy — the actor uses RF or camera detectors, signal-mapping, or coverage research productively rather than as props.
Cut-out and exposure control — the actor uses intermediaries, avoids a consistent return signature, and manages what any single camera or officer can attribute to the actor.
low_signal_anchors: Self-defeating evasion — theatrical dodging that draws more attention than a normal approach would.
Rumor-only coverage knowledge — everything the actor 'knows' about cameras and guards is public gossip or review-site posts, with no verified operational reach.
Probe exposed on first attempt — the reaction test immediately identified the actor as the source of the stimulus.
No-concealment repetition — repeated testing with the same appearance, vehicle, and timing, defeating the purpose of counter-surveillance.
Misreads coverage — the actor fixates on decoy or non-functional cameras and misses live coverage, showing poor tradecraft.
Direct-contact breach — the actor asked staff directly about camera or guard coverage, surrendering the concealment counter-surveillance is meant to preserve.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when counter-surveillance progresses from casual caution toward deliberate, repeated defeat of the facility's observation, when the actor retains what was learned about coverage, and when the evasion is paired with stated hostility toward the site or with other target-development behavior. Intent falls with generic privacy caution, isolated evasive moments, and a verifiable benign purpose.
high_signal_anchors: Behavioral progression casual-to-deliberate — an observable shift from ordinary caution to systematic probing and defeat of the site's coverage.
Facility-specific counter-surveillance — the effort concentrates on this site's cameras, guards, and following coverage rather than general situational awareness anywhere.
Operational specificity in testing — the actor measures response time, identifies who responds, or maps exactly which fields capture the actor, treating the answers as inputs to an approach.
Sustained adaptation to defender posture — the actor tracks changes in the facility's coverage over time and re-routes or re-times to stay unseen.
Retention of what was learned — coverage maps, guard-timing notes, or annotated imagery of camera positions kept and organized, suggesting later operational use.

Hostile attribution paired with counter-surveillance — the actor has expressed grievance toward the facility AND is observed defeating its observation of the actor; the combination is intent-diagnostic in a way no single indicator captures.
low_signal_anchors: Generic privacy caution — broad wariness of cameras consistent with an ordinary privacy-conscious person, not pinned to this site as an objective.
One-time evasion without escalation — a single evasive moment that did not repeat or develop.
Verifiable legitimate purpose — journalist, licensed investigator, process server, or someone avoiding a personal contact surfaces and checks out.
No retention behavior — coverage noticed in passing but nothing recorded, mapped, or organized.
Target ambiguity — evasive behavior spread across many locations without narrowing counter-surveillance to this facility.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the actor can act on knowledge of the facility's observation — combining a working model of camera coverage and patrol timing, a demonstrated ability to move unseen, exploited insider knowledge of the security picture, and positional presence during low-coverage windows. Opportunity falls with observation the actor cannot defeat, distance not closed, or a covert posture the actor has not detected; when opportunity appears reduced, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: No detection friction encountered — the actor moves against the site repeatedly without being reliably observed, recorded attributable, or followed.

Coverage-timing mastery — the actor reliably knows when cameras are unmonitored, when patrols are thin, and which windows minimize the site's observation of the actor. The informational dimension of opportunity.
Blind-spot and following knowledge — the actor knows camera dead zones, patrol gaps, and how to break any following coverage around the facility.

Insider connection being exploited — an identified employee, contractor, or vendor relationship the actor is actively leveraging for the security-coverage picture. Dormant connections are potential, not realized; the exploitation pattern is what is high-signal.
Geographic-temporal proximity — the actor lives or works near the facility and is present during its low-coverage windows.
Unseen access achieved — the actor has moved through the site or its approaches without generating attributable coverage.
low_signal_anchors: Covert coverage undetected by the actor — the facility's discreet or plainclothes observation is capturing the actor without the actor's awareness. Durable signal: sticky unless the actor detects and adapts to it.
Institutional rule-out of insider access — access audits or process actively cleared the possibility the actor is drawing on inside knowledge of the security picture.
Structural access degradation — the actor's prior source of coverage knowledge terminated (role ended, contract lapsed, relocation).
Detection friction encountered without adaptation — the actor was observed and challenged, left, and did not return or change method. Transient: may flip if the actor adapts.
Geographic distance not closed — the actor is remote and defeating the site's coverage in person requires a travel investment not yet made.
Posture change created barriers — new or randomized coverage, covert overlays, or active surveillance-detection countermeasures block the actor's known evasion methods; transient unless sustained.

false_positive_context.criteria: Many legitimate activities resemble surveillance detection on the surface — a privacy-conscious member of the public avoiding cameras looks similar to an actor mapping coverage; a journalist or licensed investigator working discreetly looks similar to counter-surveillance. What distinguishes a false positive is whether the underlying behavior has a verifiable legitimate purpose, a transparent identity behind it, or institutional accountability that can be checked.
contexts: Verified professional purpose — authorized security consultants and red-teamers conducting sanctioned surveillance-detection or penetration testing of the facility; auditors verifying camera and guard coverage under contract.
Legal authority — authorized law-enforcement counter-surveillance and covert operations; licensed private investigators working lawful matters discreetly; process servers avoiding avoidance.
Privacy-conscious public — ordinary people who dislike being filmed, avoid cameras, or take indirect routes for personal-safety or privacy reasons unrelated to the site.
Press and research activity — journalists protecting sources or working sensitively near a facility; academics studying surveillance or urban movement.
Personal-safety avoidance — individuals evading an abuser, stalker, or personal contact whose movements coincidentally read as counter-surveillance near the facility.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Findings correlating with staging-class facility behaviors elsewhere — accelerant or explosive-precursor acquisition, observed dry runs against the site, emplacement of materiel, or alignment with an occupancy or anniversary window — warrant immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Tier-determination for this tactic's findings depends on three factors: credibility of the indicator, breadth across modalities, and persistence over time. A single low-credibility indicator with an available legitimate explanation (privacy-conscious member of the public) sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility indicator with operational specificity — a measured guard-reaction test or a deliberate route to defeat following coverage of this facility — sits at the investigation tier. Because counter-surveillance is deliberately covert, its low detectability should raise, not lower, analytic weight: absence of an obvious signal is consistent with disciplined tradecraft, not with absence of threat. Cross-modal corroboration — grievance plus coverage-mapping plus reaction-testing against the same site — sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating as coordinated facility target development by a disciplined actor. Indicators persisting despite implemented countermeasures, or evidence the actor has detected and adapted to covert coverage, sit at the committed-actor tier, suggesting potential entry into mobilization. Multiple lower-priority indicators correlating temporally or modally may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding warrants; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered actions: monitoring triggers discreet logging and pattern-detection; investigation triggers actor-identification and a facility coverage-gap review; elevation triggers covert-coverage reinforcement and countermeasure activation appropriate to the site's posture; the committed-actor tier triggers a defensive-posture upgrade held as close-hold to avoid confirming coverage to the actor; a confirmed actor matching a known threat-actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor tests guard or officer reaction to a staged stimulus — a dropped package, a briefly triggered door or alarm, a staged distraction — to measure response time and posture, then withdraws without committing
Threat actor runs decoy or dry-approach passes at the facility to see who responds, flushing plainclothes, roving, or covert security into the open

Threat actor works to identify and map the facility's coverage of the actor — spotting CCTV fields that capture the actor, picking out plainclothes or roving personnel, and noting which positions can see or record the actor
Threat actor deliberately varies approach, appearance, vehicle, and timing across visits to defeat the facility's pattern-of-life detection and deny security a stable baseline

Threat actor detects and evades being followed or observed by facility security or law enforcement — running surveillance-detection routes, using cut-outs, and controlling exposure to break any coverage of the actor

countermeasures.measure: Train guards and officers to recognize counter-surveillance behavior directed at them — reaction-tests, decoy passes, coverage-mapping, and approach variation — and to report it discreetly rather than reacting in a way that confirms coverage to the actor
countermeasures.limitations: Depends on observer discipline and turnover; disciplined actors deliberately keep each probe below the threshold any single guard would flag, and reporting culture varies by site

countermeasures.measure: Maintain covert and plainclothes observation overlays and concealed CCTV so the facility's coverage of an approaching actor is not itself observable, denying counter-surveillance the confirmation it seeks
countermeasures.limitations: Covert coverage is expensive to sustain and degrades once patterns leak; a disciplined actor running surveillance-detection routes may still detect and adapt to it over repeated visits

countermeasures.measure: Randomize patrol timing, routes, and response choreography so the actor cannot build a stable baseline to probe, and so a reaction-test yields no reliable model of the site's posture
countermeasures.limitations: Randomization trades efficiency for unpredictability and can degrade coverage of fixed critical points; determined actors compensate by sampling across more visits

countermeasures.measure: Log and correlate anomalous test-class events across the site — false alarms, dropped-package reports, brief unexplained door triggers, and repeat visitors observed watching the guard response — into a suspicious-activity pipeline that surfaces probing patterns
countermeasures.limitations: Test events individually resemble routine nuisance incidents; correlation requires disciplined logging and analytic capacity many facilities lack, and closed or oblique probing may never enter the pipeline

response_protocols.trigger: Counter-surveillance behavior reported against the facility — a guard-reaction test, a decoy or dry-approach pass, observed coverage-mapping, or an actor watching who responds to a stimulus
response_protocols.action: Open or update the facility threat case without tipping the actor. Conduct a 24-hour preliminary assessment: (a) discreetly corroborate the observation across CCTV and guard accounts, (b) preserve imagery and logs of the testing behavior, (c) review whether covert coverage captured the actor, (d) brief facility security leadership close-hold and avoid overt posture changes that confirm coverage. Document all sourcing.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Actor identified with apparent means and proximity, OR the actor is observed detecting and adapting to covert coverage, OR indicators across other facility tactics surface for the same actor
response_protocols.legal_notes: Covert observation and any monitoring of an identified actor may implicate privacy, anti-stalking, and wiretap statutes that vary by jurisdiction. Consult counsel before active or covert monitoring; document the investigative basis for any action.

response_protocols.trigger: Confirmed disciplined counter-surveillance by an identified actor — surveillance-detection routes, use of cut-outs, or evidence the actor has detected and is defeating the site's coverage
response_protocols.action: Treat as an advanced-tradecraft indicator and elevate. Reinforce covert coverage held close-hold, coordinate with law enforcement on discreet follow, avoid revealing the full security picture, and reassess the facility's coverage gaps the actor may be exploiting. Hold posture changes as close-hold to prevent confirming coverage to the actor.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Counter-surveillance resolves to a specific actor with staging-class behavior elsewhere, or a date-certain threat emerges
response_protocols.legal_notes: Coordinated covert surveillance and law-enforcement follow raise heightened legal exposure; document the threat basis, defend proportionality, and keep counsel engaged throughout.

tactics.field_notes: Surveillance detection is the actor turning the lens around — not watching the building, but watching whether the building is watching the actor. The clearest tells are small and easy to dismiss one at a time: a package dropped near an entrance to see how fast a guard moves, a first pass that seems to accomplish nothing but flushes a plainclothes officer into view, the same person arriving three times looking different each time. Because good counter-surveillance is designed to be invisible, the absence of an obvious signal is not reassurance — it is consistent with discipline. The practitioner error is reacting visibly to a probe, which hands the actor exactly the reaction they staged the test to measure. The right posture is discreet: log it, preserve it, keep covert coverage covert, and let the pattern assemble before the actor knows they have been seen.
observed_contexts: actor who dropped a bag near a lobby entrance and timed the guard response on two separate visits before withdrawing each time
repeat visitor who changed vehicles and clothing across approaches, defeating the guard force's ability to recognize a pattern until CCTV review connected the visits
case where an actor's first pass at a facility drew a plainclothes officer into the open, after which the actor never returned by the same route
[literature: SANDIA-GARCIA-VAPPS-2006 / DHS-ISC-RMP-2021 pattern — adversary reaction-testing and coverage-mapping of a facility's protection system before an approach]

tactics.name: Operational Rehearsal
tactics.notes: Practice execution of the attack plan against the targeted facility short of the act itself — dry runs, dress rehearsals, timed practice approaches, response-time probes, and off-site practice on a stand-in layout. Distinct from Physical Reconnaissance (which studies the site to build the plan) and from Approach (the single final movement immediately before execution): rehearsal repeats and refines an already-formed plan to reduce friction, validate timing, and build the actor's confidence. The behavior here is about repetition and calibration against the specific place — walking the route until the window is known, testing whether the plan survives contact with the site's live posture.
tactics.cpn_notes: Rehearsal increasingly leaves a digital trail: actors time practice approaches with mapping and navigation apps, review street-level and satellite imagery to pre-walk the route, and record or narrate dry runs to a phone or cloud account for later study. GPS logs, dashcam and helmet-cam footage, and repeated location pings against the facility can corroborate a physical rehearsal pattern that is otherwise easy to dismiss as ordinary movement.

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises with corroboration across modalities, repetition of the same behavior over time, and recoverable evidence tying the actor to timed or staged practice against the specific facility. Credibility falls when a single pass is over-read, when the source or temporal pattern is thin, and when an ordinary reason for the movement — commute, delivery, routine visit — was never ruled out.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-modal corroboration — CCTV of repeat timed approaches, access-log anomalies, and GPS or app data against the same facility within overlapping timeframes.
Behavioral repetition — the same route, arrival window, or entry test observed multiple times, not a single pass that admits a benign reading.
Material evidence — recovered dashcam or helmet-cam footage, a narrated dry-run recording, timing notes, or an annotated route that physically ties the actor to rehearsal of the plan.

First-hand witness fidelity — a named guard, employee, or neighbor who observed the actor pausing to time a response, tailgating a test, or measuring an approach, with high-resolution reporting of what was done and when.
Behavioral specificity — the practice is pinned to the specific facility and its access, timing, or response features rather than a vague pattern of presence.
Source motivation aligned with accuracy — a trained observer reporting through a formal channel, not an informal tip with a competing agenda.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — single anonymous tip, reporter cannot be re-contacted to confirm repetition.
Content-specificity weakness — one observed pass that could describe any driver, walker, or delivery on that route.
Temporal-pattern weakness — a single sighting with no observed repetition or measured behavior.
Source-motivation misalignment — reporter has a structural reason to embellish (dispute with the actor, tenant rivalry, litigation).
Unrebutted legitimate explanation — the movement admits a benign reading (commuter, courier, neighbor, exercise route) that investigation did not exclude.
Reconstructive memory — reporting delay long enough that ordinary movement may be retrofitted to a rehearsal narrative.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when the practice shows operational discipline — covert repetition, accurate measurement of timing and response, use of a realistic stand-in, and the tradecraft to run a dry run without exposing intent. Capability falls with conspicuous, un-concealed repetition, practice that fails on first contact with the site's posture, and rehearsal that produces no usable calibration.
high_signal_anchors: Covert repetition tradecraft — varied vehicles, appearance, or approach vectors across practice runs; no fixed pattern a defender can easily flag.
Multi-modal coordination — physical practice approaches, digital route study, and response-time probing coordinated across overlapping timeframes.
Measured calibration — the actor reliably captures travel time, arrival window, guard-reaction interval, or law-enforcement response time and refines the plan against it.
Realistic stand-in practice — rehearsal on a comparable off-site structure, mock layout, or similar venue that transfers to the target.
Counter-surveillance during rehearsal — the actor watches for observation while practicing, aborts and re-runs, and avoids a detectable return signature.
Demonstrated execution literacy — the dry run exercises the full sequence (approach, entry, movement, egress) competently, indicating the plan is mature rather than aspirational.
low_signal_anchors: Conspicuous posture — obvious repeated loitering, timing an approach in the open, lingering at the entrance past any plausible purpose.
No-concealment repetition — the same vehicle and appearance on an identical route with no attempt at variation or cover.
Practice failure on initial contact — the run collapsed when challenged by staff or an unexpected posture and was not re-attempted.
No measurement — presence without any observable timing, testing, or refinement; movement that yields no calibration.
Single-modality engagement — only physical or only digital practice; no coordination across modes.
Direct-contact attempts — the actor engaged staff or security during a run in a way that breached operational discipline about exposure.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when practice progresses from loose familiarization toward precise, execution-shaped repetition, when the actor retains timing and route products, and when rehearsal is paired with stated grievance against the place or a fixed date. Intent falls with incidental repetition, runs that do not tighten toward an execution window, and a verifiable benign purpose for the movement.
high_signal_anchors: Behavioral progression loose-to-precise — an observable tightening from general familiarization to timed, execution-shaped runs against the specific facility.
Execution-shaped behavior — practice mirrors the attack sequence (staged approach, entry test, timed egress) rather than ordinary transit or observation.
Operational specificity in the run — the actor times a delivery window, tests a specific door or alarm, or rehearses to a particular occupancy period or anniversary.
Sustained attention to defender response — the actor probes and re-probes guard and law-enforcement reaction and adapts the plan to it.
Retention of rehearsal products — route timings saved, dry-run footage archived, notes maintained, suggesting a plan being finalized for use.

Hostile attribution paired with rehearsal — the actor has expressed grievance toward the facility or its function AND is observed running timed practice against it; the combination is intent-diagnostic in a way no single indicator captures.
low_signal_anchors: Incidental-repetition behavior — a repeated route explained by commute, work, or errand rather than practice of an attack.
One-time run without escalation — a single anomalous pass with no tightening or follow-through.
Verifiable legitimate purpose — courier, contractor, employment, or residence relationship surfaces and checks out.
No retention behavior — runs occur but no timing, footage, or notes are captured or organized.
Window ambiguity — practice does not converge on any particular time, entrance, or occupancy period.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when rehearsal confirms the actor can act — validated mastery of timing and access, tested knowledge of security gaps, exploited insider access rehearsed in practice, and the positional ability to reach the site during its vulnerable window. Opportunity falls with defensive friction the rehearsal exposes and the actor cannot overcome, distance not closed, or a posture that defeats the rehearsed plan; when opportunity appears reduced, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: No defensive friction encountered — practice runs proceed unimpeded, confirming the plan survives the site's live posture.

Validated pattern-of-life mastery — rehearsal confirms the site's occupancy cycles, delivery and service windows, and low-security periods with tested accuracy. The informational dimension of opportunity, now proven by practice.
Tested security-gap knowledge — the actor has practiced against camera blind spots, standoff weaknesses, patrol timing, or a specific unmonitored entry and found them exploitable.

Insider connection exploited in rehearsal — an employee, contractor, or vendor relationship the actor is actively leveraging to run or cover a practice entry. Dormant connections are potential; the rehearsed exploitation pattern is high-signal.
Geographic-temporal proximity — the actor lives or works near the facility and rehearses during its vulnerable windows.
Direct rehearsed access — the actor has run a practice entry through a legitimate role or credential and reached the intended position.
low_signal_anchors: Rehearsal defeated by hardened posture — practice runs were actively blocked by the facility's countermeasures. Durable signal: sticky unless the actor materially adapts or the posture drops.
Institutional rule-out of insider access — access audits or process actively cleared the possibility the rehearsal would exploit, not merely failed to find it.
Structural access degradation — the rehearsed pathway terminated (role ended, contract lapsed, relocation) after practice.
Defensive friction encountered without adaptation — the actor aborted a run when challenged and did not return or re-run. Transient: may flip if the actor adapts.
Geographic distance not closed — the actor is remote and physical practice requires a major travel investment not yet made.
Posture change invalidating the rehearsal — hardened access, changed schedules, or active surveillance detection defeats the practiced plan; transient unless sustained.

false_positive_context.criteria: Much ordinary movement resembles rehearsal on the surface — a commuter driving the same route at the same hour looks similar to a timed approach; a delivery driver testing a loading dock looks similar to an access probe; a film crew or event planner walking a venue looks similar to a dry run. What distinguishes a false positive is whether the repeated behavior has a verifiable legitimate purpose, a transparent identity behind it, or institutional accountability that can be checked.
contexts: Routine movement — commuters, couriers, rideshare and delivery drivers, and service personnel whose repetition on a route or at an entrance is explained by their work.

Verified professional purpose — contractors, inspectors, surveyors, film and event crews, and security professionals conducting authorized drills, walk-throughs, or vulnerability tests of the facility.
Legal authority — authorized law-enforcement activity with proper basis; licensed investigators on lawful matters; sanctioned red-team or penetration exercises against the site.
Personal or community connection — employees, patrons, congregants, students, and neighbors whose familiar comings and goings produce a repeated but benign pattern.
Non-threatening activity — hobbyist drivers, cyclists and runners on a fixed route, photographers, and trainees practicing a legitimate skill near the site.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Rehearsal is a mobilization behavior: it presumes a formed plan and signals a shortening runway to execution, so its findings weight higher than target-development signals and warrant faster action. Findings correlating with other staging-class behaviors — accelerant or device emplacement, materiel caching near the site, a stated or observed date-certain, or alignment with an occupancy or anniversary window — warrant immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Tier-determination for this tactic's findings depends on three factors: credibility of the indicator, breadth across modalities, and repetition over time. A single low-credibility pass with an available legitimate explanation sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility run with measured timing or a response probe against the facility sits at the investigation tier. Cross-modal corroboration — grievance plus repeated timed approaches plus a defender-response probe against the same site — sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating as active preparation for attack. Rehearsal persisting despite implemented countermeasures, or tightening toward a specific window, sits at the committed-actor tier and suggests imminence. Multiple lower-priority observations correlating temporally or modally may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single run warrants; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered actions: monitoring triggers logging and pattern-detection across CCTV and access data; investigation triggers actor-identification and a facility-vulnerability reassessment against the observed practice; elevation triggers countermeasure activation and pattern randomization appropriate to the site's posture; the committed-actor tier triggers a defensive-posture upgrade and law-enforcement notification; a confirmed actor matching a known threat-actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor conducts repeated timed practice approaches to the facility, driving or walking the same route to measure travel time, arrival windows, or the interval between key points
Threat actor rehearses a full dry run of the attack sequence against the site — approach, entry, movement, and egress — short of the act, sometimes recorded or narrated for later study
Threat actor tests defender response by probing an alarm, tailgating an entry, or staging a minor incident to time guard reaction and law-enforcement arrival at the facility

Threat actor practices with a specific weapon, device, or method at an off-site location resembling the target — a stand-in structure, mock layout, or comparable venue — to rehearse the method before use
Threat actor runs a decoy or reconnaissance-in-force pass timed to the facility's occupied hours, observing crowd density and staff positioning during a specific recurring window

countermeasures.measure: Deploy CCTV pattern-detection and guard-awareness protocols to flag rehearsal signatures — repeat visits, timed approaches, measured pauses, and the same vehicle or individual on an identical route across multiple passes
countermeasures.limitations: Rehearsal blends into ordinary movement; disciplined actors vary vehicles and appearance to defeat pattern-matching, and analytics generate false positives on legitimate repeat traffic that must be triaged

countermeasures.measure: Randomize security patterns — patrol timing, response drills, access-check schedules, and posture changes — so a rehearsed timeline cannot be relied upon and the practiced plan is invalidated
countermeasures.limitations: Randomization raises the cost of a rehearsed plan but does not detect the actor; sustaining true unpredictability strains staffing, and a determined actor may re-rehearse against the new pattern

countermeasures.measure: Train staff and coordinate with neighbors and local law enforcement to report suspected response probes — nuisance alarms, tailgating attempts, and staged minor incidents — as possible rehearsal rather than routine annoyances
countermeasures.limitations: Depends on staff reporting discipline and the tendency to dismiss repeated false alarms as faults; a single probe is easy to rationalize, and neighbor reporting is uneven

countermeasures.measure: Conduct a structured after-action review of any detected probe or anomalous alarm, correlating CCTV, access logs, and prior reports to test for a rehearsal pattern, and temporarily elevate posture on the finding
countermeasures.limitations: Reactive by design — it acts only after a probe is noticed, and it cannot resolve intent from a single event; posture elevation is temporary and resource-limited

response_protocols.trigger: One or more Operational Rehearsal indicators reported (repeat timed approaches, an observed dry run, off-site practice on a stand-in, or a decoy pass timed to occupied hours)
response_protocols.action: Open or update the facility threat case and treat as active preparation. Conduct an expedited assessment: (a) correlate CCTV, access logs, and any GPS or app evidence to establish repetition and pattern, (b) identify the actor and review the digital footprint for recorded or narrated runs, (c) reassess the facility's vulnerability against the specific behavior practiced, (d) brief facility security leadership and elevate posture during the identified window. Preserve all evidence for law enforcement.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Rehearsal tightens toward a specific window or date, correlates with materiel/emplacement indicators, OR the actor matches a known threat-actor profile
response_protocols.legal_notes: Rehearsal often occurs on public routes and rights-of-way where expectation of privacy is limited, but targeted monitoring of an identified actor may implicate privacy and anti-stalking statutes that vary by jurisdiction. Consult counsel before active monitoring; document the investigative basis and chain of custody for any evidence.

response_protocols.trigger: A defender-response probe is detected against the facility (nuisance alarm test, tailgating attempt, or staged minor incident) consistent with rehearsal of an attack timeline
response_protocols.action: Treat as an imminent-planning signal, not a nuisance. Immediately randomize patrol and response patterns to invalidate any rehearsed timeline, surge visible security presence, coordinate with local law enforcement on patrol emphasis and a possible fixed post, preserve alarm and access records, and run an after-action review to test for a broader rehearsal pattern. Reassess posture at window close.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Probe resolves to an identified actor, recurs, or correlates with other rehearsal or staging indicators for the same site
response_protocols.legal_notes: Posture changes and pattern randomization are within facility authority; document the threat basis to support resource requests and to defend proportionality. Coordinate evidence handling with law enforcement if a probe is charged as trespass, tampering, or a false-alarm offense.

tactics.field_notes: Rehearsal is where a plan stops being talk and starts being muscle memory, and it is one of the highest-value catches in the mobilization phase because it presumes the plan already exists. The tells are repetition and measurement: the same route walked or driven at the same hour, a pause to watch a guard react, a nuisance alarm that turns out to have an audience timing the response. The hard part is that each pass, taken alone, looks like a commuter, a courier, or a faulty sensor — the signal only emerges when the repetition is aggregated and the behavior is measured rather than incidental. The most dangerous variant is the dry run timed to occupied hours, because it reveals both the intended window and a willingness to stand among the people who would be harmed. Defenders who dismiss repeated false alarms as maintenance problems miss the single clearest opportunity to disrupt an attack before the approach.
observed_contexts: actor caught on CCTV making three timed approaches to a house of worship at the same Friday hour over consecutive weeks before an interdicted attack
response probe in which an actor triggered a side-door alarm and sat in a nearby lot timing the guard's reaction and the police response
off-site case where an actor practiced a breach-and-move sequence on a vacant building of similar layout before targeting the live facility
[literature: NTAC-MASS-2021 / FBI-PREATTACK-2018 pattern — pre-attack rehearsal and probing behavior preceding facility attacks]

tactics.name: Concealment
tactics.notes: Deliberate hiding of the actor, the attack means, or the intent in the run-up to an attack on a specific facility — caching materiel near or en route to the site, disguising a device or vehicle as ordinary, adopting cover or physical disguise to blend at the place, and practicing communications and digital security to go dark before action. Distinct from Cover Construction in the target-development phase (which builds the pretext or legend) and from Device/Materiel Emplacement (which places the means for use). Concealment here is about defeating the facility's detection and the observer's attribution during staging: keeping the means, the identity, and the plan out of view until the moment of execution.
tactics.cpn_notes: Modern concealment increasingly blends physical and digital tradecraft — anonymized storage rentals, cash or cryptocurrency for materiel, encrypted and disappearing messaging, and scrubbed accounts — so the run-up to a facility attack can go dark across exactly the channels that carried earlier target-development signal.

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises with corroboration across modalities that the actor is actively hiding materiel, identity, or intent ahead of an attack on the site, with persistence over the staging window, and with recoverable evidence — a located cache, a seized disguised device, or forensically recovered communications. Credibility falls when the source, the content, or the temporal pattern is thin, and when a plausible legitimate explanation for the concealment was never ruled out.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-modal corroboration — a located materiel cache, a disguised object recovered at an approach, and observed OPSEC behavior against the same actor within overlapping timeframes.
Temporal persistence — a concealment pattern (caching, going dark, cover-building) sustained across the run-up to a suspected action window, not a single lapse.

Material evidence — recovered materiel, a seized disguised device, storage-rental records, or forensically recovered communications physically tying the actor to concealed preparation against the site.
First-hand witness fidelity — a named witness who observed the actor cache gear, alter a device, or stage cover near the facility; high-resolution reporting of what, where, and when.
Behavioral specificity — the concealment is method- and site-specific (materiel matched to an attack means, cover matched to the facility's access controls), not generic secrecy.
Source motivation aligned with accuracy — trained reporter or forensic channel, not an informal tip with a competing agenda.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — single anonymous tip about a 'suspicious package,' reporter cannot be re-contacted.
Content-specificity weakness — a vague impression of secrecy that could fit ordinary privacy behavior.
Temporal-pattern weakness — one-time observation with no follow-through.
Source-motivation misalignment — reporter has a structural reason to embellish (dispute with the facility, tenant rivalry, litigation).
Unrebutted legitimate explanation — the storage, disguise, or privacy behavior admits a benign reading (lawful storage, work uniform, privacy preference) that investigation did not exclude.
Reconstructive memory — reporting delay long enough that concealment details may be retrofitted to a threat narrative.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when concealment shows operational OPSEC discipline — clean caching tradecraft, credible disguises, communications security, evidence sanitization, and the literacy to defeat the facility's detection. Capability falls with sloppy caching, obvious disguise, OSINT-only reach, and cover that fails on first contact.
high_signal_anchors: Clean caching tradecraft — materiel stored off the actor's known footprint, using cut-outs, cash, or third-party accounts, with no observable return pattern.
Multi-modal OPSEC coordination — physical concealment, communications security, and digital sanitization coordinated across overlapping timeframes.
Detection-defeating disguise — a device or the actor is disguised in a way calibrated to the facility's specific screening, package handling, or access controls.
Cover durability — vendor, contractor, or delivery cover holds up under staff scrutiny at the site.
Counter-forensic behavior — the actor scrubs accounts, uses encryption and compartmentation, and stages an alibi, showing awareness of investigative methods.
Demonstrated technical literacy — the actor conceals materiel or a device in a manner reflecting understanding of the attack means and the site's detection posture.
low_signal_anchors: Conspicuous caching — materiel stored in the open, on the actor's own account, or in a way that invites discovery.
No-concealment repetition — attack-preparatory behavior with no OPSEC or cover at all.
Disguise failure on initial contact — staff or screening immediately flagged the object or cover as anomalous.
OSINT-only reach — concealment knowledge is generic and public; no operational tradecraft.
Single-modality engagement — only physical caching or only digital scrubbing; no coordination.
Direct-contact exposure — the actor breached OPSEC by contacting facility staff or boasting, undermining the concealment.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when concealment escalates from generic secrecy toward purpose-built hiding of an attack means or identity against the specific facility, when materiel or cover is retained and staged, and when concealment is paired with stated grievance against the place. Intent falls with generic privacy behavior, encounters that do not escalate, and a verifiable benign purpose.
high_signal_anchors: Behavioral progression broad-to-narrow — an observable funnel from general secrecy to purpose-built concealment of a specific means against the named facility.
Facility-specific concealment — the cover, cache location, or disguise is matched to the specific site's access, screening, or occupancy features.
Operational specificity — caching an attack means, altering a device to defeat the site's detection, or building a cover keyed to the facility's vendor and delivery process.
Sustained OPSEC against defender posture — the actor tracks the facility's countermeasures over time and adapts concealment accordingly.
Retention and staging of concealed materiel — materiel cached and maintained, disguises kept ready, an alibi staged, suggesting imminent operational use.

Hostile attribution paired with concealment — the actor has expressed grievance toward the facility or its function AND is observed hiding materiel, identity, or intent; the combination is intent-diagnostic in a way no single indicator captures.
low_signal_anchors: Generic-secrecy behavior — ordinary privacy or discretion not tied to an attack means or the site.
One-time observation without escalation — a concealment lapse surfaced but no follow-through or pattern.
Verifiable legitimate purpose — lawful storage, work uniform, or privacy preference surfaces and checks out.
No retention or staging behavior — materiel or cover observed casually but not maintained or positioned.
Target ambiguity — concealment not tied to any specific facility as an objective.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the actor can act on concealed preparation — a cache positioned near the site, cover that grants access, a disguise that defeats screening, exploited insider help — combined with knowledge of the facility's detection gaps. Opportunity falls with detection friction not adapted to, distance not closed, or a hardened screening posture that blocks the actor's known concealment methods; when opportunity appears reduced, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: No detection friction encountered — caching, cover, and disguise proceed unimpeded despite the facility's screening posture.
Concealment positioned for use — materiel cached within operational reach of the site, cover and disguise ready to deploy during a vulnerable window. The positional dimension of opportunity.
Detection-gap knowledge — the actor knows screening blind spots, unscreened delivery paths, or camera coverage gaps that make concealed materiel or cover viable.

Insider connection being exploited — an identified employee, contractor, or vendor relationship the actor is actively leveraging to cache materiel, validate cover, or bypass screening. Dormant connections are potential, not realized; the exploitation pattern is what is high-signal.
Geographic-temporal proximity — the actor can position and retrieve concealed materiel during the site's vulnerable windows.
Direct facility access under cover — the actor holds unsupervised access to the site through a legitimate-seeming role or credential.
low_signal_anchors: Concealment defeated by hardened screening — the facility's screening or access controls actively exposed the cache, disguise, or cover. Durable signal: sticky unless the actor materially adapts.
Institutional rule-out of insider access — audits or process actively cleared insider facilitation, not merely failed to find it.
Structural access degradation — the actor's cover or access pathway terminated (role ended, contract lapsed, relocation).
Detection friction encountered without adaptation — the actor abandoned the concealed approach after being challenged and did not return or adapt. Transient: may flip if the actor adapts.
Geographic distance not closed — the actor and the cache are remote and positioning requires a major move not yet made.
Screening posture change created barriers — added package screening, credential validation, or active surveillance blocks the actor's known concealment methods; transient unless sustained.

false_positive_context.criteria: Many legitimate activities resemble concealment on the surface — a tenant renting storage looks similar to caching; a contractor in uniform looks similar to cover; a privacy-conscious person going dark looks similar to OPSEC. What distinguishes a false positive is whether the underlying behavior has a verifiable legitimate purpose, a transparent identity behind it, or institutional accountability that can be checked.
