contexts: Verified professional purpose — vendors, contractors, and delivery personnel in legitimate uniforms with valid work orders; couriers and logistics staff handling packages and equipment on the site.

Legal authority — authorized law-enforcement or security personnel conducting covert but lawful operations; licensed private investigators; security professionals staging tools for authorized penetration tests of the facility.
Personal or community connection — tenants and residents using lawful storage; employees carrying work bags and equipment; ordinary privacy and communications-security preferences.
Non-threatening attention — hobbyists, collectors, and tradespeople who store tools, chemicals, or equipment for lawful use.
Academic and research purpose — researchers and students handling materials for legitimate work, or privacy advocates practicing routine operational security.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Findings correlating with staging- or execution-class facility behaviors — a located materiel cache, a disguised device recovered at an approach, observed emplacement, or alignment with an occupancy or anniversary window — warrant immediate activation of response protocols, and where a device or accelerant is suspected, EOD and law-enforcement rendering-safe, regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Tier-determination for this tactic's findings depends on three factors: credibility of the indicator, breadth across modalities, and persistence over time. A single low-credibility 'suspicious package' report with an available legitimate explanation sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility indicator with operational specificity — a cache matched to an attack means, or cover matched to the facility's process — sits at the investigation tier. Cross-modal corroboration — grievance plus caching plus OPSEC against the same site — sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating as coordinated mobilization concealment. Concealment persisting despite implemented countermeasures sits at the committed-actor tier, indicating potential imminent action. Multiple lower-priority indicators correlating temporally or modally may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding warrants; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered actions: monitoring triggers logging and pattern-detection; investigation triggers actor-identification, a search for cached materiel, and a facility-screening review; elevation triggers screening and access-control activation plus law-enforcement notification; the committed-actor tier triggers a defensive-posture upgrade and EOD/law-enforcement coordination; a confirmed actor matching a known threat-actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor caches attack materiel (accelerants, explosive precursors, weapons, or breaching tools) near the targeted facility or along the approach route, using storage units, vehicles, or concealed positions off the actor's known footprint

Threat actor disguises the attack means — concealing a device inside an ordinary package, altering a vehicle to appear routine, or masking materiel as legitimate cargo — to defeat the facility's screening and package handling

Threat actor practices communications and operational security ahead of action against the site — going dark on prior channels, adopting encrypted or disappearing messaging, and compartmenting the plan from associates

Threat actor adopts a physical disguise or cover to blend at the facility — altering appearance, wearing a vendor, contractor, or delivery uniform, or assuming a legitimate-seeming role to move unremarked near the site

Threat actor sanitizes the digital and physical trail before action — scrubbing accounts and search history, destroying preparatory materials, and staging an alibi to conceal intent and complicate later attribution

countermeasures.measure: Monitor for pre-attack caching indicators near the facility — new storage-unit rentals tied to the site's vicinity, repeated deliveries to vacant or transient addresses, and concealed materiel along approaches — and integrate the feed with suspicious-package reporting
countermeasures.limitations: Caching off the actor's known footprint, using cash or cut-outs, is difficult to attribute; coverage of off-site storage is limited and much of it is lawful and private

countermeasures.measure: Deploy package, vehicle, and anomaly screening at loading docks, entrances, and the standoff perimeter to detect disguised devices and out-of-pattern objects before they reach occupied space
countermeasures.limitations: Screening is bounded by throughput and coverage; a well-disguised device calibrated to the specific screening posture may pass, and unscreened delivery or service paths remain a gap

countermeasures.measure: Verify vendor, contractor, and delivery credentials against a live authorized list, and validate uniforms and work orders before granting access, to defeat cover and physical disguise at the point of entry
countermeasures.limitations: Insider facilitation or a validated but compromised vendor relationship can defeat verification; enforcement depends on staff discipline under time pressure at busy access points

countermeasures.measure: Run a suspicious-activity reporting program training staff to report abandoned items, staged materiel, out-of-place vehicles, and personnel whose behavior or cover does not fit the setting, with a low-friction reporting channel
countermeasures.limitations: Reporting quality varies and produces false positives from ordinary activity; effective concealment is designed precisely to look unremarkable to staff

response_protocols.trigger: Concealment of attack means detected — a suspected materiel cache near the site, a disguised device or out-of-pattern object at an approach, or staged materiel inside the perimeter
response_protocols.action: Treat as imminent mobilization. Do NOT handle a suspected device: establish a cordon and standoff, evacuate or shelter per plan, and request EOD and law enforcement to locate and render safe. Secure and preserve the scene and any recovered materiel for attribution, elevate facility posture, and brief security leadership. Document all sourcing and chain of custody.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Confirmed device or accelerant cache, OR an identified actor observed in a staging posture with means and proximity to the facility
response_protocols.legal_notes: Handling of suspected devices is a law-enforcement and EOD function; do not disturb. Search of cached materiel and any actor property implicates warrant requirements and chain-of-custody rules — coordinate with counsel and law enforcement before action.

response_protocols.trigger: Concealment of identity or intent signaled without located materiel — an identified actor going dark, sanitizing a trail, or adopting cover and disguise keyed to the facility
response_protocols.action: Treat as a heightened pre-attack indicator. Intensify monitoring of the identified actor within legal limits, brief facility staff on cover and disguise tells and reporting, validate the current vendor and contractor access list, and coordinate with law enforcement on the emerging picture. Reassess as indicators develop.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Concealment resolves to a located cache, a disguised device, or a date-certain or occupancy-window signal against the site
response_protocols.legal_notes: Monitoring of an identified actor may implicate privacy and anti-stalking statutes that vary by jurisdiction. Consult counsel before active monitoring; document the investigative basis for any action.

tactics.field_notes: Concealment is mostly caught by the seams — the storage unit that does not fit the actor's life, the package with no sender, the uniform that is a little wrong, the account that went dark right before an anniversary. By this phase the actor has usually stopped talking, so the expressive signal that carried target selection is gone; what remains is the physics of hiding attack means and identity near a place. The clearest tells are a materiel cache positioned for use and a cover keyed to the facility's own access and delivery process. The hard part is that every one of these — storage, uniforms, going quiet — is also ordinary life, so concealment is rarely diagnostic alone and earns its weight by pairing with a located means, a grievance, or an occupancy window.
observed_contexts: arson case where the actor pre-positioned accelerant in a rented unit blocks from the clinic and staged a delivery-driver cover for the approach
interdicted plot in which the device was disguised as a routine parcel to defeat the facility's package screening
insider-facilitated case where a contractor uniform and a valid-looking work order were used to cache tools inside the perimeter ahead of an intended action
[literature: ATF-EIR-2024 / FBI-PREATTACK-2018 pattern — pre-attack caching, device disguise, and OPSEC discipline preceding facility attacks]

tactics.name: Perimeter Breach
tactics.notes: Defeat of a facility's outer physical boundary to gain access to the controlled area — cutting or climbing perimeter fencing, forcing or ramming a gate or vehicle barrier, scaling a wall or roofline, or overpowering the personnel and access controls that hold the boundary. This is the first hard, chargeable physical act of a facility attack and the last clean line before the actor is inside. Distinct from Interior Penetration (which is movement through the building past the perimeter toward the objective) and from Approach (the final last-leg movement to the site). The focus here is the boundary itself: how the outer layer is overcome and what that defeat exposes.
tactics.cpn_notes: Perimeter breaches are increasingly pre-planned from remote reconnaissance — satellite and drone imagery of fence lines and clear zones, published site plans, and observed gate and patrol schedules let an actor select the weakest boundary segment, blind spots, and low-security windows before ever touching the fence.

credibility.criteria: Credibility of a perimeter-breach indicator rises with sensor-plus-human corroboration, recoverable physical evidence of a forced boundary defeat, and timing consistent with an approach rather than routine activity. Credibility falls when a single unverified alarm, an available benign cause that was never ruled out, or a thin sensor trace is all that supports the finding.
high_signal_anchors: Multi-sensor corroboration — a fence-line intrusion alarm confirmed by CCTV and by a responding officer's observation of a defeated boundary.
Recoverable physical evidence — cut fabric, a pried gate, a defeated lock, tool marks, or a displaced barrier section, photographed and preserved.
Timing consistent with approach — the boundary defeat occurs in a known low-security window or aligns with other staging behavior against the same site.
Directionality inward — the breach point and any tracks show movement into the controlled area, not out of it.
Method matched to the barrier — the means used are appropriate to defeat this specific perimeter, indicating purpose rather than accident.
Corroboration across time — prior probing of the same boundary segment captured by earlier sensor or patrol logs before the defeat.
low_signal_anchors: Single unconfirmed alarm — a lone fence-sensor activation with no CCTV or officer confirmation.
Unruled-out benign explanation — wildlife, weather, vegetation, or a maintenance crew could account for the disturbance and was not excluded.
No physical evidence — the boundary is intact on inspection and only an electronic anomaly exists.
Ambiguous directionality — disturbance consistent with someone leaving or with accidental contact, not a deliberate inward breach.
Nuisance-prone sensor history — the affected segment has a documented false-alarm rate that degrades the signal.
Reporting delay — the breach was discovered long after the fact with no timeline to tie it to an actor or approach.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when the actor defeats the boundary cleanly, uses tools or a vehicle matched to the barrier's rating, neutralizes detection during the crossing, and moves with rehearsed economy. Capability falls with noisy or failed attempts, a mismatch between method and barrier, and abandonment when the boundary resists.
high_signal_anchors: Barrier-appropriate tooling — bolt cutters, an angle grinder, hydraulic tools, or a vehicle of sufficient mass to defeat this specific fence, gate, or bollard rating.
Detection neutralized during breach — sensors jammed, cameras obscured or blinded, lighting defeated, or the crossing placed in a known blind spot.
Clean, rapid defeat — the boundary is overcome quickly and quietly, consistent with prior rehearsal or professional skill.
Vehicle employed against a rated barrier — a ram or forced-gate approach using a vehicle selected for mass and approach speed.
Coordinated breach — more than one actor working the boundary in defined roles: cut, cover, and carry.
Counter-response readiness — the actor anticipates and defeats the guard-response path, timing the breach against known reaction times.
low_signal_anchors: Method-barrier mismatch — hand tools attempted against a crash-rated or anti-cut barrier, making no progress.
Noisy or failed attempt — the breach was abandoned after triggering alarms or drawing attention.
No detection defeat — the actor made no effort to counter cameras or sensors and was captured cleanly.
Single unaided actor against a hardened boundary — no coordination, no vehicle, no specialized tools.
Abandonment on first resistance — the actor withdrew when the barrier held or a patrol appeared.
Opportunistic entry through an open point — no barrier was defeated; the actor exploited a gate someone else left open.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when boundary defeat is deliberate, directed at the controlled side, concealed to preserve the pathway, and continuous with an approach toward the objective. Intent falls with accidental contact, a crossing that does not progress inward, and a verifiable lawful reason to cross the boundary.
high_signal_anchors: Deliberate defeat of a marked, secured boundary — the actor crossed a clearly controlled perimeter, not an ambiguous property line.
Inward progression after the breach — the actor continued toward the building or a sensitive area rather than stopping at the fence.
Concealment of the breach — the cut hidden, the gate re-closed, or the entry point disguised to delay discovery and preserve the pathway.
Breach timed to a vulnerable window — occupancy, shift-change, or event timing indicates a purposeful crossing.
Materiel carried across the boundary — the actor brought tools, accelerant, a device, or a weapon through the breach.
Pre-breach probing of the same segment — earlier testing of the boundary shows the defeat was planned, not spontaneous.
low_signal_anchors: Accidental or incidental contact — someone brushed or crossed the boundary without apparent purpose and did not proceed.
No inward progression — the actor stopped at, or immediately returned from, the boundary.
Verifiable lawful crossing — a contractor, utility worker, or authorized party with a legitimate reason and credentials.
Recreational trespass pattern — location and behavior fit shortcut-taking, thrill-seeking, or juvenile trespass without further objective.
No concealment or materiel — the crossing was open, empty-handed, and made no effort to preserve a pathway.
Immediate compliance when challenged — the person left or identified themselves cooperatively on first contact.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the perimeter has exploitable gaps, response is slow or absent, the actor can reach the boundary during a low-security window, and the breach yields onward access to the objective. Opportunity falls when the boundary is hardened in depth, response is fast and confirmed, the actor's method is blocked, and any reduction in exposure is durable.
high_signal_anchors: Known perimeter gap — an unmonitored segment, a blind spot, a weak barrier, or a chronically unsecured gate the actor can reach.
Slow or absent response — no guard force, a long reaction time, or a response path the actor can outrun after the breach.
Reachable low-security window — the actor can be at the boundary during hours when detection and response are weakest.
Onward access from the breach — defeating the perimeter directly exposes the objective, with no effective secondary layer.
Local positioning to the boundary — the actor lives, works, or has staged near the perimeter and can approach without a major movement.
Insider knowledge of the boundary — the actor knows patrol timing, sensor placement, or gate schedules for this specific perimeter.
low_signal_anchors: Defense-in-depth beyond the boundary — a breach yields only a clear zone or a second barrier, not the objective; durable unless the layers are defeated.
Fast, confirmed response — a rapid guard or law-enforcement reaction has repeatedly interdicted approaches to this perimeter.
Method blocked by hardening — crash-rated barriers, anti-climb, or anti-cut treatment defeat the actor's known technique; sticky unless the actor re-equips.
No reachable low-security window — the perimeter is continuously monitored and staffed, leaving no soft time.
Positional distance not closed — the actor is remote and has not staged near the boundary.
Durable posture upgrade — a recent, sustained perimeter improvement removed the gap the actor relied on.

false_positive_context.criteria: Boundary crossings and perimeter alarms are among the noisiest security signals — wildlife, weather, maintenance, delivery error, and ordinary trespass all resemble a breach. What separates a false positive is a verifiable lawful purpose, an accountable identity, an innocent physical cause, or the absence of any inward progression or carried materiel.
contexts: Authorized crossing — maintenance, grounds, utility, or delivery personnel with legitimate business at the boundary; contractors holding gate access.
Innocent physical cause — wildlife, wind-blown debris, vegetation, or weather triggering a perimeter sensor with no human agent.
Ordinary trespass — shortcut-takers, foragers, photographers, or juveniles crossing a boundary without further objective and complying when challenged.
Emergency or mistaken entry — a lost driver, a stranded motorist, or a person seeking help who crossed a boundary in good faith.
Authorized testing — security staff, red-team assessors, or law enforcement conducting a sanctioned perimeter penetration test.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: A confirmed perimeter breach is a mobilization-phase event and is treated as presumptively urgent until resolved — it sits far closer to execution than any target-development indicator. Tier-determination depends on three factors: confirmation of the breach, its directionality, and what the defeat exposes. An unconfirmed single-sensor alarm with an available benign cause sits at the monitoring tier pending verification. A confirmed boundary defeat with inward progression sits at the response tier and triggers immediate interdiction and actor-identification. A breach that applies force to a guard, or one timed to occupied hours, sits at the critical tier — treat it as an attack in progress, activate active-threat and mass-notification protocols, and request emergency law-enforcement response regardless of this tactic's computed weight. Breaches recurring against the same boundary segment despite implemented countermeasures indicate a committed actor and warrant a defensive-posture upgrade and law-enforcement coordination. Multiple lower-confidence perimeter indicators correlating in time or against the same segment may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single alarm warrants; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered actions: monitoring triggers verification and logging; response triggers interdiction, actor-identification, and a boundary-integrity assessment; the critical tier triggers active-threat protocols, medical readiness, and emergency response.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor tampers with or pre-stages a perimeter breach point — jamming a gate latch, pre-cutting and re-concealing a fence section, propping a boundary door, or defeating a barrier sensor to enable a later crossing
Threat actor cuts, climbs, or otherwise defeats perimeter fencing or barrier fabric to create a breach point and cross into the controlled area
Threat actor forces or rams a perimeter gate or vehicle barrier — prying, defeating the lock, or driving a vehicle through the crash beam or bollard line to open the boundary
Threat actor overpowers, assaults, or forcibly restrains a perimeter guard or gate officer to force entry through a manned boundary control point
Threat actor scales or accesses over a perimeter wall, roofline, or elevated boundary, timed to occupied hours or an event window, to enter the controlled area above ground-level defenses

countermeasures.measure: Harden the perimeter to the assessed threat: crash-rated vehicle barriers and bollards at approach vectors, anti-climb and anti-cut fencing, and rated gates that force the actor into slower, noisier defeat methods
countermeasures.limitations: Hardening rarely stops a committed actor outright; it buys detection and response time rather than denial, and rated barriers are costly to retrofit around long or irregular boundaries

countermeasures.measure: Deploy a perimeter intrusion detection system with assessment coverage — fence-mounted or buried sensors, video analytics, and lighting tied to CCTV so every alarm can be visually confirmed and located within seconds
countermeasures.limitations: Nuisance alarms from wildlife, weather, and vegetation degrade trust in the system; coverage gaps and blind spots persist on long perimeters, and detection without a response force only documents the breach

countermeasures.measure: Posture the guard force to survive and respond to a boundary assault: eliminate lone perimeter posts, provide protected gate positions and duress alarms, and rehearse a fast, layered response to a breach or officer-down event
countermeasures.limitations: Guard response cannot prevent a determined, coordinated, or armed breach at the point of contact; officer safety and use-of-force constraints limit interdiction, and staffing costs recur

countermeasures.measure: Establish defense-in-depth beyond the boundary: standoff and clear zones, secondary barriers, and layered access so that defeating the perimeter yields time and observation rather than immediate access to the objective
countermeasures.limitations: Clear zones and layered standoff require land and sightlines many sites lack; the approach slows an actor and improves detection but does not stop a breach on its own

response_protocols.trigger: Perimeter intrusion indicator reported (fence-line alarm, observed cut or climb, forced gate, or breach detected by patrol or analytics)
response_protocols.action: Verify before you commit: confirm the alarm against CCTV and a responding officer within the response window. If a boundary defeat is confirmed, dispatch to interdict, establish directionality and whether the actor progressed inward, preserve the breach point as evidence, and open or update the facility threat case. Assess boundary integrity along the affected segment and brief security leadership on posture.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Breach confirmed with inward progression, carried materiel, force applied to a person, or timing to occupied hours
response_protocols.legal_notes: Detention and use of force by guard personnel are constrained by state law and duty-of-care standards; document the observed breach and the basis for any response. Preserve the scene for law-enforcement evidentiary use.

response_protocols.trigger: Breach involving force applied to a guard or occupant, a vehicle ram of the boundary, or a confirmed crossing during occupied hours
response_protocols.action: Treat as an attack in progress. Activate active-threat protocol and site lockdown, initiate mass notification to occupants, stage medical response for any injured personnel, and request emergency law-enforcement response with a description of the breach point, actor, and last-known direction of travel. Do not treat as a routine trespass; assume the actor intends to reach an interior objective.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Actor reaches interior spaces, materiel or a weapon is confirmed, or casualties occur
response_protocols.legal_notes: Mass-notification and lockdown decisions carry liability in both directions; act on the confirmed breach and document the decision timeline. Coordinate public messaging with counsel and law enforcement to avoid compromising the response.

tactics.field_notes: Perimeter breach is the moment tradecraft becomes trespass — the first hard, physical, chargeable act and the last clean line before the actor is inside. Most real perimeters generate constant nuisance noise, so the operative discipline is fast verification: a sensor without a camera and an officer is a question, not a finding. The tells that separate an attack from a raccoon are directionality inward, concealment of the breach, materiel carried across, and continuity with an approach. The dangerous variant is a breach that goes through a person — an overpowered or assaulted guard is not a perimeter event, it is force-on-person, and it floors the assessment to critical no matter how the arithmetic reads. Hardening the boundary rarely stops a committed actor outright; it buys detection and response time, which is the currency that actually matters once someone is at the fence.
observed_contexts: forced vehicle-gate entry at a fenced facility during off-hours, defeated crash beam followed by movement toward the main structure
cut and concealed fence section at an unmonitored perimeter segment, discovered with tracks progressing inward toward a utility yard
coordinated activist incursion over a perimeter fence at a controlled industrial site, timed to a shift change and breaching as a group
[literature: DOD-UFC4010-2018 / GAO-19-138-2018 pattern — layered perimeter defeat and guard-force response gaps documented in facility security assessments]

tactics.name: Interior Penetration
tactics.notes: Movement through the interior of the targeted facility after the outer boundary has been defeated, advancing past internal barriers, controlled zones, and staffed checkpoints toward an interior objective. Distinct from Perimeter Breach (which defeats the outer boundary of the site) and from Position Establishment (taking up a fixed attack position). The behavior here is progression through the built interior: defeating internal doors, exploiting access control, routing around cameras and staff, and navigating corridors and stairwells to reach a specific room, floor, or space inside the place.
tactics.cpn_notes: Interior navigation is increasingly pre-loaded from digital sources — leaked or permitted floor plans, building-management and wayfinding systems, tenant directories, and cloned or credential-stuffed access badges that let an actor move through internal zones without learning the layout on site.

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises with corroboration across modalities, persistence over time, and recoverable evidence that an actor moved through the facility's interior past a controlled boundary rather than wandering a public lobby. Credibility falls when the observation is thin, when the interior space was in fact open to the public, and when a plausible legitimate presence inside the building was never ruled out.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-modal corroboration — an interior-door alarm, a badge-log anomaly, and camera capture of the same unescorted movement within overlapping timeframes.
Temporal persistence — repeated unauthorized interior movement observed across visits, not a single stray entry into a back corridor.
Material evidence — recovered interior photos, annotated floor plans, defeated interior locks, or propping devices that physically tie the actor to controlled internal space.
First-hand witness fidelity — a named staff member who saw the actor beyond a staffed checkpoint and can describe the location, direction of travel, and manner.
Behavioral specificity — the movement targeted a specific interior objective (a floor, a secured room, a plant space) rather than aimless drift.
Source motivation aligned with accuracy — captured by access-control and CCTV systems or reported through a formal security channel, not an informal secondhand account.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — a single uncorroborated report of someone 'where they shouldn't be,' reporter cannot be re-contacted.
Content-specificity weakness — presence in a semi-public interior area that dozens of visitors traverse daily.
Temporal-pattern weakness — one-time entry into an unlocked back area with no repetition or progression.
Source-motivation misalignment — reporter has a structural reason to embellish (staff dispute, tenant rivalry, disciplinary cover).
Unrebutted legitimate explanation — the interior presence admits a benign reading (lost visitor, new contractor, delivery) that investigation did not exclude.
Reconstructive memory — reporting delay long enough that the route and intent may be retrofitted to a threat narrative.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when interior movement shows operational discipline — defeating internal access control, exploiting escort and challenge gaps, routing around cameras and staffed choke points, and demonstrating prior knowledge of the building's internal layout. Capability falls with conspicuous fumbling, immediate challenge by staff, and movement that depends entirely on doors happening to be open.
high_signal_anchors: Interior access-control defeat — the actor bypasses badge readers, mantraps, or locked internal doors through cloned credentials, lock defeat, or exploitation of held-open conditions.
Route discipline — the actor moves via service corridors and stairwells that avoid staffed checkpoints and known camera coverage, indicating rehearsed or researched internal navigation.
Layout foreknowledge — the actor proceeds directly toward an interior objective without hesitation, searching, or backtracking, consistent with acquired floor plans or insider briefing.
Social-engineering fluency — the actor tailgates, uses a durable escort or contractor pretext, and defuses staff challenge without breaking stride.
Counter-surveillance behaviors inside the envelope — the actor tracks camera arcs, times patrol and cleaning cycles, and adjusts pace to blind spots within the building.
Barrier-defeat toolkit — the actor carries or improvises the means to open internal doors (bypass tools, propping devices, duplicated keys) appropriate to the facility's internal hardware.
low_signal_anchors: Conspicuous posture — the actor is visibly lost, tries locked doors at random, or lingers in staffed areas past any plausible purpose.
Immediate challenge success — staff or an escort intercepted the movement at the first controlled boundary.
Open-door dependence — all progress relied on doors that were already open; no capability to defeat a secured internal boundary was shown.
Pretext failure on contact — the actor's account of why they were inside collapsed on first questioning.
Single-modality engagement — presence without any access-control defeat, route discipline, or layout foreknowledge.
Escort-defeat absence — the actor made no attempt to evade or exploit escort and badging controls, breaching operational discipline about interior exposure.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when interior movement progresses purposefully toward a specific objective, when the actor defeats successive internal boundaries rather than stopping at the first, and when penetration is paired with stated grievance against the facility or its occupants. Intent falls with aimless presence, movement that stops when challenged, and a verifiable benign purpose for being inside.
high_signal_anchors: Behavioral progression outer-to-inner — an observable funnel from the entry point through successive controlled zones toward a defined interior objective.
Objective-specific direction of travel — movement concentrates on a particular floor, secured room, or internal space rather than sweeping the building broadly.
Operational specificity in the route — the actor selects paths that maximize concealment and minimize staff contact, indicating a considered interior plan.
Boundary-defeat persistence — the actor defeats or attempts to defeat more than one interior barrier rather than retreating after the first locked door.
Materiel carried inward — the actor advances into the interior with tools, containers, or a device consistent with acting once the objective is reached.

Hostile attribution paired with penetration — the actor has expressed grievance toward the facility or its occupants AND is observed moving through its controlled interior; the combination is intent-diagnostic in a way no single indicator captures.
low_signal_anchors: Aimless-presence behavior — interior movement with no consistent direction or objective.
Challenge-terminated movement — the actor stopped, complied, and left when questioned, with no attempt to resume.
Verifiable legitimate purpose — a contractor, delivery, employment, or visitor relationship surfaces and checks out.
No-progression pattern — the actor entered a single interior area and did not attempt any further boundary.
Objective ambiguity — movement touches several unrelated interior areas without narrowing to one.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the actor can move through the interior at will — combining knowledge of internal layout and access schemes, exploited escort and challenge gaps, insider-enabled interior access, and timing that puts them inside during low-supervision windows. Opportunity falls with layered internal access control, active escort enforcement, and compartmentalization that contains movement; when opportunity appears reduced, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: No interior friction encountered — the actor progresses through internal zones unimpeded despite the facility's access controls and staffing.

Internal pattern-of-life mastery — the actor reliably knows staffing of interior checkpoints, cleaning and patrol cycles, and which internal doors are habitually held open. The informational dimension of opportunity.
Interior security-gap knowledge — the actor knows camera blind spots, unmonitored stairwells, and badge-reader gaps along the internal route.

Insider connection being exploited — an identified employee, contractor, or escort the actor is actively leveraging for interior access or navigation. Dormant connections are potential, not realized; the exploitation pattern is what is high-signal.
Legitimate interior access — the actor holds a role, badge, or escort relationship granting unsupervised movement through controlled internal space.
Timing alignment with low supervision — the actor is inside during after-hours, shift-change, or reduced-staffing windows when interior challenge is least likely.
low_signal_anchors: Movement contained by compartmentalization — layered internal zones actively blocked progression beyond the entry area. Durable signal: sticky unless the actor materially adapts or the zoning drops.
Institutional rule-out of insider access — access audits or escort process actively cleared the possibility, not merely failed to find it.
Structural access degradation — the actor's prior interior access pathway terminated (role ended, badge revoked, contract lapsed).
Challenge enforced without adaptation — the actor was intercepted at an interior boundary, left, and did not return or adapt. Transient: may flip if the actor adapts.
Objective behind hardened internal control — the target space sits behind access control the actor's known methods cannot defeat.
Interior posture change created barriers — new escort enforcement, re-keyed internal doors, or added interior surveillance blocks the actor's known route; transient unless sustained.

false_positive_context.criteria: Many legitimate activities resemble interior penetration on the surface — a lost visitor in a back corridor looks similar to an actor routing around staff; a new contractor moving through service areas looks similar to reconnaissance in motion. What distinguishes a false positive is whether the interior presence has a verifiable legitimate purpose, a transparent identity behind it, or institutional accountability that can be checked.
contexts: Verified professional purpose — contractors, maintenance and cleaning crews, deliveries, inspectors, and vendors with authorized interior access and service business inside the building.

Legal authority — authorized law-enforcement or regulatory activity with proper basis; security professionals conducting authorized penetration tests or interior vulnerability assessments of the facility.
Personal or community connection — employees, tenants, patrons, or congregants with legitimate familiarity with interior spaces and routine reasons to traverse them.
Non-threatening confusion — lost or disoriented visitors, first-day employees, and attendees who wandered past a poorly marked boundary without hostile intent.
Operational irregularity — staff using service corridors or stairwells during elevator outages, drills, or events, producing atypical interior movement patterns.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Interior penetration is a mobilization-stage behavior: the actor is already inside the envelope, so findings here carry less tolerance for delay than target-development signals. Interior movement correlating with staging-class behaviors elsewhere — materiel carried inward, a device or accelerant emplaced, a fixed attack position taken, or alignment with an occupancy or anniversary window — warrants immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier. Tier-determination for this tactic's findings depends on three factors: credibility of the indicator, breadth across modalities, and the depth and direction of penetration. A single low-credibility report of someone in a semi-public interior area with an available legitimate explanation sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility indicator of controlled-boundary defeat with purposeful direction of travel sits at the investigation tier. Cross-modal corroboration — access-control defeat plus camera capture plus objective-specific movement toward the same interior space — sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating as an active interior intrusion in progress. Movement that overpowers or forces past interior staff, or that continues toward a populated interior space during occupied hours, sits at the committed-actor tier and warrants immediate physical intervention and law-enforcement coordination. Multiple lower-priority indicators correlating temporally or spatially may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding warrants; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered actions: monitoring triggers logging and pattern-detection; investigation triggers actor-identification and an interior-access review; elevation triggers zone lockdown and security dispatch; the committed-actor tier triggers building lockdown, occupant protection, and urgent law-enforcement response.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor defeats an interior secured barrier — a badge-controlled door, stairwell lock, or internal gate — to progress from a public or lobby area into a controlled interior zone of the facility

Threat actor traverses the building interior via service corridors, stairwells, and back-of-house routes that avoid staffed checkpoints and known camera coverage while advancing toward an interior objective

Threat actor tailgates or piggybacks through a controlled interior access point behind an authorized person, or exploits a propped or held-open internal door, to move deeper into occupied interior space

Threat actor advances through the occupied interior toward a populated internal space — a sanctuary, trading floor, auditorium, or open office — during operating hours, revealing a crowded objective inside the building
Threat actor forces past or overpowers interior staff at a reception desk or internal checkpoint to continue toward the objective, applying direct physical force to a person during interior movement

countermeasures.measure: Layer interior access control — badge-controlled internal doors, anti-passback, and mantraps or turnstiles at sensitive interior zones — so that defeating the perimeter does not grant free interior movement
countermeasures.limitations: Costly to retrofit into existing floor plans; tailgating and held-open doors defeat readers behaviorally, and legitimate high-traffic interior flow limits how tightly zones can be locked during operating hours

countermeasures.measure: Extend CCTV coverage and analytics to interior corridors, stairwells, and choke points, with real-time alerting on unescorted movement into controlled zones and on tailgating events
countermeasures.limitations: Interior blind spots persist in stairwells and service areas; analytics generate false positives in high-traffic interiors, and detection alone does not stop a fast-moving actor without a paired response capability

countermeasures.measure: Enforce interior escort, visitor and contractor badging, and a staff challenge-culture program so unescorted or unbadged movement through controlled interior space is questioned and reported quickly
countermeasures.limitations: Effectiveness depends on staff willingness to challenge and on consistent enforcement; social-engineering pretexts and authority intimidation suppress challenge, and challenge itself can trigger a violent response from a committed actor

countermeasures.measure: Compartmentalize the building into containment zones with duress alarms and localized lockdown at interior reception and checkpoints, so a breach of one zone can be isolated and further penetration delayed
countermeasures.limitations: Lockdown can trap occupants with a hostile actor if not paired with protected egress; life-safety codes constrain how interior egress may be secured, and compartmentalization delays rather than defeats a determined actor

response_protocols.trigger: Active interior intrusion detected — unescorted movement into a controlled zone, an interior-door alarm, a tailgating event, or a report of someone forcing past interior staff
response_protocols.action: Treat as an intrusion in progress. Lock down the affected zone and adjacent zones, dispatch security to interdict and deny further progression, account for and protect occupants along the actor's likely path, and initiate law-enforcement response if force against staff or a weapon is indicated. Preserve access-control and CCTV records. Do not rely on challenge alone against a committed actor.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Actor applies force to a person, is armed, carries materiel inward, or continues toward a populated interior space despite lockdown
response_protocols.legal_notes: Use-of-force and detention by facility staff or contract security is governed by jurisdiction-specific law; lockdown must preserve protected egress under life-safety codes. Document the threat basis and the decision timeline to support proportionality.

response_protocols.trigger: Post-incident review or credible signal that an actor has interior-layout knowledge or insider-enabled interior access to the facility
response_protocols.action: Audit interior access logs and badge assignments for anomalies and shared or cloned credentials, review escort and challenge compliance, reassess camera coverage of internal routes, and validate compartmentalization and lockdown readiness. Re-key or reissue credentials where compromise is suspected and brief staff on the observed interior route.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Insider facilitation is confirmed, or the same interior route or credential surfaces in another facility indicator
response_protocols.legal_notes: Investigation of an identified employee or contractor implicates employment and privacy protections that vary by jurisdiction; consult counsel and HR before adverse action and document the investigative basis.

tactics.field_notes: Interior penetration is where a plot stops looking like anything else — a person who has defeated an internal boundary and is moving with purpose toward a specific space is hard to explain benignly, and the time to intervene is short. The clearest tells are direction and discipline: an actor who moves straight for an objective without searching, who favors stairwells and service corridors over the main flow, and who defeats or tailgates through internal doors rather than stopping at the first locked one. The hardest cases are the ones that ride legitimate access inward — a real badge, a real escort, a real contractor pretext — because the boundary defeat is social, not physical, and the only signal is that the movement does not match the cover. Once an actor forces past interior staff or presses toward an occupied space, the assessment question is over and it becomes a protection problem.
observed_contexts: actor who defeated a stairwell lock and moved via back-of-house corridors to reach a secured executive floor, bypassing the staffed lobby entirely
tailgating entry behind a badged employee followed by direct movement toward an open-plan office during business hours
contractor-pretext penetration in which the actor's confident interior navigation, not a document, was what exposed prior layout knowledge
[literature: DOD-UFC4022-2017 / GAO-19-138-2018 pattern — entry-control and interior access-control gaps enabling unescorted movement into controlled facility zones]

tactics.name: Device/Materiel Emplacement
tactics.notes: Positioning the attack means — an explosive or incendiary device, an accelerant cache, or a vehicle-borne load — at or immediately adjacent to the targeted facility so that a later initiating act produces its intended effect. Distinct from Capability Acquisition (obtaining the means) and from Approach (the final movement of the actor to the site): here the means itself is brought to and placed at the objective, often ahead of the actor's return to initiate. Emplacement is a mobilization act that reveals both the method and, through where it is placed, the intended effect on the structure or its occupants.
tactics.cpn_notes: Emplacement increasingly leaves a digital and logistical trail — delivery and rideshare records, parking and access logs, and public imagery that can place a vehicle or package at the site — even when the physical placement itself is covert.

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises when the emplacement signal is corroborated across observers or sensors, when recoverable evidence — CCTV of the drop, a recovered container, a witnessed placement — physically ties the act to the site, and when the object's presence has no legitimate account. Credibility falls when the report is single-source and unverifiable, when the item admits an ordinary explanation that was never ruled out, and when the temporal record is too thin to distinguish emplacement from routine delivery.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-source corroboration — a staff report of an out-of-place item matched by CCTV of the person who left it, within an overlapping window.
Recoverable physical evidence — a recovered container, cache, or vehicle load that materially confirms an attack means was positioned at the site.
Placement inconsistent with any delivery record — the object appears with no manifest, work order, or vendor account behind it.
First-hand witness fidelity — a named observer who saw the actor position and leave the item and can describe the placement, timing, and behavior precisely.
Behavioral specificity of the drop — deliberate concealment, wiping, or positioning against a structural or occupied point rather than casual abandonment.
Sensor confirmation — a trace, canine, or screening alert on the emplaced or transported materiel corroborating the human report.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — a single anonymous report of a 'suspicious bag' that cannot be re-contacted or reviewed.
Ordinary-object ambiguity — the item is consistent with routine deliveries, lost property, or contractor materials left in normal course.
Temporal-pattern weakness — a one-time sighting with no dwell, return, or concealment behavior around it.
Reconstructive memory — reporting delayed long enough that placement details may be retrofitted to a threat narrative.
Unrebutted legitimate account — a vendor, tenant, or maintenance explanation for the object surfaces and was not excluded.
Source-motivation misalignment — the reporter has a dispute with the tenant, vendor, or facility that could color the report.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when emplacement shows operational discipline — covert transport, correct positioning against structural or occupancy-critical points, concealment that defeats casual discovery, and the sequencing to return and complete the act. Capability falls when the placement is clumsy or conspicuous, when the object is misplaced relative to any damage logic, and when the actor is discovered on first contact.
high_signal_anchors: Covert transport tradecraft — the attack means reached the site without triggering screening, using concealment, timing, or a cover delivery.
Correct placement logic — positioning against a load-bearing element, occupied space, or high-throughput node consistent with maximizing effect.
Concealment that defeats casual discovery — the item is hidden, disguised as ordinary property, or placed where routine sweeps miss it.
Coordinated sequencing — transport, placement, and a planned return to complete the act observed as a disciplined progression.
Standoff exploitation — a vehicle or load positioned to exploit the site's minimum standoff and structural geometry.
Demonstrated materiel literacy — handling and positioning consistent with understanding how the means produces its intended effect.
low_signal_anchors: Conspicuous placement — the object is left in the open, in an obviously wrong spot, or with no attempt at concealment.
Discovery on first contact — staff or security identified the item immediately as out of place.
Transport failure — the means was intercepted at screening or could not be moved to the intended position.
Incoherent placement — the object's location bears no relationship to any plausible damage or casualty logic.
Single-attempt fragility — a lone, unrehearsed placement with no fallback and no evidence of a return plan.
Exposure-breaching behavior — the actor engaged staff or lingered in a way that broke operational discipline about the placement.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when the act crosses from possessing a means to positioning it against the site — placement at an occupied or structural point, concealment for later initiation, and a return to arm or verify. Intent falls when the object's presence is explained by legitimate business, when placement is casual and unlinked to the site's vulnerabilities, and when no follow-through is observed.
high_signal_anchors: Positioning against the objective — the means is placed at the specific structural, utility, or occupancy point whose compromise accomplishes the attack.
Concealment for later initiation — the item is hidden or disguised in a way that only makes sense if it is meant to remain until an initiating act.
Return-to-complete behavior — the actor comes back to arm, connect, verify, or reposition the emplaced materiel.
Occupancy-aligned placement — the drop is timed or sited to coincide with the presence of people or a symbolic window.
Retention of the pathway — the actor preserves access, keys, or a route back to the emplaced means for the initiating step.
Hostile framing paired with emplacement — a grievance or claim against the site AND a positioned attack means; the pairing is intent-diagnostic beyond either alone.
low_signal_anchors: Legitimate-business account — the object is a delivery, contractor material, or tenant property with a verifiable purpose.
Casual abandonment — placement shows no relationship to the site's vulnerabilities or occupancy.
No follow-through — the item appears once and is neither returned to, armed, nor referenced.
Target ambiguity — the object could relate to any of several nearby premises, not this site as the objective.
Recoverable innocent intent — the actor's identity and purpose surface and check out.
No retained access — the actor kept no route, key, or means to return and complete.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the actor can place and later reach the means — access to the emplacement point, mastery of the site's screening gaps and sweep intervals, insider facilitation, and the positional ability to return. Opportunity falls when screening or standoff blocks placement, when discovery routines find the item, and when access to return is cut; when opportunity drops, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: Unimpeded placement — the actor reached the emplacement point and left the means without encountering friction.
Screening- and sweep-gap mastery — the actor knows the delivery windows, unscreened routes, and sweep intervals that let materiel sit undetected.
Standoff availability — a vehicle or load can be positioned within damaging distance of the occupied structure.
Insider facilitation — an employee, vendor, or contractor relationship is being used to move or position the means past controls.
Retained return access — the actor holds a role, key, or route that permits coming back to arm or verify.
Geographic-temporal proximity — the actor is present during the site's vulnerable delivery, service, or low-security windows.
low_signal_anchors: Placement defeated by screening or standoff — controls actively blocked positioning the means. Durable unless the actor adapts or the controls drop.
Discovery-routine interception — sweeps, canine, or staff protocols found or would find the item. Sticky while maintained.
Standoff enforced — bollards, controlled zones, or no-park buffers keep any vehicle load outside damaging distance.
Insider pathway ruled out — access audits actively cleared facilitation rather than merely failing to find it.
Return access severed — the actor's role, key, or route to come back terminated.
Positional distance not closed — the actor is not present during the site's vulnerable windows and has not staged to be.

false_positive_context.criteria: Unattended items and parked vehicles are overwhelmingly innocent — lost property, routine deliveries, contractor caches, and ordinary parking vastly outnumber emplacements. What distinguishes a false positive is a verifiable account for the object's presence, a transparent identity behind it, and consistency with the site's normal logistics rather than its vulnerabilities.
contexts: Routine logistics — scheduled deliveries, mail and parcel drops, vendor restocking, and waste pickup that leave items or vehicles in normal course.
Construction and maintenance — contractor materials, tool caches, staged equipment, and work vehicles tied to permitted work at the site.
Ordinary parking and drop-off — visitors, rideshare, and loading activity in designated zones consistent with the facility's use.
Lost and left property — bags, packages, and personal items misplaced by staff, tenants, or the public.
Authorized activity — law-enforcement, security, or emergency-services staging and equipment placement under proper authority.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Emplacement is among the last observable acts before initiation; a credible indicator that an attack means has been positioned at or near the site is treated as an imminent-threat condition, not a monitoring matter. Tier-determination rests on three factors: credibility that an actual means was placed, the specificity of the placement against the site's structural or occupancy-critical points, and evidence of a plan to return and initiate. A suspected unattended item with an available legitimate account and no corroboration sits at the investigation tier pending render-safe assessment. A corroborated placement at a structural, standoff, or occupied point — or a sensor or canine confirmation — sits at the imminent tier and triggers isolation, standoff evacuation, and EOD and law-enforcement notification without delay; the object is not to be handled. Cross-signal correlation — a positioned means together with staging, rehearsal, or an occupancy-window alignment for the same site — sits at the committed-actor tier and warrants treating the site as under active attack preparation. Tier-triggered actions: investigation triggers area isolation, CCTV reconstruction of the placement, and screening of the object by qualified personnel; the imminent tier triggers evacuation to standoff, EOD and fire coordination, and law-enforcement response; the committed-actor tier triggers full protective activation and a search for additional emplaced means. A confirmed actor matching a known threat-actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor transports the attack means — a device, accelerant containers, or a vehicle-borne load — toward the targeted facility, moving it from a cache or acquisition point to the site
Threat actor positions or conceals a device or attack materiel at or against a load-bearing element, occupied space, or high-throughput node of the site, sited to maximize effect
Threat actor pre-stages accelerant, incendiary, or precursor materials in a concealed cache at or near the site for later use
Threat actor parks or abandons a vehicle at a standoff-critical location — loading dock, drop-off lane, or point adjacent to the structure — inconsistent with legitimate use or any delivery window
Threat actor returns to an emplaced means to arm, connect, verify, or reposition it — a final placement act immediately preceding an intended initiation

countermeasures.measure: Deploy explosive- and incendiary-detection screening at delivery, dock, mailroom, and access points — trace detection, canine sweeps, and package screening — to catch transported or emplaced materiel before it is positioned
countermeasures.limitations: Screening covers defined entry paths; materiel introduced through unscreened routes, insider facilitation, or perimeter placement can bypass it, and canine and trace coverage is intermittent rather than continuous

countermeasures.measure: Establish and enforce vehicle standoff — bollards, controlled loading zones, and no-park buffers — so a vehicle-borne load cannot be positioned within damaging distance of the occupied structure
countermeasures.limitations: Standoff is constrained by site geometry, streetscape, and access needs; achievable distance may be limited, and barriers must be rated to the credible vehicle threat to be effective

countermeasures.measure: Institute unattended-item and abandoned-vehicle protocols — staff reporting, defined sweep intervals, and rapid CCTV review of dwell and drop behavior in occupied and standoff-critical areas
countermeasures.limitations: Depends on staff vigilance and reporting discipline; high false-positive volume can dull response, and concealed or disguised placements may defeat visual sweeps

countermeasures.measure: Maintain render-safe, EOD, and evacuation coordination so a suspected emplaced device triggers immediate isolation, standoff clearance, and bomb-squad and fire response without the object being handled
countermeasures.limitations: Reduces consequence rather than preventing emplacement; effectiveness depends on response time, evacuation route capacity, and pre-established liaison with EOD and fire services

response_protocols.trigger: Credible indicator that an attack means has been positioned at or near the site — a suspected device or unattended item at a structural or occupied point, a concealed accelerant cache, or an abandoned vehicle at a standoff-critical location
response_protocols.action: Treat as a live threat. Do NOT handle or move the object. Isolate the area and evacuate to standoff distance per bomb-threat protocol; establish a cordon; notify EOD/bomb squad, law enforcement, and fire. Reconstruct the placement from CCTV to identify the actor and any accomplices, and initiate a search for additional emplaced means. Document all sourcing and the timeline.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Sensor, canine, or EOD confirmation of a live device; an identified actor with retained return access; or emplacement correlating with rehearsal, staging, or an occupancy-window alignment for the same site
response_protocols.legal_notes: Evacuation, cordon, and render-safe actions engage law-enforcement and EOD authority; preserve the scene and chain of custody for any recovered materiel, and document the threat basis for evacuation decisions.

response_protocols.trigger: Pre-staging or transport indicators without a confirmed positioned device — a suspected cache, materiel observed moving toward the site, or a screening or canine alert not yet resolved
response_protocols.action: Secure and monitor the suspect area without disturbing it; hold qualified personnel for screening. Review access, delivery, parking, and CCTV records to establish the object's account and the responsible party. Coordinate with law enforcement on identification, and prepare to escalate to full isolation if a device is confirmed or the account cannot be resolved.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Screening or investigation confirms an attack means, the object's presence cannot be legitimately accounted for, or the actor returns to the cache
response_protocols.legal_notes: Detaining an object or reviewing logs must rest on articulable suspicion; document the investigative basis, and involve law enforcement before any interdiction of a suspected actor.

tactics.field_notes: Emplacement is the point where a plot stops being expressive and becomes physical: the means is at the site. The reliable tells are an object or vehicle that does not fit the site's normal logistics — present with no manifest, positioned against a load-bearing element or an occupied space rather than in a delivery lane, concealed or disguised, and often followed by the actor's return to arm or verify. The hard part is base rates: unattended items and parked vehicles are almost always innocent, so the discriminators are placement logic (does the location match a damage or casualty objective?) and account (is there a verifiable, transparent reason for the object to be there?). Because this act is so late, the response posture is isolation and standoff first, investigation second — the item is treated as live until cleared.
observed_contexts: incendiary cache pre-staged in a stairwell of a targeted building days before an intended ignition
vehicle left running and abandoned in a building's drop-off lane outside any delivery window, prompting evacuation
actor observed returning after hours to reposition a concealed package against an interior load-bearing column
[literature: ATF-EIR-2024 / FEMA-426-2011 pattern — device placement against structural and standoff-critical points to maximize effect]

tactics.name: Position Establishment
tactics.notes: Taking up an attack position at or near the targeted facility — a firing point, overwatch, standoff location, vehicle staging spot, or a position covering an entrance or egress choke point — from which the actor intends to initiate action against the site. Distinct from Approach (the final movement to the site) and from Device/Materiel Emplacement (placing the attack means): here the actor positions their own body or platform to command the target, having selected the ground that best exploits sightlines, standoff, cover, and the site's occupancy geometry. Position establishment is a late-mobilization act: the actor has moved from studying the place to occupying the piece of ground from which the attack is meant to be launched.
tactics.cpn_notes: Attack positions are increasingly selected online before any physical occupation — satellite and street-level imagery, elevation data, and published site plans let an actor identify elevated vantage points, unobstructed lines of fire, vehicle staging spots, and egress choke points remotely, so the physical position-taking may be the first observable step of a decision already made against the site.

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises with corroboration across modalities, persistence of the positioning behavior over time, and recoverable evidence that the actor has occupied ground against a specific site in an attack-consistent way. Credibility falls when the source, the observation, or the temporal pattern is thin, and when a plausible legitimate reason for a person or vehicle to be in that location was never ruled out.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-modal corroboration — a static position, a staged vehicle, and prior grievance or reconnaissance against the same site converge within overlapping timeframes.
Temporal persistence — the same attack-consistent position observed across repeated occasions rather than a single sighting.
Material evidence — recovered range cards, marked sightline photos, GPS points, or annotated imagery that physically tie the actor to a chosen firing point or standoff location.
First-hand witness fidelity — a named observer who saw the actor take up and hold a position commanding the site, with high-resolution detail on location, orientation, and duration.
Behavioral specificity — the position commands a specific entrance, occupied area, or approach lane rather than being a generic vantage on the neighborhood.
Source motivation aligned with accuracy — a trained guard or reporting employee through a formal channel, not an informal tip with a competing agenda.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — single anonymous report of a person 'standing around,' reporter cannot be re-contacted.
Content-specificity weakness — a vague sense that someone lingered, with no read on sightlines, orientation, or what the position commands.
Temporal-pattern weakness — one-time presence with no repetition and no other mobilization signal.
Source-motivation misalignment — reporter has a structural reason to embellish (parking dispute, tenant rivalry, personal conflict with the individual).
Unrebutted legitimate explanation — the position admits a benign reading (rideshare wait, delivery staging, smoke break, photography) that investigation did not exclude.
Reconstructive memory — reporting delay long enough that the position's significance may be retrofitted to a threat narrative.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when the actor's positioning shows tactical literacy — ground chosen for genuine advantage in sightline, standoff, cover, and escape; disciplined concealment; and coordination with staged means. Capability falls when the position is tactically naive, conspicuous, or unsupported by any observed means to exploit it.
high_signal_anchors: Tactical ground selection — the position exploits a real advantage: elevation, unobstructed line of fire, standoff beyond the site's response reach, or command of a choke point.
Concealment discipline — the actor uses cover, a vegetation line, a vehicle, or a structure to occupy the position without drawing attention.
Coordination with means — the position is co-located with or oriented to staged materiel, a device, or a vehicle already positioned for the attack.
Range and orientation work — observed ranging, sightline checks, or adjustments consistent with preparing a firing solution rather than idle waiting.
Escape-route integration — the position is chosen with a departure lane, showing the actor plans beyond the initiation point.
Counter-surveillance during occupation — the actor watches for guards and cameras while holding the position, varying posture to avoid detection.
low_signal_anchors: Tactically naive placement — the position offers no real sightline, standoff, or cover advantage over the site.
Conspicuous occupation — obvious loitering in the open, orientation and attention that immediately read as out of place.
No observed means — positioning with nothing staged, carried, or reachable that would let the actor exploit the ground.
Single-modality presence — a static individual with no correlating vehicle, materiel, or prior-recon signal.
Position abandoned on first friction — the actor left the moment staff or a patrol took notice, with no return or adaptation.
Direct-contact behavior — the actor engaged staff from the position, breaching the concealment a genuine attack posture requires.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when occupation of the position is deliberate, held, and oriented to the site's people or function, and when it pairs with prior grievance or reconnaissance against the place. Intent falls with transient or ambiguous presence, positions that do not command anything, and a verifiable benign purpose for being there.
high_signal_anchors: Deliberate occupation and hold — the actor takes a position and remains, orienting to the site rather than passing through.
Command of people or function — the position covers occupied areas, a busy entrance, or a critical node, indicating the objective is the site's occupants or operation.
Timing to occupancy — the position is taken during opening, shift-change, service, or event hours when the site is populated.

Pairing with prior signal — the actor who now holds an attack position has previously expressed grievance toward or surveilled this specific site; the combination is intent-diagnostic in a way neither is alone.
Rehearsal-to-position continuity — the position matches ground the actor previously walked, timed, or dry-ran against the site.
Readiness posture — sightline checks, ranging, cover adjustment, or watching the entrance in a way inconsistent with any waiting purpose.
low_signal_anchors: Transient presence — the actor passes through the vantage without holding or orienting to the site.
Position commands nothing — the vantage does not overlook the site's people, entrances, or critical points.
Verifiable legitimate purpose — rideshare, delivery, service call, employment, or a documented appointment surfaces and checks out.
Off-hours occupation — presence during closed or unpopulated periods with no other mobilization signal.
Ambiguous orientation — attention is not fixed on the site; the person is plausibly waiting for or watching something else.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the actor can actually occupy commanding ground against the site — reachable vantage points, exploitable standoff, an insider-enabled or unsecured position, and freedom to hold it undetected. Opportunity falls with hardened approaches, denied vantage, positions defeated by defensive friction, or ground the actor cannot reach or hold; when opportunity appears reduced, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: Commanding ground available — an elevated vantage, standoff line, or entrance-covering position exists and is reachable for the actor.
Undefended vantage — the position sits outside camera coverage, patrol routes, or access control and can be held unobserved.
Standoff beyond response reach — the position lets the actor command the site from a distance the facility's security cannot quickly close.
Insider-enabled positioning — an employee, contractor, or vendor relationship gives the actor access to interior or restricted ground from which to establish a position.
Geographic-temporal proximity — the actor is present at the site's vulnerable window and able to occupy the position when it matters.
Freedom to hold — no defensive friction interrupts the occupation; the actor can establish and maintain the position at will.
low_signal_anchors: Vantage denied by design — sightlines, standoff spots, and overwatch positions are already blocked by landscaping, glazing, or barriers. Durable signal: sticky unless the environment changes.
Position covered by surveillance — cameras or patrols command the ground the actor would need, and challenged the occupation. Transient: may flip if the actor finds uncovered ground.
Standoff eliminated — controlled perimeter and setback deny any position within effective reach of the site.
Institutional rule-out of insider-enabled access — audits or process actively cleared interior positioning, not merely failed to find it.
Position abandoned under friction without adaptation — the actor left after being challenged and did not return or relocate. Transient: may flip if the actor adapts.
Ground not reachable — the commanding positions require access or proximity the actor has not achieved and no path toward is observed.

false_positive_context.criteria: Many legitimate activities resemble position establishment on the surface — a rideshare driver idling with a view of an entrance looks similar to overwatch; a photographer on high ground looks similar to a firing-point survey; a parked delivery vehicle looks similar to a staged platform. What distinguishes a false positive is whether the presence has a verifiable legitimate purpose, a transparent identity behind it, or an orientation and behavior inconsistent with an attack posture.
contexts: Transportation and delivery — rideshare and taxi drivers staging near entrances, delivery and courier vehicles waiting for pickups, service vehicles parked for a job.
Verified professional purpose — surveyors, inspectors, appraisers, utility crews, and film or news crews with legitimate reason to occupy vantage points around the site.
Legal authority — authorized law-enforcement surveillance or overwatch, licensed private investigators, and security professionals conducting authorized assessments of the facility's exposure.
Non-threatening presence — smokers, phone-callers, people waiting to meet someone, birdwatchers, and photographers drawn to elevated or scenic vantage points.
Personal or community connection — employees, patrons, and neighbors habitually occupying the same spots for benign reasons.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: A person or platform established in an attack-consistent position against an occupied site is a late-mobilization signal and should be treated as time-critical, not queued. Tier-determination for this tactic's findings depends on three factors: credibility of the observation, whether the position genuinely commands the site's people or function, and correlation with other mobilization signals. A single low-credibility sighting with an available legitimate explanation sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility position that clearly commands an occupied entrance or line of fire sits at the investigation tier and warrants immediate on-site verification. A held or repeated attack position, especially one paired with a staged vehicle, staged materiel, prior rehearsal, or grievance against the site, sits at the elevation tier and should be treated as an imminent-attack indicator warranting emergency response coordination. Positions occupied during the site's occupancy window, or oriented to a crowd, choke point, or standoff line of fire, escalate the tier regardless of other factors because the collateral geometry is revealed. Multiple lower-priority positioning observations correlating temporally or spatially may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered actions: monitoring triggers logging and pattern-detection; investigation triggers on-site verification and actor-identification; elevation triggers protective action for occupants (relocation away from the commanded ground, controlled lockdown) and urgent law-enforcement coordination; a confirmed actor matching a known threat-actor profile at any tier warrants emergency response activation.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor takes up and holds a concealed static position with sightlines to a facility entrance or approach lane, orienting to the site in a manner consistent with overwatch rather than transient presence
Threat actor establishes a standoff firing position — elevated vantage, vehicle, or vegetation line — offering an unobstructed line of fire into occupied areas of the site during populated hours
Threat actor stages a vehicle in a position enabling a ramming run or covering a departure route, oriented to the site's pedestrian flow or a crowded approach
Threat actor occupies a position covering the facility's primary egress or a pedestrian choke point, timed to occupied hours, consistent with an intent to trap or channel occupants

Threat actor pre-positions at the site during its opening or occupancy window and lingers in a readiness posture — checking sightlines, ranging distances, adjusting cover — inconsistent with any legitimate wait

countermeasures.measure: Train guards and staff to recognize and report attack-consistent positioning — static individuals holding sightlines to entrances, vehicles staged oddly against pedestrian flow, and readiness behaviors such as ranging or persistent orientation to the site
countermeasures.limitations: Depends on staff vigilance and reporting discipline; a well-concealed or standoff position may never enter staff view, and legitimate waiting behavior generates false positives

countermeasures.measure: Deny commanding ground through environmental design — manage sightlines with landscaping and screening, apply protective glazing, eliminate elevated vantage points and cover near occupied areas, and remove standoff firing positions
countermeasures.limitations: Cannot eliminate every external vantage, especially against long-standoff positions on adjacent property; reduces rather than removes commanding ground

countermeasures.measure: Extend camera coverage and video analytics to approaches, elevated vantage points, and parking oriented to pedestrian flow, with loitering and static-object detection to flag persistent positioning
countermeasures.limitations: Analytics generate false positives from legitimate waiting; coverage gaps and long-standoff positions on adjacent property may fall outside the camera field

countermeasures.measure: Establish vehicle standoff and access control around pedestrian zones — bollards and hostile-vehicle-mitigation barriers, controlled and monitored parking, and setback — to deny ram-staging and vehicle firing positions
countermeasures.limitations: Capital-intensive and constrained by site geometry and public right-of-way; protects designed approaches but cannot cover every improvised staging position

response_protocols.trigger: Report of a person or vehicle established in an attack-consistent position against an occupied site — holding sightlines to an entrance, occupying a standoff or firing vantage, staging for a ram, or covering an egress choke point
response_protocols.action: Treat as time-critical.
