response_protocols.trigger: Active ignition or an established fire observed against an occupied facility (fire applied to the structure, incendiary introduced into an occupied space, or multiple points of origin while people are inside)
response_protocols.action: Execute life-safety response immediately: activate the fire alarm and suppression, initiate evacuation along maintained egress, account for occupants at a muster point, and call emergency services. Report to responding fire and law enforcement that the fire is believed deliberate, note observed points of origin and any accelerant or blocked-egress indicators, and preserve scene and imagery for investigation once life-safety is secured.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Blocked egress, multiple points of origin, occupants unaccounted for, or an identified actor still on scene
response_protocols.legal_notes: Life-safety authority is immediate and unambiguous; preserve the scene and evidence to the extent it does not delay rescue. Coordinate origin-and-cause determination with the fire marshal and law enforcement; document all observations for arson investigation.

response_protocols.trigger: Precursor observed — staged accelerant or a readied ignition source at the site, a credible imminent incendiary signal, or a fire set against an unoccupied structure
response_protocols.action: Intercept and harden before force is applied where possible: dispatch response to the staging point, deny access to ignition-vulnerable areas, notify law enforcement, and elevate fire watch and evacuation readiness for the exposure window. For an unoccupied-structure fire, activate suppression and emergency services, confirm no occupants are present, and treat origin as deliberate pending determination.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Ignition begins, the site is or becomes occupied, or the actor reaches an interior or egress point
response_protocols.legal_notes: Interception of a staged incendiary act may involve detention and evidence handling; coordinate with law enforcement and document the observed basis. Preserve staged materials as evidence for arson investigation.

tactics.field_notes: An incendiary attack is one of the few facility tactics a defender may actually witness in progress, and the single fact that decides everything is whether the place is occupied. Fire against an occupied site is a mass-casualty method — it spreads, it blocks escape, and it defeats response — so it floors to critical regardless of what the arithmetic says. The tells that separate an attack from an accident are physical and observable: more than one point of origin, a spread pattern faster and hotter than the building alone would burn, ignition at or blocking of the exits, and a light set where nothing accidental could have started it. Precursors are catchable — accelerant staged against a wall, an ignition source readied at a service door — and that narrow window before force is applied is where interception is possible. A fire set when the building is empty is a serious property attack but not, by itself, a casualty event; the occupancy fact, not the flame, sets the tier.
observed_contexts: occupied clinic set alight during operating hours, with fire applied at the entrance and the primary egress path while patients and staff were inside
accelerant containers staged against the ground-floor facade of an occupied building and an ignition source readied, interrupted before the fire took hold
after-hours fire set to an unoccupied place of worship, multiple points of origin found, no occupants present at the time of ignition
[literature: ATF-AIR-2023 / NFPA-INTENTIONAL-2021 pattern — intentionally set structure fires with multiple points of origin and accelerant-consistent spread against occupied and symbolic facilities]

tactics.name: Explosive Attack
tactics.notes: Detonation of an explosive device against, inside, or immediately adjacent to a facility to destroy the structure, kill or injure its occupants, and deny use of the site. This tactic is authored at detection-indicator altitude only: it describes what a defender observes — device emplacement, vehicle-borne emplacement, initiation behavior at scene, the detonation itself, and secondary-device patterns — not device construction, formulation, quantities, or method. Explosive is a mass method: against an occupied or public facility it reveals a population target and carries a casualty floor. Distinct from Incendiary Attack (fire/accelerant) and Structural Sabotage (attacking load-bearing integrity by non-blast means), though blast may be used to achieve structural collapse.
tactics.cpn_notes: Explosive execution against a facility is increasingly telegraphed by immediate-precursor digital and physical signals — a package or vehicle left in a no-standoff position captured on CCTV, a claim or countdown posted to a channel, or an actor observed clearing and taking cover before a blast. These converge in the final minutes to hours and are the last window for interdiction.

credibility.criteria: In execution, credibility is established less by inference and more by direct observation — a device or suspected device is present, a detonation occurred, or trained witnesses saw emplacement and initiation. Credibility rises with physical evidence at scene, sensor and CCTV capture, and consistent multi-witness accounts. It falls when the report is a claim without corroborating physical or sensor signal, when the object's nature is ambiguous, or when a benign explanation for an unattended item was never excluded.
high_signal_anchors: Physical evidence at scene — an emplaced device, suspected device, or post-blast signature (over-pressure damage, fragmentation pattern, seat of blast) present and documented.
Sensor and CCTV capture — camera footage of emplacement or the detonation, alarm activation, or acoustic and seismic signal consistent with a blast.
Multi-witness convergence — independent occupants or staff describe the same emplacement, actor, or blast with consistent timing and location.
First-responder confirmation — EOD, fire, or law-enforcement personnel on scene confirm a device or a detonation rather than a suspected item.
Behavioral specificity at scene — the actor was observed positioning an item against an occupied area or structural support and then departing.
Corroborated claim — a communicated claim or countdown that names the site and matches an observed device, timing, or blast.
low_signal_anchors: Uncorroborated claim — a threat or claim of a device with no physical, sensor, or witness signal to support it.
Object ambiguity — an unattended item whose nature is genuinely unclear and admits a routine explanation.
Single distant witness — one remote report of a sound or object that cannot be re-contacted or localized.
Benign explanation unexcluded — a package, vehicle, or contractor activity with a plausible legitimate basis that was not ruled out.
Reconstructive account — a witness statement given after significant delay, with details that may be retrofitted to a blast narrative.
Source-motivation misalignment — the reporter has a structural reason to raise a false alarm (dispute, hoax pattern, prior false reports).

capability.criteria: In the explosive execution window, capability is demonstrated by the physical presence of a functioning or credible device and by the discipline of its emplacement and initiation. Capability rises with evidence of a working initiation method, defeat of standoff, deliberate placement for maximum effect, and secondary-device or anti-handling behavior. It falls with non-functioning or hoax items, conspicuous fumbling, and emplacement that ignores the site's protective geometry.
high_signal_anchors: Functioning device confirmed — the item is assessed by responders as a viable device rather than a hoax or inert replica.
Standoff defeated — the actor placed the device inside standoff, against the structure, or in an interior occupied space, negating the site's protective distance.
Deliberate effect placement — positioning against a load-bearing element, in a chokepoint, or amid maximum occupancy indicates effect-seeking placement.
Initiation discipline observed — an actor takes cover, controls a hand-held initiator, or times initiation to occupancy, indicating a working method.
Secondary or anti-handling behavior — a second suspected device or emplacement along evacuation and responder routes indicates layered capability.
Vehicle-borne emplacement — a laden vehicle driven into a no-standoff position and abandoned indicates capacity for a larger-effect device.
low_signal_anchors: Hoax or inert item — responders assess the object as non-functioning, a replica, or a claim with no device.
Conspicuous, undisciplined behavior — the actor fumbles emplacement in the open with no concealment or timing.
Standoff not defeated — the item is left outside effective range, at a barrier, or far from occupied space.
No initiation method evident — no observed initiator, no cover-taking, no timing to occupancy.
Single low-effect item — one small item with no secondary and no placement logic.
Abandoned before completion — the actor left without emplacing or initiating.

intent.criteria: Intent in execution is expressed by the act itself and its targeting choices — timing to occupancy, placement for casualties versus property, communicated claims, and persistence through interdiction. Intent to harm people rises sharply when the device is emplaced and timed to a populated site. It falls when timing and placement deliberately avoid people, when the act reads as symbolic property destruction, or when the actor aborts on encountering occupants.
high_signal_anchors: Occupancy timing — emplacement or initiation timed to peak occupancy, an event, or business hours indicates intent to harm people.
Casualty placement — the device is positioned amid people, at an entrance flow, or in an occupied interior rather than an empty perimeter.
Communicated lethal intent — a claim, countdown, or manifesto naming the site and its occupants as the objective.
Persistence through interdiction — the actor continues emplacement or initiation despite alarms, challenge, or evacuation.
Secondary targeting of responders — a second device set for those who arrive or evacuate indicates intent to maximize the toll.
Symbolic-date or grievance alignment — the act falls on an anniversary or is paired with grievance against the site or its function.
low_signal_anchors: Deliberate empty-hours timing — the act is staged when the site is verifiably unoccupied, indicating property rather than casualty intent.
Property-only placement — the device targets an unoccupied structure, sign, or perimeter with no people-effect logic.
Abort on contact with occupants — the actor withdrew upon encountering people.
No communicated people-targeting — no claim or statement directed at occupants.
Warning given — the actor issued a genuine, actionable warning intended to clear people before initiation.
Single-symbol focus — attention fixed on defacing or damaging a symbol, not on occupants.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity in execution is the actor's realized ability to reach the site and place or initiate a device against people or structure. It rises with unimpeded approach, defeated standoff, exploited access, and knowledge of occupancy windows. It falls with hardened standoff that held, access denied at the point of attack, or an evacuation that removed the population before initiation; when opportunity is reduced at the moment of attack, whether the reduction held through initiation is decisive.
high_signal_anchors: Unimpeded approach to placement — the actor reached the emplacement point without being stopped by barrier, screening, or guard.
Standoff and screening defeated — vehicle or personnel screening was bypassed, or standoff distance was closed to the structure.
Occupancy-window mastery — the actor timed the act to a known populated period, maximizing exposed people.
Exploited insider or credentialed access — a role, credential, or relationship placed the actor and device inside the protected envelope.
Geographic-temporal presence — the actor was physically present at the site during its vulnerable, occupied window.
Interior placement achieved — the device reached an occupied interior space rather than an exterior perimeter.
low_signal_anchors: Standoff held — barriers or bollards kept a vehicle or actor outside effective range at initiation. Durable if the geometry is fixed.
Screening interdicted the device — vehicle or bag screening stopped emplacement at the boundary.
Evacuation removed the population — a warning or alarm cleared occupants before initiation, collapsing the casualty opportunity.
Access denied at attack point — locked, guarded, or hardened access blocked entry to the intended placement.
Distance not closed — the actor could not physically reach the site during an occupied window.
Posture change defeated the plan — changed schedules, added screening, or active response disrupted the known method. Transient unless sustained.

false_positive_context.criteria: Execution-phase explosive indicators generate high-consequence false positives — an unattended bag, a parked delivery vehicle, or a construction concussion can all resemble the early signal of a device. What distinguishes a false positive is whether the object or event has a verifiable legitimate origin, an accountable owner, or a routine operational explanation that responders can confirm before the situation is treated as an attack.
contexts: Routine unattended property — forgotten bags, luggage, and packages with a locatable owner; lost-and-found items in transit hubs.
Legitimate deliveries and vehicles — couriers, freight, and service vehicles parked in loading zones under a verifiable manifest or schedule.
Authorized work — construction, demolition, blasting, or utility work producing concussions, debris, or staged materials under permit.
Facilities and maintenance — HVAC, generator, or pressure-vessel events producing bangs or damage with a maintenance record.
Training and exercises — scheduled EOD training, drills, or pyrotechnic events with prior notification and authorization.
Media and pyrotechnics — permitted special-effects, film, or event pyrotechnics with documented authorization.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Explosive execution collapses the assessment timeline: an emplaced or suspected device, an observed initiation behavior, or a detonation warrants immediate protective action — evacuation or shelter, standoff, and EOD and law-enforcement activation — without waiting to resolve every credibility question. Tier-determination here turns on immediacy and confirmation. An uncorroborated claim of a device with no physical or sensor signal sits at the assessment tier but still triggers a search-and-clear protocol. A confirmed suspected device or credible emplacement sits at the interdiction tier: isolate, evacuate to safe distance, and call EOD. An observed initiation behavior or a vehicle-borne emplacement in a no-standoff position sits at the imminent tier and drives immediate life-safety action. A detonation, or a placed device timed to occupancy, sits at the active-attack tier: mass-casualty response, secondary-device sweep of evacuation and responder routes, and treatment of any emplaced item as live. Any indicator that applies direct physical force to people — a detonation with occupants present — carries a critical severity floor regardless of computed weight. Secondary-device patterns targeting responders and evacuees must be assumed until cleared. A confirmed actor matching a known threat-actor profile at any tier warrants urgent law-enforcement coordination.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor places or abandons an unattended package, container, or suspected device against or inside the occupied facility, positioned near occupied areas, an entrance flow, or a structural support, then departs
Detonation of an explosive device at, inside, or against the facility while occupants are present, producing casualties and structural damage
Threat actor drives or parks a vehicle carrying a suspected device into a no-standoff position adjacent to the occupied structure and departs on foot
Threat actor at scene exhibits initiation behavior immediately before a blast — taking cover, controlling a hand-held initiator, or clearing and timing to occupancy
A second suspected device is placed along evacuation routes or responder approaches following an initial blast, indicating a layered attack on evacuees and first responders

countermeasures.measure: Enforce vehicle and personnel standoff around occupied structures using bollards, barriers, controlled setbacks, and screened access so a device cannot be brought into effective range of the building or its occupants
countermeasures.limitations: Fixed standoff is costly and constrained by site geometry; interior and pedestrian-accessible spaces may still be reachable, and insiders with credentialed access can bypass perimeter screening

countermeasures.measure: Train staff on unattended-item recognition and maintain a suspicious-package and bomb-threat protocol that isolates the item, initiates evacuation or shelter to safe distance, and activates EOD and law enforcement
countermeasures.limitations: Depends on staff attentiveness and reporting discipline; concealed or vehicle-borne devices may not present as an unattended item, and the interdiction window can be very short

countermeasures.measure: Maintain rehearsed evacuation and shelter plans with predesignated safe assembly areas selected to avoid predictable secondary-device positions, and sweep evacuation and responder routes before movement
countermeasures.limitations: Assembly areas can themselves be targeted; route sweeps take time under mass-casualty pressure, and a determined actor may anticipate standard evacuation patterns

countermeasures.measure: Harden the occupied structure against blast effects through glazing protection, progressive-collapse-resistant detailing, and protected egress so that a detonation within range produces fewer casualties
countermeasures.limitations: Structural hardening is expensive, most feasible in new construction, and reduces but does not eliminate casualties from an interior or close-in device

response_protocols.trigger: A suspected device is reported or observed at the facility, or an actor is seen emplacing an item or a vehicle in a no-standoff position
response_protocols.action: Do not approach, touch, or transmit near the item. Isolate and cordon, evacuate or shelter occupants to safe distance along a swept route, and activate EOD and law enforcement. Preserve CCTV and witness accounts of emplacement. Treat the item as live until cleared by EOD.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Initiation behavior observed, a second suspected device found, or a detonation occurs
response_protocols.legal_notes: Evacuation and cordon are within facility authority; preserve scene evidence for law enforcement and document the basis for protective actions. Do not interfere with EOD or investigative jurisdiction.

response_protocols.trigger: A detonation has occurred at the facility
response_protocols.action: Execute mass-casualty response: account for and treat occupants, and move survivors along swept routes to safe assembly areas chosen to avoid predictable secondary-device positions. Assume a secondary device targeting evacuees and responders until routes and assembly areas are cleared. Establish unified command with fire, EMS, EOD, and law enforcement; preserve the scene for investigation.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Secondary device confirmed, structural collapse risk identified, or a coordinated multi-site pattern emerges
response_protocols.legal_notes: Coordinate public messaging with law enforcement to avoid compromising the investigation; document response decisions and preserve evidence chain-of-custody for the blast scene.

tactics.field_notes: Explosive execution against a facility usually shows its hand only in the final window — an item or vehicle left where it should not be, an actor taking cover, a claim posted minutes out. Because the method is a mass method, the default assumption for an occupied or public site is a population target, and the casualty floor applies the moment a device is initiated with people present. The two hardest problems are the short interdiction window and the secondary device: attackers who intend a high toll set a second device for the people who evacuate and the responders who arrive, so evacuation routes and assembly areas are treated as part of the threat space, not the safe space. Standoff is the single most protective control against the vehicle-borne case, and unattended-item discipline is the most protective against the emplaced-package case — but both fail against a credentialed insider who carries a device inside the envelope.
observed_contexts: vehicle left in a loading zone against a no-standoff wall of an occupied building and abandoned on foot, captured on CCTV minutes before a blast
unattended package placed inside an occupied lobby near an entrance flow, recognized by trained staff who initiated evacuation before EOD arrival
secondary suspected device located along an evacuation route after an initial blast, targeting evacuees and first responders
[literature: ATF-EIR-2024 / FEMA-426-2011 pattern — vehicle-borne and placed devices against occupied and symbolic facilities, with secondary-device targeting of responders]

tactics.name: Structural Sabotage
tactics.notes: Deliberate attack on the load-bearing or structural integrity of a facility to damage, weaken, or collapse it. Distinct from Explosive Attack (which achieves structural failure through detonation) and Systems Sabotage (which targets building services rather than the frame): the objective here is the structure itself — its columns, beams, connections, foundations, bracing, and passive protection. Structural sabotage ranges from the overt (cutting a primary member) to the covert and patient (loosening moment connections, undermining a footing, stripping fireproofing) so that failure appears accidental or is deferred to a moment of maximum occupancy. When the targeted structure is occupied, a successful attack is a mass-casualty event; when the site is empty, the same act is a destructive property attack. The severity of an observed indicator therefore turns on whether people are present, not on the method alone.
tactics.cpn_notes: Structural sabotage is increasingly informed and enabled by digital exposure — building-information models, structural engineering drawings and calculations in permitting portals, and as-built documentation that reveal which members are load-bearing, where redundancy is absent, and how a progressive collapse would propagate. Structural-health-monitoring instrumentation is itself a cyber-physical target: an actor who can read or suppress that telemetry can both select the decisive member and mask the tampering until failure.

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises with corroboration across modalities, persistence over time, and recoverable evidence that a structural element has been deliberately compromised rather than degraded by age, load, or accident. Credibility falls when the finding is a single unverified report, when the observed condition admits an ordinary explanation, and when no forensic or engineering assessment has distinguished sabotage from deterioration.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-modal corroboration — physical evidence of tampering on a structural member aligns with access-log anomalies and a stated grievance against the site within overlapping timeframes.
Forensic signature of intent — tool marks, fresh cuts, removed fasteners, or defeated tamper seals that a qualified structural engineer attributes to deliberate action, not wear.
Temporal persistence — repeated unexplained access to load-bearing areas, crawlspaces, or roof structure over days to weeks rather than a single visit.
Material evidence — recovered cutting or excavation equipment, saved structural drawings, or annotated imagery physically tying an actor to the compromised element.
First-hand witness fidelity — a named witness who observed the actor working on or near a primary structural member and can describe the location, timing, and activity.
Source motivation aligned with accuracy — a structural inspector, engineer, or maintenance professional reporting through a formal channel, not an informal tip with a competing agenda.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — single anonymous report of 'damage,' reporter cannot be re-contacted or lacks the competence to distinguish sabotage from wear.
Ordinary-cause explanation unrebutted — the cracking, deflection, or corrosion admits a benign reading (age, overload, settlement, deferred maintenance) that engineering assessment did not exclude.
Content-specificity weakness — a vague claim that a building is 'unsafe' with no identified member, mechanism, or evidence of tampering.
Temporal-pattern weakness — a one-time observation with no recurrence and no access anomaly.
Source-motivation misalignment — reporter has a structural reason to embellish (tenant dispute, contractor rivalry, litigation over the building).
Reconstructive memory — reporting delay long enough that an accidental condition is retrofitted to a sabotage narrative.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when the actor demonstrates the technical literacy to identify the decisive structural element and the means to defeat it — reading engineering documents productively, obtaining cutting, drilling, or excavation tools, exploiting authorized access to structural spaces, and working covertly enough that the compromise is not caught before failure. Capability falls with conspicuous or ineffective effort, absence of tools or access, and attempts that a routine inspection would immediately catch.
high_signal_anchors: Demonstrated structural literacy — the actor reasons correctly about load paths, redundancy, and which member's failure propagates to collapse, rather than attacking a non-critical element.
Restricted-material acquisition — the actor obtains structural drawings, load calculations, or as-built documentation that identify load-bearing members and standoff-critical elements.
Tool and method fit — possession of cutting torches, saws, core drills, jacks, or excavation means matched to the structure's material and the member being attacked.
Access to structural spaces — legitimate or defeated access to columns, roof structure, mechanical penthouses, crawlspaces, or foundations where primary members are reachable.
Covert execution discipline — tampering is concealed, tamper seals are defeated cleanly, and the work is staged to defer detection until occupancy peaks.
Counter-inspection awareness — the actor times work around inspection cycles or targets members that routine inspection does not examine.
low_signal_anchors: Non-critical-element error — effort directed at a partition, cladding, or secondary member whose failure does not threaten the structure.
Tool or method mismatch — means insufficient to sever or meaningfully weaken the targeted member (hand tools against heavy steel or reinforced concrete).
No access to load-bearing areas — the actor cannot reach primary structural elements without defeating controls not yet defeated.
Conspicuous posture — visible cutting or excavation in occupied or observed areas, work abandoned when challenged.
OSINT-only reach — knowledge of the structure is public-record only; no operational reach to the members themselves.
Detection on first inspection — the tampering is crude enough that a routine walk-through would catch it before any failure.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when activity progresses from interest in the structure toward operational compromise of a specific decisive member, when the actor conceals the work to defer failure, and when structural targeting is paired with a stated grievance against the site or a desire to maximize harm. Intent falls with generic maintenance activity, encounters that do not escalate, and a verifiable legitimate purpose for working on the structure.
high_signal_anchors: Behavioral progression toward the decisive member — an observable narrowing from general structural interest to work on the specific column, connection, or footing whose failure is catastrophic.
Concealment to defer failure — the actor hides tampering, restores surface appearance, or defeats monitoring so that collapse occurs later, at chosen occupancy.
Operational specificity — selection of load-bearing members, transfer elements, or progressive-collapse-critical connections rather than incidental damage.
Occupancy alignment — the work is timed or staged to precede a period of peak occupancy or a symbolic date, revealing a casualty objective.
Retention of structural intelligence — saved drawings, marked-up plans, or notes on which member to attack, suggesting deliberate planning.

Hostile attribution paired with structural access — expressed grievance against the site combined with observed presence in or work on its load-bearing areas; the combination is intent-diagnostic in a way no single indicator captures.
low_signal_anchors: Generic maintenance activity — authorized repair, retrofit, or inspection work that touches structure for a legitimate reason.
One-time encounter without escalation — presence near structural elements that surfaced but did not recur or progress.
Verifiable legitimate purpose — contractor, engineer, or facilities role explains the structural access and checks out.
Non-decisive targeting — damage to elements whose failure is cosmetic or localized, inconsistent with a collapse objective.
No concealment or timing — activity is open and unconnected to occupancy, inconsistent with a casualty-maximizing plan.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the actor can reach and act on a decisive structural element — combining access to load-bearing spaces, knowledge of which member is critical and unmonitored, an inspection regime that would not catch the tampering, and the time to work undisturbed. Opportunity falls with hardened access to structural spaces, monitoring or inspection that would detect compromise, and structural redundancy that denies a single-point failure; when opportunity appears reduced, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: Direct access to load-bearing areas — the actor has unsupervised access to columns, roof structure, foundations, or mechanical spaces through a legitimate role or a defeated control.
Knowledge of an unmonitored critical member — the actor knows which element is decisive and that it is not instrumented, sealed, or routinely inspected.
Inspection-cycle mastery — the actor knows the structural inspection schedule and can work in the interval, or targets members inspection does not examine.
Absence of structural redundancy — the structure lacks alternate load paths, so a single compromised member yields disproportionate or progressive collapse.
Time to work undisturbed — low-occupancy or after-hours windows in the structural spaces long enough to cut, drill, or excavate.
Insider connection being exploited — an identified employee, contractor, or maintenance relationship the actor is actively leveraging for access to structural spaces or as-built documentation.
low_signal_anchors: Access to structural spaces denied — load-bearing areas, crawlspaces, and roof structure are access-controlled and the actor has not defeated the controls. Durable signal: sticky unless the actor materially adapts.
Structural-health monitoring in place — instrumentation or tamper-evident seals on critical members would reveal compromise; transient only if the actor can suppress the telemetry.
Inspection would catch it — the compromise mechanism is one a routine structural inspection examines and would detect before failure.
Redundant load paths — progressive-collapse-resistant design denies single-point failure, forcing the actor to compromise multiple members undetected.
Structural access degradation — the actor's prior access pathway to load-bearing areas terminated (role ended, contract lapsed).
Institutional rule-out of insider access — access audits or process actively cleared the possibility rather than merely failing to find it.

false_positive_context.criteria: Many legitimate activities resemble structural sabotage on the surface — a demolition contractor cutting a member, a retrofit crew drilling into a beam, or ordinary cracking from settlement can all look like an attack. What distinguishes a false positive is whether the work has a verifiable authorization, whether the responsible party is transparent and accountable, and whether an engineering assessment attributes an observed condition to a natural cause rather than deliberate action.
contexts: Authorized construction and retrofit — demolition, seismic or structural retrofit, tenant improvement, and repair crews with permits and engineering oversight cutting, coring, or shoring members by design.
Legitimate inspection and testing — structural engineers, special inspectors, and non-destructive-testing technicians examining or instrumenting members under authorized scopes.
Ordinary deterioration and distress — cracking, deflection, spalling, or corrosion from age, settlement, overload, water intrusion, or thermal movement, confirmed by assessment as non-deliberate.
Facilities and maintenance work — authorized personnel accessing crawlspaces, roof structure, and mechanical penthouses for legitimate service, some of which touches structure.
Emergency stabilization — post-event shoring, bracing, or member removal directed by responders or engineers after fire, flood, vehicle impact, or partial failure.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: A structural finding on an OCCUPIED structure — a severed or partially cut load-bearing member, an undermined footing, a defeated support system, or tampering an engineer attributes to deliberate action — is a potential mass-casualty condition and warrants immediate activation of response protocols regardless of this tactic's internal tier: evacuate, cordon, and obtain emergency structural assessment before anything else. Tier-determination for less acute findings depends on three factors: credibility of the finding, whether the compromised element is structurally decisive, and whether people are or will be present. A single low-credibility report of unexplained 'damage' with an available ordinary-cause explanation sits at the monitoring tier. A single high-credibility finding of deliberate compromise on a non-critical member, site unoccupied, sits at the investigation tier. Deliberate compromise of a decisive load-bearing member, or covert tampering staged to defer failure to an occupancy window, sits at the elevation tier and warrants treating the structure as under active attack. Any indicator confirming a compromised primary member with occupancy present sits at the committed-actor tier and triggers evacuation and structural cordon. Multiple lower-tier findings correlating temporally or spatially — access anomalies plus fresh tool marks plus a stated grievance — may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding warrants. Tier-triggered actions: monitoring triggers logging, inspection tasking, and access review; investigation triggers actor-identification and a forensic structural assessment; elevation triggers occupancy restriction and structural monitoring of the member; the committed-actor tier triggers evacuation, cordon, and law-enforcement coordination.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor observed cutting, severing, drilling through, or removing a load-bearing column, beam, or primary structural member of an occupied structure
Threat actor observed excavating, undermining, or removing lateral support beneath the foundation, footings, or slab of an occupied structure

Structural inspection discovers covert tampering with critical connections — loosened or removed anchor bolts, cut welds, defeated moment connections, or severed bracing — bearing tool marks or defeated tamper seals indicating deliberate action
Threat actor observed deliberately overloading a floor or roof beyond design capacity, or defeating a support, shoring, or retaining system, while the structure is occupied

Removal or degradation of structural fire protection — stripped fireproofing, scraped intumescent coating, or defeated passive protection on load-bearing steel — discovered on a member whose failure under heat or load would propagate collapse

countermeasures.measure: Establish a structural integrity monitoring regime — periodic engineer-led inspection of primary members, tamper-evident seals on critical connections, and structural-health-monitoring instrumentation on decisive elements with alerting on anomalous strain or movement
countermeasures.limitations: Instrumentation covers only the members chosen for it; covert tampering on an uninstrumented element, or suppression of the telemetry, defeats detection. Inspection intervals leave windows in which compromise can be staged and concealed

countermeasures.measure: Control and log access to load-bearing spaces — columns, roof structure, mechanical penthouses, crawlspaces, and foundations — with credentialed entry, escort of contractors, and review of access anomalies against maintenance schedules
countermeasures.limitations: Structural spaces are often shared with legitimate maintenance and utility access, creating cover; an insider or credentialed contractor retains authorized reach to the very members most at risk

countermeasures.measure: Design or retrofit for progressive-collapse resistance — alternate load paths, member redundancy, and structural continuity so that loss of a single element does not propagate to disproportionate collapse
countermeasures.limitations: Capital-intensive and constrained by existing construction; redundancy raises the number of members an actor must compromise but does not make sabotage impossible, and retrofit of an occupied structure is slow

countermeasures.measure: Pre-plan an emergency structural-compromise response — a standing protocol for evacuation, cordon standoff, and immediate engineer assessment triggered by any credible sign of deliberate structural damage
countermeasures.limitations: Effective only if the compromise is detected before failure; a covert attack staged to collapse without warning gives no trigger, and evacuation of a large occupied structure takes time the actor may have denied

response_protocols.trigger: Credible sign of deliberate structural compromise on an occupied structure — a cut or partially severed load-bearing member, an undermined foundation, a defeated support system, or tampering an engineer attributes to deliberate action
response_protocols.action: Treat as an imminent collapse hazard. Immediately evacuate occupants along routes that avoid the compromised member, establish a collapse-standoff cordon, and stop all loads and vibration to the structure. Obtain emergency structural-engineer assessment before re-entry. Preserve the scene and tool marks for forensic attribution. Notify law enforcement of a deliberate attack on the structure.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Engineer confirms the compromised element is decisive and failure is imminent, OR a second compromised member is identified, indicating a progressive-collapse attack
response_protocols.legal_notes: Evacuation and cordon of an occupied structure are within facility authority and are defensible on a documented engineering hazard basis. Preserve the compromised element and surrounding area as a crime scene; document chain of custody for forensic and prosecutorial use.

response_protocols.trigger: Discovery of covert structural tampering with no active collapse in progress — loosened connections, stripped fireproofing, or staged undermining found during inspection
response_protocols.action: Secure and restrict access to the affected structural area. Commission a forensic structural assessment to determine whether the element is decisive and whether other members are compromised. Restrict or reduce occupancy pending findings. Review access logs and CCTV for the tampering window, identify the responsible party, and refer for investigation.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Assessment finds the tampered element is decisive or that multiple members are compromised, OR occupancy is scheduled to rise before the structure is cleared
response_protocols.legal_notes: Access review and CCTV analysis of maintenance and contractor personnel may implicate employment and privacy considerations; document the objective structural basis for the inquiry and consult counsel before adverse action.

tactics.field_notes: Structural sabotage is the quietest of the execution tactics and the one most likely to be mistaken for an accident. The decisive move is often small — a few bolts removed from a moment connection, a footing undermined, fireproofing scraped from a column — and its consequence is deferred to whenever the structure is fullest. That deferral is the tell: an actor who conceals the work and times it to occupancy has revealed a casualty objective, not merely a property one. The hardest part for a defender is that most structural distress is ordinary — buildings crack, deflect, and corrode — so the signal only separates from the noise when an engineer can attribute the condition to deliberate action, or when tampering pairs with access anomalies and a grievance against the site. Occupancy is the severity hinge: the same cut member is a mass-casualty event with people inside and a destructive property attack with the building empty. When in doubt on an occupied structure, evacuate first and assess second.
observed_contexts: insider with maintenance access to a mechanical penthouse found to have loosened anchor bolts on a transfer connection, concealed and timed to a high-occupancy period
sabotage case where a footing was progressively undermined from an adjacent excavation framed as legitimate site work
grievance-driven actor who acquired structural drawings and marked the single column whose loss the documents showed would propagate to collapse
[literature: FEMA-426-2011 / DOD-UFC4010-2018 pattern — progressive-collapse vulnerability and standoff dependence of load-bearing members in occupied structures]

tactics.name: Systems Sabotage
tactics.notes: Deliberate attack on a facility's building systems — electrical power, HVAC and air handling, fire detection and suppression, potable and domestic water, and physical-security systems — to either disable a protective function or weaponize the system against occupants. Distinct from TF0208 (which is merely defeating a system to gain access) in that TF0304 is the sabotage act itself: the objective is the system's failure or misuse, not passage through it. The consequence spectrum ranges from denial (a blackout, a silenced alarm) to mass harm (air handling used to disperse a contaminant through an occupied building, or fire-suppression disabled immediately before an incendiary attack). Whether a given act reveals a mass-casualty objective turns on occupancy at the time and on which system is targeted — disabling life-safety before a fire, or turning air handling into a dispersal mechanism, exposes a population target in a way that disabling an exterior camera does not.
tactics.cpn_notes: Building systems are increasingly reachable online. Internet-exposed building-automation systems, HVAC and energy-management controllers, and IP-based access-control and video head-ends — many discoverable through device-search engines and running default or shared credentials — let an actor reach, map, and manipulate a facility's systems remotely, without the physical presence that older sabotage required. Vendor remote-maintenance links and flat operational-technology networks widen the reachable surface.

credibility.criteria: Credibility rises with corroboration across modalities — system telemetry, physical observation of the plant spaces, and recoverable planning material converging on the same system — with persistence over time, and with evidence that a benign fault or authorized maintenance was affirmatively ruled out. Credibility falls when a single anomalous reading stands alone, when the observation could be an ordinary equipment fault, and when a legitimate service explanation was never checked.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-modal corroboration — a supervisory trouble signal on a life-safety system, physical evidence of tampering at the panel or valve, and recovered notes about the system within overlapping timeframes.

Fault-versus-attack adjudication — a qualified technician examined the failure and found deliberate manipulation (bypassed interlock, closed and chained valve, spoofed sensor) rather than wear or malfunction.
Material evidence — recovered schematics of the mechanical, electrical, or automation systems, annotated access sequences, or acquired controller credentials tied to the site.

First-hand witness fidelity — a named facilities or security staffer who observed the actor in a systems space or manipulating a controller and can describe what was touched, when, and in what sequence.
Behavioral specificity — the actor targeted a specific system and a specific control point rather than causing generalized damage.
Source motivation aligned with accuracy — reporting through a formal channel by staff with no stake in the outcome, not an informal tip amid a labor or vendor dispute.
low_signal_anchors: Source-quality weakness — a single anonymous report of 'something wrong with the system' that cannot be re-contacted or corroborated.
Fault ambiguity — the outage or anomaly is fully explainable by known equipment age, weather, or a documented maintenance issue.
Temporal-pattern weakness — one isolated reading with no recurrence and no supporting physical or planning evidence.
Source-motivation misalignment — the reporter is in a dispute with a contractor, tenant, or the facility that gives structural reason to allege sabotage.
Unrebutted legitimate explanation — an authorized service call, commissioning test, or scheduled shutdown fits the event and was not excluded.
Reconstructive memory — the report arrives long after the event, with details that may be retrofitted to a sabotage narrative.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when the actor demonstrates literacy in how the targeted system works and how its safeguards are supervised — reaching control points, defeating tamper and supervisory signals, and manipulating a system covertly enough that the failure reads as a fault. Capability falls with crude conspicuous damage, no evident system knowledge, and manipulation that fail-safe design or supervision immediately defeats.
high_signal_anchors: Demonstrated system literacy — the actor reasons correctly about interlocks, control logic, or dependency chains (that disabling suppression precedes a fire, that an air-handling path serves occupied zones, that one disconnect drops egress lighting).
Reach to control points — the actor gets to panels, valves, controllers, intakes, or the automation network, physically or over the OT network, not merely to the building's public spaces.
Supervision defeat — the actor bypasses, spoofs, or silences tamper and supervisory signals so the sabotage does not annunciate.
Insider or privileged access — an employee, contractor, or vendor role gives hands-on or credentialed access to mechanical, electrical, or automation systems.
Covert manipulation tradecraft — the alteration is designed to present as an equipment fault, delaying attribution and response.
Acquisition of system-specific means — obtained controller credentials, keys to plant spaces, or matched tools and fittings for the specific equipment.
low_signal_anchors: Crude conspicuous damage — smashing or cutting in the open with no attempt at concealment or at defeating supervision.
No system knowledge — the actor touches the wrong component, or the attempt reflects no understanding of how the system fails.
Defeated by fail-safe — the manipulation triggered a fail-secure or fail-safe response that contained it, and the actor did not adapt.
No privileged reach — all access is to public areas; the actor never reaches a control point or the OT network.
Single-point crudeness — a one-off tamper with no supervision defeat, immediately annunciated to the central station.
Direct-contact exposure — the actor asked staff how a system works in a way that breached concealment and drew attention.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when the manipulation is aimed at a protective or life-safety function specifically, when it is timed to occupancy, when it is paired with a stated grievance against the place, and when the actor retains system information suggesting planned use. Intent falls when the effect is generic and explainable as opportunistic damage, when timing is indifferent to who is present, and when a benign purpose checks out.
high_signal_anchors: Life-safety targeting — the act disables detection, suppression, egress, or backup power, or weaponizes air or water handling, rather than causing incidental damage.
Occupancy-timed action — the manipulation is set for, or executed during, hours when the facility is occupied, or staged to coincide with a planned attack window.
Function-specific selection — the actor concentrates on the one system whose failure produces harm (suppression before a fire, air handling for dispersal), not on whatever is nearest.
Sequencing with another tactic — systems sabotage is paired with observed incendiary, explosive, or contamination preparation against the same site.
Retention of system materials — saved automation schematics, valve and panel photographs, or controller credentials maintained for later use.

Hostile attribution paired with system access — expressed grievance toward the facility or its function AND observed manipulation of its systems; the combination is intent-diagnostic in a way neither signal is alone.
low_signal_anchors: Generic disruption — the effect is a nuisance outage with no life-safety dimension and no occupancy timing.
Occupancy indifference — the act is as likely to occur when the site is empty, consistent with property grievance rather than harm to persons.
One-time interference without escalation — a single interference surfaced with no pattern, sequencing, or retained material.
Verifiable legitimate purpose — a maintenance, testing, or energy-management action explains the manipulation and checks out.
No retention behavior — system details were viewed in passing but not saved or organized.
System ambiguity — interference spread across unrelated components without narrowing to a function whose failure causes harm.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the actor can reach and hold the targeted system — through unsupervised physical access to plant spaces, an insider or vendor role, knowledge of which safeguards are unmonitored, or an exposed automation network — and act during a consequential window. Opportunity falls with segmented and monitored systems, hardened plant spaces, revoked access, and fail-safe defaults that blunt a single-point manipulation; where opportunity looks reduced, the durability of that reduction matters.
high_signal_anchors: Unsupervised systems access — the actor reaches mechanical, electrical, water, or automation spaces without challenge and can dwell long enough to act.

Insider or vendor role exploited — an identified employee, contractor, or service-vendor relationship is being actively used for hands-on or credentialed system access. Dormant access is potential; the exploitation pattern is high-signal.
Safeguard-gap knowledge — the actor knows which supervisory signals are out of service, which spaces lack monitoring, or which controllers run default credentials.
Exposed automation surface — the building-automation or security network is reachable remotely, flat, or internet-facing, and the actor has demonstrated reach into it.
Occupancy-window mastery — the actor reliably knows when the facility is occupied and when systems are least attended, aligning the act to maximum consequence.
Direct system control — the actor holds legitimate operational control of the targeted system through role or contract.
low_signal_anchors: Segmented, monitored systems — OT is segmented, supervised, and anomaly-alarmed, and the actor's reach was blocked or immediately flagged. Durable unless the actor materially adapts.
Institutional rule-out of insider access — access audits or process actively cleared privileged reach, not merely failed to find it.
Structural access degradation — the actor's prior access pathway terminated (role ended, contract lapsed, credentials revoked).
Hardened plant spaces without adaptation — mechanical, electrical, and intake spaces are locked, alarmed, and access-logged, and the actor left without defeating them.
Fail-safe posture — systems default to fail-secure or fail-safe, so a single manipulation does not cascade; the actor has shown no way around it.
Remote-only reach not converted — the actor probed an exposed controller but never achieved control-changing access; transient unless sustained.

false_positive_context.criteria: Many legitimate activities resemble systems sabotage on the surface — a contractor at an electrical panel looks similar to an actor disabling backup power; an air-handling shutdown for filter service looks similar to defeating ventilation; a silenced alarm during testing looks similar to disabling detection. What distinguishes a false positive is whether the activity has an authorized work order, a transparent identity behind it, and institutional accountability that can be verified, and whether the system's behavior is explained by a known fault or scheduled action.
contexts: Authorized maintenance and service — HVAC, electrical, plumbing, fire-protection, elevator, and controls technicians performing scheduled or work-order service, including alarm impairment permits and system-inspection windows.
Commissioning and testing — building commissioning, fire-alarm and suppression testing, generator load tests, and controls programming that legitimately silence, bypass, or cycle systems.
Equipment fault and environmental cause — genuine component failure, power-utility events, weather, and age-related malfunctions that mimic tampering.
Energy and facilities management — authorized setpoint changes, load-shedding, and after-hours setbacks driven by energy-management programs.
Legal authority — authorized inspectors, utility personnel, and security professionals conducting sanctioned system assessments or penetration tests of the building's operational technology.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: Systems sabotage is an execution-phase act, and any credible indication that a life-safety or protective system has been deliberately disabled or misused warrants immediate response regardless of this tactic's internal tier — the interval between disabling a safeguard and exploiting its absence can be minutes. Findings that reveal a mass-casualty objective — air handling manipulated to move a substance through an occupied building, fire-suppression disabled while the site is occupied or immediately before an incendiary act, or contamination of a domestic water supply — warrant treating occupants as at imminent risk and activating protective evacuation or shelter alongside response protocols. Tier-determination for lower-signal findings depends on three factors: credibility that the failure is deliberate rather than a fault, the criticality of the system touched, and occupancy at the time. A single anomalous reading with an available maintenance explanation sits at the monitoring tier. Confirmed deliberate manipulation of a non-life-safety system at an empty site sits at the investigation tier. Deliberate manipulation of a life-safety system, or any manipulation while the facility is occupied, sits at the elevation tier. Manipulation sequenced with preparation for another attack, or persisting despite countermeasures, sits at the committed-actor tier and should be treated as an attack in progress. Multiple lower-priority indicators correlating temporally or across systems may compose to a higher aggregate tier than any single finding; consumer triage tooling should make this composition rule explicit. Tier-triggered actions: monitoring triggers logging and technician adjudication of the fault; investigation triggers actor-identification and a systems-vulnerability review; elevation triggers system isolation, physical response, and a protective-action decision; the committed-actor tier triggers evacuation or shelter and law-enforcement and HAZMAT coordination as the system implicates.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor deliberately disables or impairs the facility's fire-detection or suppression system — closing and securing a sprinkler control valve, bypassing detection zones, or silencing supervisory alarms — with the site occupied or as an immediate precursor to an incendiary attack

Threat actor manipulates the HVAC or air-handling system of an occupied facility to disperse a hazardous substance through the ventilation network — introducing material at an air intake or return, or overriding controls to drive distribution

Threat actor sabotages the facility's electrical power system — main disconnect, transfer switch, or backup generator — to force a blackout that disables egress lighting, elevators, life-safety, and security systems while the site is occupied

Threat actor defeats the facility's physical-security systems — access control, video surveillance, and alarm monitoring — at the panel or network head-end to blind defenders and suppress annunciation ahead of or during an attack

Threat actor tampers with the facility's water system to contaminate the domestic or potable supply of an occupied building — introducing a hazardous agent through a cross-connection, storage tank, or treatment point that occupants will contact or ingest

countermeasures.measure: Supervise and monitor life-safety systems end to end — tamper-supervised fire detection and suppression reporting to a constantly attended central station, valve tamper switches, and impairment-permit procedures so any disablement annunciates and is adjudicated immediately
countermeasures.limitations: Supervision reports the impairment but does not physically prevent it, and an insider who controls the impairment-permit process or the monitoring path can suppress the very signals meant to catch the act

countermeasures.measure: Segment and monitor the building-automation and operational-technology network — isolate HVAC, energy-management, access-control, and video systems from IT and the internet, remove default and shared credentials, control vendor remote access, and alarm on anomalous control commands
countermeasures.limitations: Segmentation is undermined by legacy controllers that cannot be patched or authenticated, by convenience remote-access links, and by an insider with legitimate OT credentials whose commands look authorized

countermeasures.measure: Physically harden critical systems spaces and intakes — lock, alarm, and access-log mechanical, electrical, water, and controls rooms; elevate or secure outdoor air intakes; and protect water storage and treatment points against unauthorized introduction
countermeasures.limitations: Raises the effort and exposure required to reach a control point but does not stop an insider or vendor with authorized access to these spaces, and cannot be applied uniformly to intakes and infrastructure that must remain functionally accessible

countermeasures.measure: Design for fail-safe and redundancy — fail-secure and fail-safe defaults, backup power and redundant suppression, monitored water-quality and air-quality sensing, and rapid HVAC-shutdown capability so a single-point manipulation neither cascades nor goes unnoticed
countermeasures.limitations: Redundancy and fail-safe design are capital-intensive and constrained by existing building infrastructure; a determined actor with system knowledge may target the redundancy or the sensing itself, and rapid-shutdown capability depends on correct human decision under time pressure

response_protocols.trigger: Indication that a building system has been deliberately manipulated or is behaving anomalously in a way not explained by a known fault or authorized work — a suppression supervisory-trouble signal, an unexplained power loss, an out-of-sequence controller command, or a security-system outage
response_protocols.action: Treat as potential active sabotage. Dispatch to isolate and secure the affected system, have a qualified technician adjudicate fault-versus-tampering, and check for co-located attack precursors (fire load, dispersal source, secondary hazard). Verify occupancy and make a protective-action decision — continue, shelter, or evacuate. Preserve the scene and telemetry, and notify law enforcement if manipulation is confirmed. Document all sourcing.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Manipulation confirmed on a life-safety system, occupancy at risk, or indicators of a sequenced attack against the same site
response_protocols.legal_notes: Preserve controller logs, access records, and the physical scene for potential prosecution; sabotage of life-safety systems implicates specific criminal statutes. Coordinate any OT forensic action with counsel and system owners to avoid destroying evidence or safety functions.

response_protocols.trigger: Air-handling anomaly, contaminant indication, or water-quality alarm in an occupied facility, or observed introduction of material into ventilation or the water system
response_protocols.action: Activate mass-casualty protective action immediately. Shelter or evacuate per plan by affected zone, shut down and isolate the implicated HVAC or water system to halt distribution, and initiate HAZMAT, EMS, and public-health coordination. Establish exposure zones and account for occupants. Treat as an attack in progress and hand incident command to responding authorities.
response_protocols.escalation_trigger: Confirmed contaminant release, occupant symptoms, or spread beyond the initially affected zone
response_protocols.legal_notes: Mass-casualty response and any public notification follow emergency-management and public-health authority; document the decision basis for evacuation or shelter and preserve system state for the subsequent investigation.

tactics.field_notes: The hard problem with systems sabotage is that a competent act is designed to read as a fault. A closed valve, a tripped breaker, a silenced zone, a dropped camera — each has an innocent explanation, and facilities staff are trained to restore service, not to preserve a scene. The tell is usually the pairing: a protective system fails and something else is wrong at the same time, or the failure lands precisely when the building is full. Disabling suppression and blinding the cameras are enabling moves, not ends — they say another act is meant to follow, and the interval can be very short. The weaponizing acts — air handling turned into a dispersal path, the domestic water contaminated — are the ones that move this tactic to a mass-casualty footing, and they are the covert ones, so the first sign may be occupants getting sick rather than a caught intrusion. Insiders and vendors dominate this space because reaching a control point is the whole game, and their commands look authorized. Rule out the fault deliberately and fast; do not let 'probably maintenance' become the default when the building is occupied.
observed_contexts: arson case in which the sprinkler control valve was found closed and secured and a detection zone bypassed shortly before ignition in an occupied building
insider with facilities credentials manipulating air-handling controls to move a substance through occupied floors, first noticed as a cluster of occupant symptoms
activist action against a targeted site that dropped the video head-end and access-control monitoring immediately before a coordinated intrusion

[literature: NIST-SP800-82-2023 / GAO-24-106744-2024 pattern — internet-exposed building-control and operational-technology systems manipulated to disable protective functions or drive equipment to unsafe states]

tactics.name: Forced Entry / Vehicle Ram
tactics.notes: Breaching the facility by physical force at attack time, or using a vehicle as a weapon against the structure, its perimeter barriers, or the people at it. Covers two convergent execution methods: forcing an occupied access point by overpowering doors, glazing, or the guard force, and driving a vehicle into a building entrance, protective barrier line, or crowd. Distinct from Explosive Attack (TF0302, where a vehicle is a delivery platform for a device) and from Occupation & Blockade (TF0306, where access is seized to hold and deny rather than to breach and attack). The defining act here is the application of kinetic force to defeat standoff and access controls — a ram into occupants or a forced entry that overpowers staff applies direct physical force to people and is scored at the casualty floor.
tactics.cpn_notes: Hostile-vehicle and forced-entry methods are actively promoted in extremist media, which circulates target guidance favoring crowded, low-standoff pedestrian venues and instructs on selecting heavy vehicles and high-speed approach vectors. Online mapping and street-view tools let an actor identify unprotected entrances, barrier gaps, and long run-up distances before the day of the attack.

credibility.criteria: At execution altitude, credibility is the confidence that an observed incursion is a deliberate hostile act rather than an accident or an authorized breach. It rises with corroboration across camera and eyewitness sources, with a hostile approach signature (deliberate acceleration, target-tracking steering, absence of braking), and with recoverable evidence that the act was intended. It falls when the observation is single-source and ambiguous, and when a benign explanation — driver medical event, pedal error, authorized emergency forced entry — has not been excluded.
high_signal_anchors: Cross-source corroboration — CCTV and first-hand witnesses independently describe the same deliberate ram or forced breach within the same moment.
Hostile driving signature — deliberate acceleration toward occupants or the entrance, corrective steering to track people or the doorway, and no braking or evasive input before impact.
Target selection under way at the scene — the vehicle or actor bypasses open space to reach a crowd, queue, or controlled entrance rather than striking incidentally.
Recoverable intent evidence — a claim, note, livestream, or prior threat recovered that ties the act to the actor's stated purpose against the site.
Method-consistent staging — a heavy or rented vehicle, defeated or rammed barriers, and pre-positioned breaching tools consistent with a planned forcible entry rather than an accident.
Repetition or persistence — a second approach after a first was blocked, or continued forcing after an initial barrier held, indicating a committed act.
low_signal_anchors: Single ambiguous source — one distant camera or one shaken witness, with the deliberate-versus-accidental question unresolved.
Benign driving explanation unexcluded — signs of medical emergency, intoxication, or pedal error that investigation has not ruled out.
Authorized-breach confusion — fire, EMS, or law-enforcement forcing a door under legitimate authority mistaken for a hostile entry.
Incidental contact — a low-speed strike consistent with a parking or maneuvering error, with no target-tracking behavior.
Reconstructive reporting — an account assembled after the fact whose 'deliberate' framing may be retrofitted to the outcome.
Reporter motivation misaligned — the source has a dispute with the driver or facility that could color the deliberate-act claim.

capability.criteria: Capability rises when the actor commands the means to defeat the facility's standoff and access controls — a vehicle heavy and fast enough to overrun the barrier line, breaching tools matched to the doors and glazing in place, and the physical ability to overpower a guard force. It falls when the means are mismatched to the protection — an underpowered vehicle against rated bollards, hand force against a hardened mantrap — and when the attempt fails at first contact with the barrier or the responder.
high_signal_anchors: Barrier-defeating vehicle — a vehicle of sufficient mass and speed, on a run-up long enough to overrun the facility's rated or unrated barrier line.
Breaching means matched to the target — pry bars, cutting tools, a hydraulic ram, or a battering implement selected for the specific doors, locks, or glazing in place.
Force sufficient to overpower staff — numbers, weapons, or physical dominance adequate to defeat the guard force or reception controls at the entry point.
Standoff-gap exploitation — the actor's approach uses a known barrier gap, an unprotected pedestrian entrance, or an unhardened glazed frontage.
Coordinated breach — a ram or forced entry paired with a second element (dismounted attackers, a follow-on device, or diversion) indicating rehearsed capability.
Speed and commitment through the barrier — the actor maintains momentum through an initial obstacle rather than stalling, showing the method was sized to the defense.
low_signal_anchors: Underpowered method — a light vehicle or hand force insufficient against the installed rated barriers or hardened entry.
Barrier defeat at first contact — the vehicle is arrested by bollards or a wedge, or the forced entry stalls at a mantrap or reinforced door.
Tool mismatch — breaching implements inadequate to the doors, locks, or glazing actually in place.
Guard-force interdiction — reception or security personnel halt the entry without being overpowered.
Solo, improvised attempt — no follow-on element, no rehearsal signature, method assembled on the spot.
Abandonment under friction — the actor breaks off when the first obstacle holds and does not adapt the method.

intent.criteria: Intent rises when the force is directed at people or at the occupied core of the site rather than at property or an empty barrier, when the actor presses the attack past the first line of defense, and when the act pairs with stated grievance or claim against the place. It falls when the contact is incidental, when the actor withdraws once inside without pursuing harm, and when a verifiable non-hostile purpose for the entry surfaces.
high_signal_anchors: Force directed at occupants — the vehicle is steered into a crowd or queue, or the forced entry drives toward occupied space rather than an empty perimeter.
Attack pressed past the first barrier — the actor continues after defeating or being slowed by the initial obstacle, targeting the occupied interior.
Grievance or claim attached to the act — a statement, banner, livestream, or prior threat framing the ram or breach as purposeful against the site or what it represents.
Occupied-hours timing — the act is executed when the site is populated, maximizing exposure rather than avoiding it.
Ram-then-dismount or breach-then-advance — the vehicle is abandoned to continue on foot, or the breach opens the way for a follow-on attack, signaling harm as the objective.
Barrier line chosen for the people behind it — the point of impact is the pedestrian frontage or entrance, not a service gate or unoccupied wall.
low_signal_anchors: Incidental contact — a strike consistent with loss of control, with no steering toward people or the occupied core.
Withdrawal after entry — the actor breaches but leaves without pursuing occupants or damage.
Property-only trajectory — force directed at an empty barrier, sign, or unoccupied structure with no path toward people.
Verifiable non-hostile purpose — an authorized breach, a delivery or access dispute, or an emergency that accounts for the forced entry.
Off-hours timing — the act occurs when the site is unoccupied, reducing the population-target reading.
No follow-through — the actor neither advances nor communicates a purpose after the initial force.

opportunity.criteria: Opportunity rises when the site's physical protection admits the method — unprotected pedestrian frontage, a long unobstructed run-up, unrated or absent barriers, thin entry controls, and timing that puts the actor at the occupied core with little friction. It falls when rated barriers, geometric approach control, hardened entries, and an alert guard force block the actor's chosen method; where a reduction in opportunity is observed, its durability depends on whether the barrier is a fixed engineered control or a transient posture that can lapse.
high_signal_anchors: Unprotected occupied frontage — a pedestrian entrance, plaza, or queue directly exposed to a vehicle approach with no rated barrier between.
Long unobstructed run-up — an approach geometry that lets a vehicle reach ramming speed before the barrier line or entrance.
Thin or absent entry control — a single unhardened door, unmonitored reception, or defeated access control at the point of forced entry.
Occupied-window timing exploited — the act is staged during peak occupancy with minimal security presence to interdict it.
Insider-assisted access — a propped door, disabled lock, shared credential, or tolerated bypass that eases the breach.
No interdiction en route — the actor reaches the barrier or entrance without being challenged, ANPR-flagged, or physically slowed.
low_signal_anchors: Rated barriers enforce standoff — crash-rated bollards, wedges, or planters arrest the vehicle before the occupied line. Durable engineered control unless removed.
Geometric approach control — chicanes, curbing, or angled approaches deny the run-up needed to reach ramming speed.
Hardened entry defeats forced breach — reinforced doors, anti-breach glazing, or a mantrap holds against hand force. Durable unless the fixture degrades.
Alert guard-force interdiction — reception or security halts the approach or entry; transient, dependent on staffing and vigilance.
Access audit closes insider paths — credential and door-status controls actively verified, not merely presumed intact.
Elevated transient posture — barriers raised, patrols emphasized, and access tightened for an exposure window; reverts when the window closes unless sustained.

false_positive_context.criteria: Several legitimate events resemble a forced entry or vehicle ram at first observation — an accidental vehicle incursion looks like a deliberate ram until the driving signature is read, and an authorized emergency breach looks like a hostile forced entry until the actor's authority is confirmed. What distinguishes a false positive is a verifiable benign cause for the incursion, a transparent and accountable identity behind the forced entry, or a driving pattern consistent with error rather than intent.
contexts: Accidental vehicle incursion — driver medical emergency, pedal misapplication, intoxication, or loss of control, with no steering toward people and evidence of attempted braking.
Authorized emergency forced entry — fire, EMS, or law enforcement forcing a door under legitimate authority to reach an occupant or hazard.
Legitimate access recovery — locksmiths, building maintenance, or a lockout situation where an authorized party forces or defeats a lock with permission.
Delivery and service maneuvering — heavy vehicles maneuvering at loading zones or barriers, with low-speed contact consistent with a maneuvering error.
Authorized security testing — sanctioned breach drills, barrier crash-testing, or vulnerability assessments conducted with facility knowledge and consent.

assessment_guidance.threshold_guidance: At execution altitude the presumption inverts from the pre-attack phases: a confirmed deliberate ram or forced breach is a life-safety emergency and triggers immediate response protocols regardless of any internal tier. Tier-determination applies only while the deliberate-versus-benign question is genuinely open. A low-speed contact or a forced door with a plausible benign cause and no target-tracking behavior sits at the assessment tier pending confirmation. A hostile approach vector — deliberate acceleration toward an occupied frontage, a heavy vehicle staged for a run-up, or breaching tools deployed against a controlled entry during occupied hours — sits at the interdiction tier and warrants active barrier deployment, denial of access, and law-enforcement notification before impact. Any impact into occupants, or a forced entry that overpowers staff, is the attack itself: activate lockdown, life-safety, and mass-casualty response, and treat a ram-then-dismount or breach-then-advance as an ongoing complex attack until cleared. Multiple lower-signal precursors correlating in time — a flagged approach plus a defeated barrier plus tools in view — compose to the interdiction tier even when no single observation confirms the act; consumer triage tooling should make this composition explicit so the response is not delayed to certainty.

indicators.behavior: Threat actor drives a vehicle into an occupied building entrance, pedestrian frontage, queue, or crowd at the site, applying direct physical force to the people present
Threat actor's vehicle accelerates on a hostile approach vector toward the facility, or a heavy vehicle is positioned for a ramming run-up at a perimeter or entrance, immediately before impact
Threat actor forces an occupied access point by overpowering the guard force, reception, or staff to breach a controlled entry during operating hours
Threat actor employs breaching tools — pry bars, bolt cutters, a hydraulic or battering ram, or cutting equipment — against doors, glazing, or barriers to force entry
Threat actor rams a vehicle into the facility's perimeter barriers, gate, or bollard line to defeat standoff and open an access path

countermeasures.measure: Install crash-rated vehicle barriers — bollards, wedges, planters, or active gates meeting ASTM F2656 impact ratings — across pedestrian frontages and vehicle approaches to enforce standoff and arrest a ramming vehicle before the occupied line
countermeasures.limitations: Effective only where the rating matches the credible vehicle mass and speed; gaps at service entrances, temporary events, or unrated frontages leave exploitable approaches, and retrofits are costly and slow

countermeasures.measure: Apply geometric approach control — chicanes, curbing, landscaping, and angled or lengthened approaches — to deny the straight run-up a vehicle needs to reach ramming speed at the barrier or entrance
countermeasures.limitations: Constrained by existing site geometry, emergency-access and delivery needs, and local right-of-way; reduces attainable speed rather than eliminating vehicle access entirely

countermeasures.measure: Harden entry control points — reinforced doors and frames, anti-breach glazing, mantraps or interlocked portals, duress alarms, and a trained guard-force response protocol for attempted forced entry
